themes.name: Do tax-based subsidies deliver social benefits to lower- and middle-income households more effectively and fairly than direct spending programs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether using the tax system to administer social benefits produces appropriate eligibility, take-up, distributional outcomes, and administrative costs compared with alternative government programs.

themes.name: Do tax preferences produce their intended behavioral effects strongly enough to justify their revenue and distributional costs?
themes.definition: This question examines whether targeted deductions, credits, exclusions, or other incentives actually change saving, investment, household, or social behavior in the intended direction.

themes.name: Should tax-favored activities be subsidized through the tax code or supported through direct spending and neutral taxation instead?
themes.definition: This question compares tax incentives with non-tax policy instruments while considering effectiveness, transparency, administrative feasibility, and unintended economic distortions.

themes.name: Can progressive income taxation reduce inequality without creating unacceptable efficiency, liberty, or compliance costs?
themes.definition: This question assesses how graduated rates and redistribution affect economic inequality, taxpayer behavior, resource allocation, and the perceived legitimacy of taxation.

themes.name: Do formally neutral tax rules impose substantively unequal burdens on taxpayers with different economic circumstances?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether uniform classifications or administratively convenient rules produce discriminatory or regressive outcomes for vulnerable groups, households, or taxpayers with unequal resources.

themes.name: Should tax liability be based on comprehensive economic ability to pay rather than on realized or conventionally defined income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether statutory income measures accurately capture taxpayers’ available economic resources, including noncash benefits, wealth changes, and other forms of economic gain.

themes.name: Should realization-based taxation of appreciated assets be redesigned to reduce lock-in and improve the measurement of capital income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether taxing gains only upon sale distorts asset dispositions, permits indefinite deferral, or inadequately reflects economic income.

themes.name: Are exclusions, deferrals, and favorable treatments for unconventional receipts consistent with a principled definition of gross income?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether payments, benefits, property transfers, and other nonstandard receipts should be included in taxable income under general income-tax principles.

themes.name: Do tax rules measure income accurately when deductions, basis, valuation, and timing determine the amount of taxable gain?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether accounting and allocation rules correctly distinguish economic gain from capital recovery, expenses, and merely nominal increases in value.

themes.name: Should capital income receive preferential tax treatment relative to labor income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the equity, incentive, and economic consequences of different tax rates or bases for capital gains, investment returns, and compensation.

themes.name: How should the tax system balance family-based taxation with equal treatment of different household and intimate-relationship arrangements?
themes.definition: This question examines whether spouses, partners, dependents, household labor, and transfers within families should be treated as a single economic unit or as separate taxpayers.

themes.name: Should estate and gift taxes limit the intergenerational concentration of wealth and economic power?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the fairness, incentive effects, and administrability of taxing inheritances, lifetime gifts, and other transfers of family wealth.

themes.name: Do the estate and gift taxes operate as a coherent system for taxing lifetime and death-time transfers?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether the relationship between gift-tax and estate-tax rules creates consistent treatment or opportunities for avoidance, estate freezing, and strategic transfer planning.

themes.name: Can tax-favored retirement savings increase retirement security without disproportionately benefiting high-income taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question assesses the effectiveness, distributional incidence, and administrative complexity of employer and individual retirement-savings preferences.

themes.name: Can individual tax rules be simplified enough for ordinary taxpayers to determine their liabilities without expert assistance?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether reducing detailed classifications, exceptions, and transaction-specific rules would improve understandability and compliance without undermining policy objectives.

themes.name: Does tax-law complexity obscure distributional effects and create costs that outweigh the benefits of targeted rules?
themes.definition: This question examines how intricate legislation, layered administrative guidance, and differentiated eligibility rules affect transparency, uncertainty, compliance, and substantive fairness.

themes.name: How should courts and administrators reconcile statutory text, precedent, economic substance, and conflicting policy objectives in interpreting the tax code?
themes.definition: This question concerns the appropriate role of judicial doctrine and administrative practice when formal statutory classifications conflict with transaction purpose, economic reality, or broader statutory policies.

themes.name: When should tax law distinguish legitimate planning from abusive avoidance or manipulation of formal classifications?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the limits of attribution, realization, substance-over-form, and related doctrines used to prevent taxpayers from exploiting legal distinctions without invalidating intended tax benefits.

themes.name: Do transaction-specific exclusions, deferrals, and reorganizations preserve legitimate economic activity or create unjustified distortions?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether special rules for exchanges, restructurings, financing, and property transactions are properly matched to their policy purposes and fairly applied.

themes.name: Is incremental reform of the existing federal tax system preferable to fundamental replacement?
themes.definition: This question compares the political feasibility, transition costs, revenue effects, distributional consequences, and structural benefits of modifying existing rules versus adopting a fundamentally different tax base or system.

themes.name: Should taxable income be measured by genuine increases in wealth rather than by formal receipts or realization events?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the income-tax base should include economic accretions to wealth even when property has not been sold, received in cash, or otherwise formally realized.

themes.name: Does the realization principle produce unjustified deferral and unequal treatment of economically similar taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how realization and timing rules allow taxpayers to postpone, reduce, or strategically structure tax liabilities and whether those effects are normatively defensible.

themes.name: Should capital gains and other capital income be taxed more effectively to prevent wealth accumulation from escaping taxation?
themes.definition: This question concerns alternative treatments of capital and investment income, including unrealized gains, deferral, and the distributional consequences of taxing capital more comprehensively.

themes.name: Would replacing or supplementing the federal income tax with a consumption-based tax improve simplicity without worsening inequality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether consumption taxation can simplify administration and promote efficiency while accounting for its effects on progressivity, savings, investment, and different income groups.

themes.name: Should tax burdens be allocated primarily according to ability to pay rather than according to equal rates or formal equality?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether progressive taxation and differentiated burdens better satisfy fairness and distributive-justice principles than flat or formally uniform taxation.

themes.name: Do tax preferences disproportionately benefit high-income and high-wealth taxpayers relative to their stated social objectives?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deductions, exclusions, credits, and other preferences deliver excessive benefits to affluent taxpayers instead of their intended lower- or middle-income beneficiaries.

themes.name: Do tax expenditures achieve their intended policy goals after accounting for fiscal costs, behavioral responses, and unintended beneficiaries?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax-favored provisions produce genuine social or economic benefits rather than functioning mainly as poorly targeted subsidies or revenue losses.

themes.name: Should tax preferences be reformed when their formal legal rationale diverges from their actual distributional and economic effects?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether longstanding or narrowly justified exclusions, deductions, and credits should be narrowed or redesigned when they operate as broader wealth transfers or avoidance mechanisms.

themes.name: Can tax reform close avoidance opportunities while preserving flexibility for legitimate economic arrangements?
themes.definition: This question explores how anti-avoidance rules should balance preventing exploitation of preferences and timing rules against administrability and taxpayers’ ability to structure lawful transactions.

themes.name: Should economically equivalent transactions receive equivalent tax treatment despite differences in legal form?
themes.definition: This question asks whether tax law should classify payments, transactions, and property according to economic substance rather than formal labels, contractual categories, or specialized legal rules.

themes.name: Do formal tax classifications create unjustified unequal treatment of taxpayers with similar economic circumstances?
themes.definition: This question examines whether statutory distinctions involving inclusion, exclusion, deduction, compensation, or taxpayer status produce inequitable outcomes among economically comparable taxpayers.

themes.name: How should tax law allocate income and deductions when legal rights, contractual arrangements, or economic control are divided among multiple parties?
themes.definition: This question concerns the rules for assigning income, compensation, losses, and tax benefits to the appropriate taxpayer when formal ownership or payment differs from substantive economic responsibility.

themes.name: Should the tax system deliver social welfare benefits directly, or are tax incentives an inadequate substitute for explicit transfers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether income-tax credits, deductions, and exclusions are effective and equitable mechanisms for providing income support compared with non-tax benefit programs.

themes.name: Does the tax-and-transfer system adequately support low-income households without undermining work incentives?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tradeoff between redistribution and labor-market participation in tax-funded benefits, income-support programs, and other forms of social assistance.

themes.name: Should family-related tax rules recognize spouses’ and dependents’ separate economic interests rather than treat the household as a unified economic unit?
themes.definition: This question examines the fairness and incentive effects of joint taxation, family allowances, dependent benefits, and alternative taxable-unit designs.

themes.name: Do tax rules governing marriage and household expenditures distribute burdens and benefits fairly across different family structures?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether married couples, unmarried households, parents, dependents, and other household types receive equitable tax treatment when financing shared economic needs.

themes.name: Can estate and inheritance taxation reduce intergenerational wealth concentration without imposing unjustified burdens on family security?
themes.definition: This question concerns the distributive and normative tradeoffs involved in taxing transfers of wealth while protecting beneficiaries, family interests, and privately accumulated security.

themes.name: Do tax rules distort saving, investment, labor, organizational, or occupational decisions enough to justify reform?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether tax-induced behavioral changes produce economically significant resource-allocation effects and whether those distortions outweigh possible equity or policy benefits.

themes.name: Do tax rates and enforcement rules for high-income taxpayers increase revenue without substantially reducing productive economic activity?
themes.definition: This question examines the revenue, compliance, avoidance, and economic-performance effects of targeting high-income individuals and economically powerful participants.

themes.name: Can the IRS and courts administer complex tax rules consistently enough to preserve both fairness and legal certainty?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether judicial interpretation, IRS enforcement, statutory clarity, and administrative capacity can resolve ambiguity without sacrificing equitable treatment or practical feasibility.

themes.name: Should federal income taxation include economically valuable noncash gains, windfalls, and unrealized appreciation?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the legal tax base should include benefits such as found property, noncash compensation, wealth increases, and other economically valuable receipts that are not ordinary cash wages.

themes.name: Should taxable income be measured according to economic substance rather than formal legal classification?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether inclusion, exclusion, deduction, and recipient rules should follow the underlying economic benefit or instead respect statutory and contractual categories.

themes.name: When should business expenses and liabilities be deducted immediately rather than capitalized or deferred?
themes.definition: This question concerns how deduction and capitalization rules should allocate business costs and losses over time while preventing distortions in investment and reporting.

themes.name: Do related-party, family, and trust transactions require stronger attribution rules to prevent tax avoidance?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether existing rules adequately address transactions in which ownership, control, or income is shifted among related parties without a corresponding change in economic substance.

themes.name: Should the federal estate and gift tax system be restructured to limit inherited wealth and concentrated economic power?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the design, justification, and distributional effects of taxing bequests, gifts, and transfers of closely held or substantial property.

themes.name: Can wealth or unrealized appreciation be taxed constitutionally and administratively without excessive economic costs?
themes.definition: This question examines the legal authority, valuation problems, and efficiency tradeoffs involved in taxing accumulated wealth or appreciation before realization.

themes.name: Do progressive rates, refundable credits, and targeted transfers reduce inequality more effectively than broad tax-rate reductions?
themes.definition: This question compares targeted redistribution with general rate changes in terms of progressivity, poverty reduction, incentives, and the distribution of tax burdens.

themes.name: Should family and child-related tax benefits be redesigned to reflect ability to pay without privileging particular household forms?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether tax provisions for children, dependents, marriage, and family support fairly treat traditional, nontraditional, and economically vulnerable households.

themes.name: Is the joint taxation of married couples consistent with equity and marriage neutrality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether treating marriage as an economic unit creates marriage penalties, bonuses, or unequal treatment relative to unmarried taxpayers.

themes.name: Do tax and social-insurance rules fairly recognize non-wage, unpaid, and gendered forms of economic contribution?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether tax and benefit systems inadequately protect women, caregivers, nontraditional workers, and people whose economic contributions fall outside conventional wage income.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for retirement saving and employer benefits adequately serve workers who lack conventional plans?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether retirement-savings subsidies, fringe-benefit rules, and employer-plan regulations distribute support fairly across workers with different access to benefits.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for investments and passive activities create unjustified subsidies and inefficient allocation of capital?
themes.definition: This question examines whether preferential treatment of investment returns, passive losses, and selected investment forms distorts economic decisions or disproportionately benefits higher-income taxpayers.

themes.name: Should the United States shift from an income-tax base toward a consumption-tax base?
themes.definition: This question compares income and consumption taxation with respect to saving incentives, progressivity, administrative simplicity, and the treatment of capital and wealth.

themes.name: Are tax incentives an effective and appropriate means of achieving social-policy goals beyond revenue collection?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether deductions, exclusions, credits, and preferential rates are better suited than direct spending or regulation to promote family support, saving, work, or other social objectives.

themes.name: Do tax deductions and exclusions achieve their intended behavioral or distributive purposes efficiently?
themes.definition: This question asks whether particular tax benefits produce the desired conduct or assistance and whether their benefits justify their fiscal cost, complexity, and unequal distribution.

themes.name: Does tax-system complexity undermine compliance, administrability, and substantively fair outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether detailed statutory rules, regulations, reporting requirements, and specialized classifications create uncertainty and burdens that outweigh gains in precision.

themes.name: Should tax rules prioritize administrability and practical effectiveness over theoretically precise measurement of income?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tradeoff between accurately capturing economic value and adopting rules that taxpayers, administrators, and courts can apply consistently.

themes.name: Do gaps between tax statutes and other legal regimes enable taxpayers to obtain unintended advantages?
themes.definition: This question investigates how conflicts among the Internal Revenue Code, property and contract law, ERISA, and other legal systems produce unanticipated federal tax consequences.

themes.name: Should legal-claim-related payments be taxed according to the nature of the underlying injury or obligation?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether payments connected to lawsuits and legal claims should be included or excluded based on their economic source rather than their formal characterization.

themes.name: Can incremental amendments produce coherent tax reform, or are structural changes to the income-tax system necessary?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether piecemeal statutory fixes can preserve policy coherence and legitimacy or whether fundamental redesign is required to correct entrenched inequities, avoidance, and inefficiencies.

themes.name: Do realization requirements and tax deferral make the taxation of capital gains inequitable?
themes.definition: This question examines whether allowing taxpayers to postpone recognition of economically accrued gains undermines fairness, revenue collection, or the integrity of the income-tax base.

themes.name: Do deductions and credits distribute tax subsidies equitably across income groups?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the structure, eligibility rules, and limitations of deductions and credits provide comparable benefits to taxpayers at different income levels.

themes.name: Should targeted tax preferences be retained, redesigned, or replaced by a neutral tax base?
themes.definition: This question asks whether special exclusions, deductions, credits, or preferential rates can be justified despite their departure from broadly applicable and tax-neutral rules.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation improve distributional fairness without imposing unacceptable efficiency or behavioral costs?
themes.definition: This question studies how tax-rate progressivity affects revenue, inequality, taxpayer incentives, and economic efficiency.

themes.name: Should capital be taxed through a comprehensive income tax, a consumption tax, or a hybrid system?
themes.definition: This question compares income- and consumption-based approaches to determining the tax base, particularly their consequences for saving, investment, fairness, and capital taxation.

themes.name: Should marriage determine the federal tax unit and the allocation of tax burdens between spouses?
themes.definition: This question examines whether married couples should be taxed as a single economic unit and whether marriage-based rules create unjustified advantages or penalties relative to unmarried households.

themes.name: Do estate, gift, and intrafamily-transfer tax rules adequately limit inequitable intergenerational wealth transmission?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether existing rules governing transfers to children, descendants, spouses, and family wealth vehicles fairly tax inherited economic advantages.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow the economic substance of a transaction rather than its formal legal structure?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether classification, basis, timing, and other tax outcomes should reflect genuine economic interests instead of nominal rights or transaction form.

themes.name: Are the federal tax rules for personal-injury damages, settlements, and casualty losses economically and normatively justified?
themes.definition: This question examines whether exclusions, deductions, and basis rules properly distinguish compensation for personal harm or property loss from taxable economic gain.

themes.name: Are anti-avoidance rules effective without creating excessive uncertainty or administrative burden?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether doctrines and statutory mechanisms that curb abusive tax planning protect the tax base while preserving predictable and administrable treatment.

themes.name: Does tax-law complexity undermine taxpayer compliance, understanding, and access to legally available benefits?
themes.definition: This question studies whether complicated, opaque, or rigid income-tax and benefit rules impose disproportionate compliance costs or discourage accurate participation.

themes.name: Should tax authorities resolve statutory ambiguity through purposive interpretation rather than isolated textual or formal rules?
themes.definition: This question examines how courts and administrators should interpret overlapping, conflicting, or underdeveloped tax provisions when literal application defeats coherent policy objectives.

themes.name: Should tax-based social benefits be targeted to economically vulnerable households rather than made broadly available?
themes.definition: This question compares targeted and universal eligibility rules for tax credits, deductions, and related benefits in terms of equity, access, administrative feasibility, and fiscal cost.

themes.name: Can tax and transfer programs address poverty effectively without sacrificing fairness, flexibility, or administrative simplicity?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether using the tax system to deliver income support produces better distributive and behavioral outcomes than direct assistance or alternative institutional arrangements.

themes.name: Should childcare and other socially important services receive tax subsidies or direct public provision?
themes.definition: This question asks whether tax incentives and privately provided alternatives can fairly and effectively address socially significant care and service needs.

themes.name: Can wealth taxation raise substantial revenue while remaining administrable and fair across different forms of wealth?
themes.definition: This question examines the tradeoff among revenue, valuation feasibility, avoidance opportunities, and distributional fairness in taxing accumulated wealth and property.

themes.name: Do tax incentives for saving and investment produce benefits that justify their economic and distributional costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential treatment of investment, savings, or socially favored activities changes behavior enough to warrant the resulting revenue loss and unequal benefits.

themes.name: Do formally neutral tax rules create horizontal inequity among taxpayers with similar economic income?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether differences in income source, asset ownership, family status, or transaction form cause economically similar taxpayers to bear unequal tax burdens.

themes.name: Do tax preferences and exemptions disproportionately benefit wealthy taxpayers and concentrate economic advantage?
themes.definition: This question measures whether exclusions, deduction limits, capital preferences, and other subsidies distribute benefits toward affluent households in ways that increase inequality.

themes.name: Do fiscal and social-welfare tax policies impose unequal burdens on historically disadvantaged racial or social groups?
themes.definition: This question examines the distributional effects of tax rules and tax-based benefits across racial, socioeconomic, and otherwise disadvantaged populations, including consequences hidden by formally universal rules.

themes.name: Should progressive taxation distribute burdens according to taxpayers’ ability to pay without imposing unacceptable efficiency costs?
themes.definition: This question examines how progressive rates and tax-base choices should balance distributive fairness, revenue needs, neutrality, and economic efficiency.

themes.name: Do formal tax classifications produce inequitable results when economically similar taxpayers or transactions receive different treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax law should prioritize economic substance and comparable economic circumstances over statutory labels, categorical rules, or formal equality.

themes.name: Should accrued but unrealized capital gains be taxed rather than escaping taxation through the realization requirement?
themes.definition: This question considers whether taxing appreciation only upon realization systematically advantages asset owners and mismeasures economic income.

themes.name: Do tax-timing, annual-accounting, and realization rules create unjustified advantages or distortions?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether deferral, deductions, recoveries, and the timing of recognition accurately reflect economic gain and loss while treating taxpayers fairly.

themes.name: Should tax treatment distinguish among different uses and forms of accumulated wealth?
themes.definition: This question examines whether savings, investment returns, retirement assets, inherited property, and other forms of wealth warrant distinct tax treatment.

themes.name: Does the tax treatment of saving and capital income promote national saving and investment or instead distort economic behavior?
themes.definition: This question assesses how preferential rates, deferral, deductions, and subsidies for capital affect saving, investment, capital formation, and distribution.

themes.name: Should lifetime transfers and death-time transfers receive different treatment under the gift and estate tax systems?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the transfer-tax distinction between gifts, inheritances, and wealth transferred at death is economically and normatively justified.

themes.name: Do existing gift and estate tax rules allow wealthy taxpayers to shift wealth through planning structures that undermine transfer-tax policy?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether trusts, fragmented interests, estate-planning documents, and other arrangements create unjustified opportunities to minimize transfer taxes.

themes.name: Should the marital deduction and other spouse-based tax rules be retained, redesigned, or eliminated?
themes.definition: This question examines whether federal taxation of spouses, marital property, and family units fairly reflects economic relationships and distributes benefits across household types.

themes.name: Do federal tax rules adequately accommodate legally and socially diverse family or multi-person economic arrangements?
themes.definition: This question asks whether rules based on conventional marital, entity, or household categories misallocate tax consequences among nonstandard families and shared economic units.

themes.name: Do child, dependent-care, and family tax benefits achieve their intended equity and social-policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether family-oriented credits, deductions, and subsidies effectively support care responsibilities and disadvantaged households.

themes.name: Can tax-based assistance reduce poverty and economic insecurity without producing counterproductive incentives or administrative burdens?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether targeted credits and related public benefits improve material security while avoiding poverty traps, exclusion errors, and dependence on complex programs.

themes.name: Do tax preferences and exclusions advance legitimate social objectives or primarily create regressive loopholes?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether carve-outs, subsidies, deductions, and exemptions are justified by their distributional and policy effects rather than by formal legislative categories.

themes.name: Do tax incentives effectively influence private behavior, or do their distortions and unintended consequences outweigh their benefits?
themes.definition: This question examines how tax provisions affect saving, investment, employment, reporting, compliance, and other decisions relative to their intended policy goals.

themes.name: Do assignment-of-income rules allocate compensation and receipts fairly among taxpayers and legally related parties?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether taxpayers can redirect income through fee arrangements, intermediaries, family transfers, or other structures without violating the underlying allocation principle.

themes.name: Can sophisticated taxpayers exploit statutory and procedural asymmetries in ways that undermine legislative tax policy?
themes.definition: This question concerns the effectiveness, fairness, and administrability of anti-avoidance rules governing legal tax planning, intermediaries, exclusions, and favorable classifications.

themes.name: Does tax-law complexity prevent taxpayers from obtaining benefits that legislation intended to provide?
themes.definition: This question examines whether technical rules, overlapping programs, uncertain doctrines, and compliance costs create unjustified barriers or contradictory outcomes.

themes.name: Would replacing specialized and overlapping tax provisions with simpler rules improve equity and administration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether simplification and structural reform can reduce complexity without creating new compliance costs, distributional harms, or unintended incentives.

themes.name: How should tax reform reconcile technically desirable changes with political feasibility and institutional constraints?
themes.definition: This question analyzes how ideology, partisan conflict, public legitimation, interest groups, and incremental legislative strategies shape the adoption and durability of tax reforms.

themes.name: Can tax administration and enforcement secure accurate revenue collection without sacrificing fairness and equal treatment?
themes.definition: This question examines the trade-off between enforceability, procedural rules, anti-abuse measures, liability determination, taxpayer compliance, and substantive tax justice.

themes.name: Should taxable income be defined according to economic accrual rather than realization upon sale or disposition?
themes.definition: This question examines whether unrealized appreciation and other nontraditional gains should be taxed when they accrue economically or only when a realization event occurs.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow the economic substance of a transaction rather than its formal legal classification?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether economically equivalent payments, ownership arrangements, and transactions should receive equivalent tax treatment despite differing legal or accounting labels.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation achieve greater distributive justice than flat, lump-sum, or consumption taxation without imposing excessive efficiency costs?
themes.definition: This question compares alternative rate structures and tax bases in terms of equity, behavioral distortions, revenue, and administrative practicality.

themes.name: Should wealth be taxed through estate and gift transfers, periodic accretion, or another form of wealth taxation?
themes.definition: This question assesses which timing and institutional mechanism can most effectively tax concentrated wealth while preserving administrability and limiting avoidance.

themes.name: Do estate and gift tax exemptions, deductions, and progressive rates undermine the redistributive purposes of transfer taxation?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether preferential treatment of marital, family, or other transfers produces unjustified reductions in wealth-transfer tax burdens.

themes.name: Do tax-favored retirement and savings arrangements promote socially valuable saving enough to justify their unequal distributional effects?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether retirement accounts, employee benefits, and other savings preferences increase saving or mainly subsidize higher-income taxpayers.

themes.name: Should deductions and exclusions be redesigned to reconcile ability-to-pay principles with economic incentives?
themes.definition: This question examines how deductions and exclusions alter the taxable base, effective burdens, and incentives while pursuing competing social and economic objectives.

themes.name: Does tax treatment of childcare and family obligations unfairly penalize parents or secondary earners who participate in the labor market?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether family-based tax rules accurately reflect reduced ability to pay and avoid discouraging work by caregivers.

themes.name: Do tax preferences and subsidies for socially valuable activities deliver benefits equitably, or do they primarily reward wealthy taxpayers and favored organizations?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the justification and distributional effects of tax expenditures supporting charitable, nonprofit, or other publicly valued activities.

themes.name: Do tax rules and professional planning enable sophisticated taxpayers to exploit formal gaps in ways that defeat legislative policy goals?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether avoidance strategies, ownership structures, and complex transactions capture benefits unavailable to less resourceful taxpayers.

themes.name: Are assignment-of-income and related-party attribution rules adequate to prevent income shifting without imposing unjustified burdens on economically distinct taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question examines when one person's tax conduct or income should be attributed to another person, particularly within families and controlled arrangements.

themes.name: Do tax incentives for corporate investment increase productive investment enough to justify their fiscal cost and distortions?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether subsidies, credits, and preferential treatment for plant, infrastructure, and business investment change real investment rather than merely alter its tax form.

themes.name: Are taxpayer behavioral responses to after-tax returns too complex for conventional incentive-based tax policy models?
themes.definition: This question tests whether changes in saving, investment, labor supply, and market participation respond in predictable ways to tax incentives.

themes.name: Do tax-and-transfer programs reduce poverty effectively, or can their eligibility rules and benefit structures deepen economic insecurity?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether anti-poverty benefits are administratively accessible and equitable across disadvantaged groups or create harmful cliffs and disincentives.

themes.name: Do formal tax categories produce unjustified unequal treatment of taxpayers in economically comparable circumstances?
themes.definition: This question examines horizontal and substantive equity when legal distinctions among income, payments, relationships, or transactions do not correspond to meaningful economic differences.

themes.name: Should tax policy prioritize distributive fairness over efficiency, or can reforms achieve both objectives?
themes.definition: This question analyzes conflicts between equitable allocation of tax burdens and the effects of tax design on resource allocation, investment, saving, and work.

themes.name: Can a simplified or standardized tax system preserve accurate measurement of economic circumstances without sacrificing fairness?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether simplification, flat rules, and standardized benefits can reduce complexity while still accounting for differences in income, family obligations, and economic capacity.

themes.name: Should entrenched tax regimes be incrementally amended or replaced with a more coherent structural framework?
themes.definition: This question compares piecemeal reform with comprehensive redesign in addressing complexity, uncertainty, historical accretion, and inconsistent treatment.

themes.name: Which institution should correct defective tax rules: Congress, tax administrators, or the courts?
themes.definition: This question examines the appropriate allocation of authority for interpreting, revising, and enforcing tax rules when statutory provisions produce inequitable or economically irrational outcomes.

themes.name: Does the federal income tax possess sufficient legal, political, and normative legitimacy to serve as an instrument of social reform?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the institutional foundations of federal taxation and whether using the tax system for redistribution and social policy is democratically and normatively justified.

themes.name: Is progressive income taxation justified as a response to unequal economic resources?
themes.definition: This question examines whether higher tax rates on higher-income taxpayers are normatively justified by distributive justice, economic inequality, or unequal ability to pay.

themes.name: Does the federal tax system favor wealth and capital over labor income?
themes.definition: This question compares the treatment of wages with accumulated wealth, capital income, property, and other returns to determine whether tax rules advantage wealth holders over workers.

themes.name: Should taxation reach unrealized appreciation and other economically valuable gains before a conventional realization event?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the realization doctrine and related timing rules appropriately determine when increases in wealth become taxable income.

themes.name: Do estate, gift, and inheritance taxes effectively reduce intergenerational wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether transfer-tax rules, including their treatment of gifts and property transfers at death, limit the accumulation and transmission of large fortunes.

themes.name: Should the transfer-tax system be structurally strengthened rather than adjusted through isolated provisions?
themes.definition: This question examines whether addressing inherited wealth requires coordinated reform of the estate, gift, and related transfer-tax regimes instead of piecemeal changes.

themes.name: Do tax deductions and exclusions accurately measure taxable income or operate as unjustified subsidies?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether preferential treatment for particular receipts, expenses, or savings has a coherent tax-base rationale or instead creates inequitable advantages.

themes.name: When should deductions or exclusions be allowed for costs associated with earning income or meeting basic living needs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the tax system should distinguish personal consumption from compensatory, income-producing, or subsistence-related expenses.

themes.name: Do refundable tax credits provide effective and equitable income support for vulnerable households?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether refundable credits successfully deliver social-welfare benefits to low-income households and whether the tax system redirects or limits those benefits.

themes.name: Is pursuing social policy through tax preferences preferable to providing benefits through direct public spending?
themes.definition: This question compares tax-based transfers with direct programs in terms of stigma, political feasibility, distributional targeting, administrative cost, and accountability.

themes.name: Do tax benefits and classifications reproduce racial, gender, or other social inequalities?
themes.definition: This question examines whether ostensibly neutral tax rules produce disparate effects for marginalized groups, including differences associated with household structure, race, gender, or social status.

themes.name: Does joint filing distribute tax burdens fairly between married couples and single taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether filing rules and household-based rate structures create marriage bonuses, marriage penalties, or unequal burdens within legally recognized relationships.

themes.name: Should tax law account for unequal financial obligations and economic contributions within families?
themes.definition: This question studies how tax rules should treat transfers, liabilities, dependents, reproductive activities, and other obligations among spouses, partners, and household members.

themes.name: Do tax-based retirement-saving incentives equitably allocate public subsidies across income groups?
themes.definition: This question assesses the fiscal and distributional effects of preferential treatment for retirement saving and whether those benefits primarily assist high-income taxpayers.

themes.name: Do complex tax rules create avoidance opportunities and behavior inconsistent with legislative objectives?
themes.definition: This question investigates how realization rules, legal classifications, timing provisions, and sophisticated planning enable taxpayers to reduce effective taxation or restructure transactions.

themes.name: Should tax law follow economic substance rather than formal labels when classifying transactions and payments?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether economically similar gains, compensation arrangements, property transfers, and financial returns should receive comparable tax treatment despite different legal forms.

themes.name: How should courts and tax administrators resolve uncertainty when statutory tax rules are incomplete or technically ambiguous?
themes.definition: This question examines the proper balance between principled statutory interpretation, administrative authority, judicial review, and policy-based resolution of unsettled tax issues.

themes.name: Do constitutional and legal constraints produce tax rules that are economically irrational or distributively unjust?
themes.definition: This question assesses how taxing-power limitations, constitutional interpretation, and other legal constraints restrict Congress or produce outcomes inconsistent with economic and normative objectives.

themes.name: Does tax-law complexity undermine compliance, administrability, and equitable treatment?
themes.definition: This question studies whether fragmented rules, uncertainty, and complicated eligibility classifications increase compliance costs, weaken enforcement, and cause similarly situated taxpayers to receive different outcomes.

themes.name: Can structural tax reform improve fairness without sacrificing efficiency, revenue, or administrative simplicity?
themes.definition: This question compares incremental amendments with broad redesigns and evaluates whether reform can reconcile distributive equity, economic incentives, fiscal capacity, and workable administration.

themes.name: Should the United States retain an income tax or replace it with a consumption- or expenditure-based system?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the competing distributional, efficiency, revenue, and administrative consequences of preserving the income-tax model versus adopting a radically different tax base.

themes.name: Should accrued investment gains be taxed before realization, including when property is transferred at death?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the realization principle should be retained, modified, or replaced for accrued gains that have not yet been converted into cash or exchanged.

themes.name: How should federal tax law define and measure income when taxpayers receive noncash benefits, unusual financial returns, or economically valuable transfers?
themes.definition: This question examines whether economically beneficial receipts should be included in gross income or excluded because they do not fit conventional legal categories.

themes.name: How should income be timed when transactions, investments, or projects span multiple tax periods?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether deferral, acceleration, or alternative allocation rules accurately measure income and prevent unjustified tax advantages.

themes.name: Should the economic substance of a transaction control its tax treatment rather than its formal legal classification?
themes.definition: This question challenges classifications such as gift versus exchange, income versus capital, or taxable versus excluded receipt when formal labels produce economically inconsistent outcomes.

themes.name: How should tax law allocate income, deductions, and liabilities between spouses and within married households?
themes.definition: This question addresses joint filing, separate reporting, innocent-spouse liability, and the effects of marital organization on federal tax burdens.

themes.name: Do family- and work-based tax rules unfairly burden single parents and households that do not conform to a preferred family model?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax and benefit systems account equitably for household structure, caregiving costs, and the economic circumstances of nontraditional families.

themes.name: Does the federal income-tax system create systematic racial or gender disparities through its treatment of household structure, work, and wealth?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether ostensibly neutral tax rules distribute benefits and burdens differently across racialized and gendered groups.

themes.name: Do targeted tax incentives effectively produce their intended economic behavior without causing excessive distortion or avoidance?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether credits, deductions, exclusions, and other preferences change behavior in socially beneficial ways or merely subsidize activity that would have occurred anyway.

themes.name: Are tax-based safety-net programs properly balancing work incentives with adequate income support for low-income beneficiaries?
themes.definition: This question examines whether benefit phaseouts, refundable credits, and related tax mechanisms improve economic security without imposing damaging labor-supply incentives.

themes.name: Do progressive rates and tax preferences distribute federal tax burdens and benefits fairly across income groups?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether the overall structure of rates, deductions, credits, and exclusions is sufficiently progressive and reduces rather than reinforces inequality.

themes.name: Should the United States rely more heavily on consumption, wealth, or wealth-transfer taxation rather than income taxation?
themes.definition: This question compares alternative tax bases in terms of equity, efficiency, administrability, and their effects on different income and wealth groups.

themes.name: Does the federal tax treatment of capital income and wealth appreciation contribute to excessive wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential or deferred treatment of investment returns gives wealthy taxpayers systematically lower effective burdens than wage earners.

themes.name: Can transfer-tax rules effectively tax accumulated wealth when taxpayers use trusts, family arrangements, or retained control to shift property across generations?
themes.definition: This question examines whether estate, gift, and generation-skipping tax regimes prevent legal and economic avoidance through intra-family transfers.

themes.name: Are retirement-related tax benefits distributed fairly across income groups?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether deductions, exclusions, and deferral for retirement saving disproportionately benefit high-income taxpayers rather than improving broad-based retirement security.

themes.name: Should longstanding tax preferences and exclusions be structurally reformed when their original administrative or policy justifications no longer hold?
themes.definition: This question asks whether historically layered provisions should be retained, narrowed, or replaced because modern economic and social conditions have changed.

themes.name: Would comprehensive structural reform of the federal income tax improve policy outcomes more than incremental amendments?
themes.definition: This question compares systemic replacement or redesign with piecemeal reform, focusing on coherence, revenue, fairness, administrability, and unintended distortions.

themes.name: How should courts and the IRS interpret ambiguous tax provisions when statutory language conflicts with congressional purpose or broader tax policy?
themes.definition: This question examines the institutional allocation of authority among Congress, courts, and tax administrators in resolving contested tax interpretations.

themes.name: Can tax rules be simplified without sacrificing accurate income measurement, equal treatment, and protection against abuse?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tradeoff between administrable uniform rules and the complexity needed to reflect economically diverse transactions and taxpayer circumstances.

themes.name: How do tax-law complexity, uncertainty, and taxpayer adaptation affect compliance and the integrity of the tax base?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether unclear or manipulable rules encourage avoidance, increase compliance costs, and undermine confidence in tax administration.

themes.name: Should tax liability reflect taxpayers’ genuine ability to pay when legal obligations, personal losses, or constrained payments reduce their economic resources?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether deductions, exclusions, and liability-allocation rules properly account for economically burdensome payments and differences in taxpayers’ circumstances.

themes.name: Do tax-favored compensation and employee-benefit arrangements worsen distributive inequality?
themes.definition: This question examines whether exclusions, deductions, and deferrals for employer-provided compensation disproportionately benefit high-income workers at the expense of lower-paid employees and the broader tax base.

themes.name: Can progressive tax rates and refundable credits promote redistribution without creating unacceptable efficiency or horizontal-equity costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether rate progressivity, credits, and alternative rate structures can improve distributional fairness while preserving incentives and comparable treatment of similarly situated taxpayers.

themes.name: Should unrealized appreciation and other accrued capital gains be taxed despite the realization requirement?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether taxing wealth increases before sale would better reflect ability to pay and prevent income-tax avoidance, or whether valuation and liquidity problems justify realization-based taxation.

themes.name: Do estate and gift tax rules adequately prevent wealth transfers from escaping taxation through planning techniques?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether exclusions, valuation rules, entity structures, and transfer-timing strategies undermine the purposes of progressive wealth-transfer taxation.

themes.name: Should income from labor be taxed differently from income from capital, inheritance, and other unearned sources?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the normative and economic justification for maintaining or eliminating tax-rate and base distinctions between labor income and returns to wealth.

themes.name: Does the income-tax base adequately measure economic resources that are not received as ordinary cash income?
themes.definition: This question examines how the tax system should treat noncash benefits, savings, investment-related receipts, imputed income, and other gains that may affect economic welfare without appearing as conventional income.

themes.name: Are deductions and exclusions justified when they depart from a comprehensive measure of income?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether particular deductions and exclusions reflect legitimate costs of earning income or instead function as inequitable tax preferences that distort the tax base.

themes.name: Is joint marital filing and preferential tax treatment of marriage normatively defensible?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether marriage-based tax rules fairly account for household resources and family obligations or produce marriage penalties, bonuses, and unequal treatment of nontraditional families.

themes.name: Should caregiving and other personal-needs expenditures be deductible as costs of earning income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deductions or credits for caregiving would better reconcile family responsibilities with labor-market participation, particularly for women, or improperly subsidize personal consumption.

themes.name: Are tax-based transfer programs an effective and equitable substitute for direct public benefits?
themes.definition: This question compares tax credits and other tax-delivered benefits with direct spending programs in terms of targeting, access, administrative burden, compliance, and effects on low-income households.

themes.name: Do tax incentives for saving and business investment generate socially beneficial investment or mainly increase asset prices and taxpayer returns?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether investment preferences change real economic behavior or are capitalized into the prices and returns of favored assets without achieving their stated policy goals.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow the economic substance of a transaction rather than its formal legal characterization?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether entity form, contractual labels, and traditional income categories produce inappropriate results when they diverge from the transaction’s underlying economic reality.

themes.name: When should amounts associated with prior deductions or tax preferences be recaptured as income?
themes.definition: This question examines how tax law should handle recovery, reversal, or later realization of amounts previously deducted or exempted, including the significance of timing and economic recovery.

themes.name: Can market value provide a fair and administrable basis for taxing noncash transfers and uncertain property interests?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether fair-market-value rules accurately measure taxable benefits and gains when valuation is disputed, benefits are noncash, or property interests are difficult to price.

themes.name: Does tax-system complexity undermine both compliance and distributive fairness?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether intricate rules, reporting requirements, and enforcement procedures impose disproportionate burdens on less-affluent taxpayers and prevent coherent administration.

themes.name: How should courts and tax administrators reconcile statutory text, legislative purpose, and economic consequences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether purposive or economically informed interpretation should limit formally permissible outcomes and how institutional roles should be divided between Congress, courts, and tax agencies.

themes.name: Should tax neutrality yield to targeted interventions that pursue social, corrective, or distributional objectives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates when the tax system should treat economically substitutable activities alike and when differential treatment is justified to address inequality, market failures, or social priorities.

themes.name: How do political incentives and institutional power shape the persistence of tax preferences and the feasibility of reform?
themes.definition: This question investigates how legislators, taxpayers, professional advisers, public opinion, ideology, and organized interests preserve or alter existing tax arrangements.

themes.name: Is comprehensive structural tax reform preferable to incremental amendments to existing federal tax rules?
themes.definition: This question compares broad redesign with targeted statutory and administrative changes as strategies for improving equity, efficiency, simplicity, revenue, and policy coherence.

themes.name: Do facially neutral tax rules reproduce wealth, status, gender, or other forms of structural inequality?
themes.definition: This question examines whether formally uniform rules distribute tax burdens and benefits unequally across historically disadvantaged groups or reinforce existing disparities in wealth and economic security.

themes.name: Do federal tax credits, deductions, and exemptions effectively achieve their stated social-policy goals, or do they mainly provide unjustified benefits to affluent taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax expenditures targeted at housing, retirement, family support, employment, or other social objectives reach intended beneficiaries and produce equitable outcomes.

themes.name: Should the federal income tax become more progressive by broadening the tax base, changing rates, or reducing preferential treatment of high-income taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question examines how rate structures, deductions, exclusions, and other design choices affect progressivity, redistribution, and the distribution of tax burdens.

themes.name: Should unrealized appreciation and other capital gains be taxed before a realization event?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether taxing accrued but unrealized gains would improve income measurement and equity sufficiently to justify valuation, liquidity, and administrative difficulties.

themes.name: Do existing income-tax rules adequately distinguish taxable income from returns of capital, restoration of property, and personal-injury recoveries?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether the classification of receipts and recoveries reflects genuine economic income rather than formal labels or inconsistent judicial doctrines.

themes.name: Should estate and gift taxes be redesigned to prevent wealthy families from transferring assets tax-free during life or at death?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the transfer-tax system coherently treats lifetime gifts, bequests, trusts, and other wealth transfers as part of a unified strategy against concentrated inherited wealth.

themes.name: Do specialized investment vehicles and financial arrangements preserve tax advantages that Congress did not intend, and should their regimes converge with general tax rules?
themes.definition: This question examines whether distinctive rules for particular investment structures create artificial or abusive differences requiring statutory clarification or reform.

themes.name: Do inconsistent rules for recognizing income, deductions, and losses create timing arbitrage that distorts economic decisions?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether taxpayers can exploit mismatched accounting periods, deferral rules, or recognition principles to obtain tax benefits unrelated to underlying economic substance.

themes.name: Do deductions and loss limitations encourage economically inefficient behavior by changing the after-tax cost of expenses, risks, or investments?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the treatment of costs, losses, and contingent liabilities creates distortions that outweigh the policy justifications for the deductions or limitations.

themes.name: When should tax law sacrifice neutrality in order to encourage socially valuable behavior?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether targeted incentives for saving, employment, investment, retirement, or other conduct generate benefits large enough to justify unequal treatment and administrative complexity.

themes.name: Should marriage and family status affect tax liability, or should spouses and households receive more uniform treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether joint filing, marriage preferences, family credits, and household-based classifications are economically justified and consistent with equality principles.

themes.name: Do taxpayers with equal economic income receive unjustifiably different treatment because their income comes from different sources or is associated with different assets and family circumstances?
themes.definition: This question tests the adequacy of horizontal equity when formally similar taxpayers face different tax burdens because of income type, wealth, household status, or legal classification.

themes.name: Should tax rules be judged by economic substance and policy consequences rather than by formal statutory categories?
themes.definition: This question examines when courts and administrators should disregard legal form, reinterpret established classifications, or apply anti-abuse doctrines to prevent artificial tax outcomes.

themes.name: Do Treasury regulations and administrative interpretations implement the Internal Revenue Code clearly, lawfully, and practically?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether delegated tax administration resolves statutory ambiguity consistently with legislative purpose without exceeding legal authority or imposing unworkable burdens.

themes.name: Should structural defects in federal income-tax law be addressed through comprehensive redesign rather than incremental amendments and judicial fixes?
themes.definition: This question compares broad tax-base, classification, and institutional reforms with piecemeal responses to recurring inequities, inconsistencies, and loopholes.

themes.name: Should accumulated wealth and wealth appreciation bear a greater tax burden than labor income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates alternative ways to incorporate wealth, inheritances, and capital appreciation into the tax system while considering avoidance, liquidity, and distributional effects.

themes.name: Do tax-law complexity and professional planning allow sophisticated taxpayers to obtain advantages unavailable to ordinary taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether technical rules, statutory gaps, and planning opportunities produce unequal access to tax benefits and undermine compliance or legitimacy.

themes.name: Are tax-based mechanisms an administratively efficient way to deliver benefits to economically vulnerable families?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether credits and related fiscal programs reach lower- and middle-income households more effectively and with fewer burdens than direct transfer or public-provision alternatives.

themes.name: How should tax policy balance distributive fairness, economic efficiency, behavioral incentives, and administrative feasibility when these objectives conflict?
themes.definition: This question evaluates concrete tax reforms by comparing their effects on inequality, economic behavior, revenue, compliance, implementation costs, and taxpayer autonomy.

themes.name: Do existing tax benefits and obligations accurately target the economic disadvantage or public-interest problem they purport to address?
themes.definition: This question examines whether eligibility criteria based on income, family status, employment, investment, or organizational activity are sufficiently precise and avoid ineffective or overbroad subsidies.

themes.name: What institutional and political conditions determine whether major tax reforms are democratically legitimate and politically sustainable?
themes.definition: This question studies public acceptance, organized resistance, legislative design, historical path dependence, and the relationship between tax distribution and confidence in democratic government.

themes.name: Does progressive income taxation meaningfully redistribute wealth while preserving horizontal equity?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether progressive rates and related income-tax structures actually shift resources toward lower-income households without treating economically similar taxpayers inconsistently.

themes.name: Should the income tax rely on a broad, relatively uniform tax base rather than categorical exclusions and special preferences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether broad-base taxation would produce greater neutrality, fairness, and revenue stability than an income tax containing numerous exclusions, deductions, and preferential rates.

themes.name: Do targeted tax deductions and credits achieve their stated social objectives, or do they primarily subsidize higher-income taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether targeted tax expenditures generate the intended behavior or service while avoiding regressive distributional effects and excessive benefits for taxpayers with greater taxable income.

themes.name: Can estate and inheritance taxation effectively reduce wealth concentration without creating incoherent or administratively unworkable transfer-tax rules?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the revenue, distributional, and administrative effects of taxing transfers made during life or at death, including the interaction between estate, gift, and income taxes.

themes.name: Should income be taxed when it accrues economically, even when realization or payment is deferred?
themes.definition: This question examines whether realization, annual accounting, and deferral rules improperly postpone taxation of investment gains, contingent payments, or other economically received income.

themes.name: Do inconsistent timing, valuation, and deduction rules create tax arbitrage opportunities?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether mismatches between the recognition of income, losses, payments, and related deductions produce unintended advantages or distortions.

themes.name: How should tax law characterize property exchanges, appreciated assets, and transactions between business entities and their owners?
themes.definition: This question asks whether formal legal classifications accurately identify the underlying economic transaction and assign an appropriate federal tax consequence.

themes.name: Should economic substance override formal legal classification when taxpayers use innovative arrangements to reduce tax?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether anti-avoidance doctrine should disregard technically compliant shelters while preserving relief for genuine economic losses and legitimate transactions.

themes.name: Do household, marital, and family classifications produce fair tax burdens and benefit eligibility?
themes.definition: This question examines how filing status, family resources, marital status, household labor, and dependent relationships affect liability and access to tax-based benefits.

themes.name: Should noncommercial household labor and shared family resources be recognized in measuring taxable capacity?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether individualized taxation and conventional income concepts overlook economically significant unpaid labor and intra-family resource arrangements.

themes.name: Are medical, insurance, and dependent-care expenses allocated fairly through the tax system?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether exclusions, deductions, and credits for health-related and care-related costs appropriately distribute their benefits and burdens across households.

themes.name: Do employer compensation and benefit rules distort firms’ ability to attract and retain workers?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether tax treatment of compensation, retirement arrangements, and employer-sponsored benefits changes labor-market decisions in unintended ways.

themes.name: Do tax incentives change private behavior in ways that advance productive investment, or do they mainly generate inefficient responses?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax-favored investment, retirement, and wealth arrangements produce socially valuable activity rather than relabeling, postponing, or reallocating existing behavior.

themes.name: How do high-income taxpayers respond to changes in tax-favored wealth accumulation and retirement rules?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether affluent taxpayers alter the timing, form, or location of income and wealth transfers in response to changes in preferential tax treatment.

themes.name: Is consumption taxation a fairer and more administrable alternative to income taxation?
themes.definition: This question compares income- and consumption-based tax bases with respect to progressivity, savings incentives, administrative feasibility, and distributional consequences.

themes.name: How should capital and wealth taxation balance revenue, investment incentives, and reduction of economic inequality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates competing designs for taxing accumulated wealth and investment income while accounting for effects on capital formation and resource allocation.

themes.name: Can tax policy serve as an effective substitute for direct social provision?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether tax preferences and credits are more effective, equitable, and administrable than direct spending or public-benefit programs for addressing household economic needs.

themes.name: Do tax preferences effectively pursue social and economic objectives beyond revenue collection?
themes.definition: This question asks whether using the tax code to subsidize socially valued investments, services, or behaviors achieves measurable policy goals without excessive complexity or unintended distributional effects.

themes.name: How should statutory and administrative interpretation resolve ambiguous tax concepts and doctrinal changes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether purposive, contextual, judicial, or administrative interpretation produces more coherent and predictable outcomes than isolated textual readings or rigid statutory categories.

themes.name: Can structural tax reform correct inequities more effectively than incremental statutory fixes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether comprehensive redesign is preferable to piecemeal amendments when existing tax provisions generate persistent distortions, uncertainty, or unequal treatment.

themes.name: How much administrative complexity is justified by gains in substantive tax fairness?
themes.definition: This question weighs the fairness benefits of detailed tax rules against taxpayer compliance costs, information burdens, enforcement limitations, and the goal of enabling ordinary taxpayers to determine their liabilities.

themes.name: What constitutional and normative limits should constrain taxation of private property and wealth?
themes.definition: This question examines whether government authority to impose financial obligations for redistribution or public welfare is compatible with theories of property entitlement, legality, and constitutional constraint.

themes.name: Should taxable income be defined by economic gain rather than by formal legal classifications?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax law should look to the economic substance of receipts, payments, and transactions instead of their legal labels or formal structure.

themes.name: How should the tax system treat unrealized appreciation and gains when property is transferred without a conventional sale?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether transfers, gifts, exchanges, or other non-sale events should trigger taxation, deferral, or elimination of tax on accrued gains.

themes.name: Do realization and timing rules produce unjustified differences in tax liability across economically similar taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the timing of income recognition, deductions, recoveries, and losses fairly reflects taxpayers’ economic circumstances.

themes.name: Should lifetime gifts and transfers at death be taxed through an integrated wealth-transfer system?
themes.definition: This question considers whether gifts and bequests should receive coordinated tax treatment to prevent wealth from escaping taxation through the choice of transfer method or timing.

themes.name: Can estate and inheritance taxes effectively reduce intergenerational wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question examines whether transfer taxes can meaningfully limit the accumulation and perpetuation of large fortunes rather than merely raise revenue.

themes.name: How should federal tax law allocate income and tax burdens within families?
themes.definition: This question concerns the treatment of spouses, divorced partners, dependents, and related parties when income, property, or financial obligations are shared or reallocated.

themes.name: Do intrafamily transfer rules and marital tax provisions unfairly advantage particular family structures or wealth levels?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax treatment of marriage, divorce, and family transfers produces inequitable outcomes among differently situated households.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation reduce inequality without imposing economically harmful burdens on work, saving, or investment?
themes.definition: This question tests the normative and behavioral justification for progressive rates in light of their effects on distribution, productivity, and economic activity.

themes.name: Does the tax system systematically favor capital and accumulated wealth over labor income?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether differences in the taxation of wages, investment returns, savings, and wealth produce a structural advantage for wealthy taxpayers.

themes.name: Do deductions, exclusions, and credits distribute tax benefits regressively?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax preferences provide disproportionately large benefits to high-income or high-wealth taxpayers and thereby undermine horizontal or vertical equity.

themes.name: Are tax-based subsidies preferable to direct government spending for delivering social and economic benefits?
themes.definition: This question compares tax incentives and refundable or nonrefundable benefits with direct public programs in terms of targeting, effectiveness, transparency, and distribution.

themes.name: Do tax incentives effectively change behavior enough to justify their distributional and fiscal costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether incentives for saving, investment, work, family support, or socially favored conduct produce benefits greater than their revenue losses and unintended effects.

themes.name: Should tax policy prioritize neutrality toward private decisions or deliberately encourage socially valued conduct?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether the tax system should avoid influencing behavior or use targeted preferences to pursue social, economic, or welfare objectives.

themes.name: Do tax rules create avoidance opportunities by treating formally different transactions differently despite equivalent economic substance?
themes.definition: This question investigates how legal form, categorical classifications, and artificial arrangements allow taxpayers to reduce liability without changing their underlying economic position.

themes.name: How should anti-avoidance doctrines balance revenue protection against flexibility, administrability, and legitimate tax planning?
themes.definition: This question examines when courts, agencies, or legislatures should override formal arrangements and when taxpayers should be permitted to rely on established planning rules.

themes.name: Does tax-system complexity undermine fairness by making intended benefits difficult to claim and compliance costly?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether technical rules, eligibility requirements, and administrative burdens create unequal practical access to tax benefits or impose disproportionate costs on vulnerable taxpayers.

themes.name: Should tax reform favor individualized treatment of taxpayers or simpler rules based on administrable categories?
themes.definition: This question considers the tradeoff between accurately reflecting taxpayers’ differing economic circumstances and maintaining rules that can be applied consistently and cheaply.

themes.name: Do political compromise and special-interest influence produce tax provisions that are economically irrational or distributively unjust?
