themes.definition: This question studies whether legislative incentives, lobbying, and historical bargains explain complex provisions that conflict with stated tax-policy principles.

themes.name: How should courts and tax administrators resolve ambiguity when statutory classifications conflict with legislative purpose or economic substance?
themes.definition: This question examines the appropriate roles of judicial interpretation, agency guidance, and legislative revision in correcting uncertainty and doctrinal inconsistency.

themes.name: Does the federal income tax possess sufficient legal and normative legitimacy to serve broader national policy goals?
themes.definition: This question addresses the limits of governmental taxing power and whether using the income tax for redistribution, social welfare, or economic investment is justified beyond ordinary revenue collection.

themes.name: Should the federal estate-and-gift tax be substantially redesigned to tax large inter vivos and testamentary transfers more effectively?
themes.definition: This question examines whether exemptions, deductions, and the relationship between lifetime gifts and death-time transfers allow substantial fortunes to escape transfer taxation.

themes.name: Does preferential tax treatment of capital income unjustifiably favor wealth over labor income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential rates, realization rules, and other capital-income provisions produce inequitable treatment relative to compensation for work.

themes.name: Should unrealized appreciation be taxed as income rather than deferred until realization?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether changes in the value of assets should enter the tax base before a sale or exchange occurs.

themes.name: Do deductions, exclusions, credits, and deferral provisions distribute tax benefits inequitably across income groups?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether the structure of tax preferences gives disproportionately large benefits to taxpayers with greater income, wealth, or tax liability.

themes.name: Are refundable tax credits more effective and equitable than deductions for delivering family and low-income support?
themes.definition: This question compares refundable credits with deductions as mechanisms for assisting households that have limited taxable income or tax liability.

themes.name: Does the joint income-tax return unfairly redistribute burdens among married couples and alternative household structures?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether joint filing appropriately reflects shared resources or instead creates marriage bonuses, penalties, and unequal treatment across families.

themes.name: Should tax liability follow substantive economic ownership rather than formal ownership or receipt?
themes.definition: This question concerns arrangements in which legal title, contractual receipt, and the person receiving the economic benefit are different taxpayers.

themes.name: Do family-transfer rules adequately distinguish legitimate support from tax-motivated wealth shifting?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the tax treatment of intra-family arrangements can separate genuine familial or marital transfers from artificial income and wealth allocation.

themes.name: Should compensatory payments and nontraditional receipts be taxed according to their recipient's actual economic benefit?
themes.definition: This question addresses the characterization of items such as personal-injury recoveries, settlements, service-related benefits, and other receipts that do not fit ordinary income categories.

themes.name: Do realization, basis, capitalization, and amortization rules accurately measure economically significant gains and costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether asset-related tax rules properly account for acquisition costs, holding costs, appreciation, depreciation, and economically meaningful losses.

themes.name: Can anti-avoidance rules prevent transaction restructuring without becoming excessively uncertain or overbroad?
themes.definition: This question examines whether substance-over-form, disclosure, and related anti-abuse doctrines deter artificial planning while preserving predictable boundaries for legitimate transactions.

themes.name: Should tax doctrines be interpreted purposively when literal application conflicts with the objectives of the statute?
themes.definition: This question concerns how courts and administrators should resolve ambiguous or underdeveloped tax authority when formal text and legislative purpose point in different directions.

themes.name: Do weaknesses in information reporting and IRS enforcement materially erode the tax base?
themes.definition: This question studies whether administrative capacity, reporting obligations, and enforcement practices determine compliance and the practical effectiveness of tax rules.

themes.name: Can the tax system deliver social-welfare benefits more effectively than direct spending or other policy instruments?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether using tax provisions to promote family support, poverty reduction, investment, or economic security achieves those objectives efficiently and equitably.

themes.name: Do tax-based subsidies actually reach disadvantaged taxpayers rather than primarily benefiting higher-income claimants?
themes.definition: This question assesses the incidence and practical accessibility of targeted tax benefits intended to assist low-income people or disadvantaged groups.

themes.name: Should progressive income taxation prioritize redistribution even when it reduces incentives to work, save, or invest?
themes.definition: This question examines the tradeoff between using rates and tax-base design to reduce inequality and preserving behavioral incentives and revenue.

themes.name: Should tax reform broaden the tax base and reduce preferential treatment even at the cost of eliminating popular incentives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether revenue, neutrality, and coherent measurement justify repealing or restructuring politically entrenched deductions, exclusions, and special rates.

themes.name: Should income taxation or consumption taxation provide the primary framework for taxing saving and investment?
themes.definition: This question compares income-based and consumption-based tax bases in terms of equity, economic efficiency, treatment of capital, and administrative feasibility.

themes.name: Do formally neutral tax classifications produce unequal burdens for taxpayers with different income sources, assets, or family circumstances?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether apparently uniform rules generate disparate outcomes because taxpayers occupy economically or socially different positions.

themes.name: How should federal tax reform balance accurate measurement, distributive fairness, economic efficiency, and administrative simplicity?
themes.definition: This question concerns the institutional and design tradeoffs involved when no tax regime can simultaneously maximize precision, equity, incentives, and workability.

themes.name: Should the realization principle continue to determine when capital appreciation becomes taxable income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether taxation should await a sale or other realization event, or instead reach unrealized increases in wealth and earning capacity.

themes.name: Can a comprehensive-income tax base fairly include income that current tax law excludes, defers, or treats preferentially?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether exclusions, deferrals, and special rules are consistent with an economically comprehensive measure of income.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow the economic substance of a transaction rather than its formal legal classification?
themes.definition: This question asks whether courts and administrators should disregard formal categories when they produce outcomes inconsistent with a transaction’s economic effects or policy rationale.

themes.name: When compensation is routed through a separate entity, should the service provider or the entity bear the resulting tax liability?
themes.definition: This question concerns assignment-of-income rules and the attribution of employment or service-related income among individuals and related entities.

themes.name: How should noncash benefits, property distributions, and mixed payments be characterized and taxed?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether property or payments containing multiple economic components should be taxed like cash income, transfers, consumption, or investment returns.

themes.name: Should lifetime gifts and transfers at death be taxed through an integrated wealth-transfer system?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether gifts and inheritances should be treated consistently to prevent untaxed transfers of wealth across generations.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation of high-income individuals reduce wealth inequality without unacceptable efficiency or growth costs?
themes.definition: This question examines the distributive, behavioral, and revenue consequences of increasing the progressivity of taxation on affluent taxpayers.

themes.name: Are deductions, exclusions, and credits justified when they provide unequal access to wealth-building or tax benefits?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax preferences distribute benefits fairly among taxpayers with different incomes, resources, and opportunities to claim them.

themes.name: Do tax preferences achieve their intended social objectives, or do they mainly create regressive and inefficient subsidies?
themes.definition: This question tests whether targeted tax expenditures actually change behavior or improve social welfare in ways that justify their distributional and revenue costs.

themes.name: Should tax policy use behavioral incentives to pursue social goals when those incentives produce unintended distributional effects?
themes.definition: This question considers whether influencing private decisions through the tax code is justified despite possible distortions, paternalism, or unequal impacts.

themes.name: Can tax rules be simplified without sacrificing equity, revenue, or accurate measurement of taxpayers’ economic capacity?
themes.definition: This question examines the tradeoffs between simpler tax rules and the ability to distinguish economically different taxpayers and transactions.

themes.name: Do complex tax rules impose disproportionate compliance and administrative burdens on resource-constrained taxpayers and organizations?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether technical requirements, uncertainty, and professional-advice costs make the tax system less accessible and less equitable.

themes.name: Do anti-avoidance rules protect the tax base at the cost of excessive uncertainty and administrative complexity?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether rules designed to prevent strategic tax planning produce sufficient revenue and fairness benefits to justify their implementation costs.

themes.name: How should courts and tax administrators resolve ambiguous statutes and novel transactions while preserving uniformity and predictability?
themes.definition: This question concerns the influence of judicial and administrative interpretation on the consistent application of federal income-tax law.

themes.name: Should formal tax classifications be rejected when they create economically inefficient or inequitable differences among similarly situated taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether legal distinctions based on labels, family arrangements, or transaction form can justify divergent tax treatment.

themes.name: How far may the government’s taxing power extend before constitutional, legal, or fairness constraints require limits?
themes.definition: This question examines the tension between expansive sovereign authority to tax and protections for private property, taxpayer autonomy, and legal certainty.

themes.name: Is structural tax reform preferable to piecemeal correction of defective income-tax provisions?
themes.definition: This question compares comprehensive redesign with incremental amendments as methods for correcting fragmented, outdated, or internally inconsistent tax rules.

themes.name: Can redistributive tax reform be politically enacted and sustained despite resistance from taxpayers and organized private interests?
themes.definition: This question investigates how political perceptions, institutional incentives, and concentrated interests affect the feasibility and persistence of redistribution through taxation.

themes.name: Should tax liability reflect taxpayers’ resources and economic capacity beyond their reported annual income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates alternatives that account for wealth, lifetime resources, consumption, deferred compensation, or other indicators of ability to pay.

themes.name: How should direct income taxation be balanced against indirect consumption taxation to achieve fair distribution with acceptable economic incentives?
themes.definition: This question compares the incidence, efficiency, and equity consequences of taxing income directly versus taxing consumption and related transactions.

themes.name: Should economically equivalent transactions receive the same tax treatment despite differences in their formal legal structure?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax neutrality and substantive economic equivalence should prevail over formal distinctions among transactions, entities, or property transfers.

themes.name: Should income be taxed when it accrues economically, when it is realized legally, or when it is actually received?
themes.definition: This question evaluates competing rules for taxing deferred, contingent, investment, litigation-related, and other income whose economic benefits arise before formal realization.

themes.name: Should the federal tax base move beyond accretion-based income taxation toward consumption, wealth, or hybrid taxation?
themes.definition: This question compares income, consumption, and wealth-based tax bases in terms of fairness, administrability, revenue, and economic effects.

themes.name: Is progressive income taxation a justified and effective means of redistributing income?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether higher tax burdens on higher-income taxpayers are normatively justified and whether progressivity advances distributive justice without unacceptable efficiency costs.

themes.name: Do deductions, exclusions, and refundable credits distribute tax benefits fairly across income groups?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether targeted tax preferences produce equitable outcomes or disproportionately benefit taxpayers with greater income, wealth, or access to tax planning.

themes.name: Do tax incentives improve investment and other socially valuable behavior enough to justify their revenue and distributional costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential treatment changes private behavior in desirable ways and whether those gains outweigh distortions, fiscal costs, and inequities.

themes.name: Should tax liability reflect household composition, personal expenditures, and differences in taxpayers’ ability to pay?
themes.definition: This question examines whether family responsibilities, education costs, medical needs, and other personal circumstances should alter individual income-tax obligations.

themes.name: Should inheritances and inter vivos wealth transfers be taxed more heavily to limit wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the fairness, effectiveness, and economic consequences of estate, gift, and other transfer taxes as instruments for addressing inherited advantage.

themes.name: Should returns to capital and accumulated wealth be taxed more heavily than labor income?
themes.definition: This question compares the tax treatment of financial capital, wealth appreciation, savings, and investment returns with that of wages and human capital.

themes.name: Should personal-injury, tort, and litigation-related payments be excluded from income when they compensate for nonphysical or difficult-to-measure harm?
themes.definition: This question addresses the boundary between compensatory damages and taxable income, including how tort-law concepts should influence federal tax treatment.

themes.name: Should tax deductions for losses be matched symmetrically with the taxation of related recoveries, insurance proceeds, or benefits?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deductions, inclusions, basis adjustments, and exclusions should be coordinated across economically connected losses and recoveries.

themes.name: Where should the legal boundary lie between legitimate tax planning and impermissible avoidance through recharacterization or entity structuring?
themes.definition: This question considers when taxpayers’ use of formal legal arrangements to convert, defer, or eliminate income should be respected or overridden by judicial and administrative doctrines.

themes.name: Should specialized tax provisions be interpreted consistently with general tax principles and their underlying legislative purposes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates conflicts between technical provisions and broader principles such as neutrality, accurate income measurement, equity, and congressional intent.

themes.name: Does tax-law complexity undermine equitable liability determination, administration, and taxpayer compliance?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether detailed classifications and specialized rules generate unintended disparities, administrative burdens, uncertainty, or opportunities for arbitrary outcomes.

themes.name: Should the IRS have broad authority to administer, deny, or recoup refundable tax benefits?
themes.definition: This question examines the proper balance between administrative enforcement, protection against improper claims, taxpayer rights, and congressional control over benefit programs.

themes.name: Are targeted amendments preferable to comprehensive restructuring of the federal income-tax system?
themes.definition: This question compares incremental reform with fundamental redesign in light of policy effectiveness, institutional disruption, administrability, and political feasibility.

themes.name: Can tax reform simultaneously promote economic growth, preserve revenue, and reduce inequality?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether a tax system can reconcile distributive goals with investment incentives, efficient allocation, and sustainable public finances.

themes.name: Are refundable tax credits an effective substitute for or complement to direct social-welfare and income-support programs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates tax-based benefits as anti-poverty and social-insurance instruments, including their effects on work, household security, access, and political acceptance.

themes.name: Do tax subsidies for education and human-capital investment correct socially inefficient underinvestment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deductions, credits, exclusions, or other tax preferences for higher education produce sufficient social and economic benefits to justify their costs.

themes.name: Do existing tax structures adequately constrain concentrated wealth and unequal political influence?
themes.definition: This question links taxation of wealth, transfers, and economic advantage to the broader problem of whether fiscal institutions reinforce or counteract concentrated economic and political power.

themes.name: Should federal tax treatment follow economic substance rather than the formal legal structure of economically equivalent transactions?
themes.definition: This question examines whether transactions with similar economic effects should receive the same federal income-tax treatment despite differences in legal form, ownership labels, or contractual structure.

themes.name: When should changes in ownership or property rights trigger immediate federal income-tax consequences?
themes.definition: This question concerns the timing of income recognition when taxpayers transfer, acquire, exchange, or otherwise alter legally recognized interests in property.

themes.name: Should taxable income account for economically related costs, losses, and personal harms when measuring a taxpayer’s net gain?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether deductions or exclusions should reflect expenses, losses, settlements, and extraordinary personal harms that reduce a taxpayer’s actual economic resources.

themes.name: How should federal tax law distinguish accumulated wealth and property from current income?
themes.definition: This question asks whether tax rules can coherently separate existing wealth, capital appreciation, and property holdings from newly realized income.

themes.name: Are preferential tax rates for capital gains, savings, and capital income justified by their effects on investment and inequality?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether favorable treatment of capital and savings produces sufficient economic benefits to justify its distributional costs.

themes.name: Can estate and gift taxes effectively limit intergenerational wealth concentration without excessive avoidance and mobility responses?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether wealth-transfer taxes are capable of achieving distributive goals while remaining administrable and resistant to tax planning.

themes.name: Does a progressive income-tax system adequately implement ability-to-pay and vertical-equity principles?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax burdens are distributed fairly among taxpayers with different incomes, wealth levels, and economic resources.

themes.name: Are exclusions, deductions, credits, and other tax subsidies justified by their distributional and behavioral effects?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether departures from ordinary taxation fairly target their intended beneficiaries or instead produce inefficient or regressive advantages.

themes.name: Do formal tax classifications create unjust disparities among taxpayers or payments that are economically similar?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether statutory categories, income labels, and recipient classifications produce unequal outcomes without a defensible substantive basis.

themes.name: Do realization rules and capital-asset classifications enable taxpayers to defer or convert ordinary income into preferentially taxed capital gain?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether the structure of realization and capital-gain rules creates avoidable opportunities for tax deferral, recharacterization, or conversion.

themes.name: Should tax rules permit the transfer or trading of tax benefits away from their original holders?
themes.definition: This question examines the economic and legal consequences of making credits, deductions, losses, or other tax attributes portable or transferable.

themes.name: How should tax rules account for multi-year timing, changing circumstances, and death when measuring income and tax liability?
themes.definition: This question asks whether annual accounting adequately captures taxpayers’ economic positions when income, losses, ownership, or financial capacity changes over time.

themes.name: Do family-based tax provisions fairly balance household autonomy, partner equality, and tax neutrality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether marriage, partnership, dependency, and family-tax rules respect individual choice while avoiding unjustified advantages or burdens among legally recognized households.

themes.name: Do tax and welfare rules promote labor-market participation at the expense of economic security and personal autonomy?
themes.definition: This question examines whether benefit eligibility, work incentives, and employment-related tax provisions produce desirable labor responses without excluding poor or unemployed people from social participation.

themes.name: Can retirement and employee-benefit regulation provide income security while preserving employer and plan-design flexibility?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether retirement and ERISA-related rules adequately protect future income without imposing excessive constraints on employers or benefit plans.

themes.name: Should tax policy pursue social and moral objectives beyond revenue raising, or should it remain neutral among competing values?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether tax incentives and preferences may legitimately shape conduct, family life, investment, or other social outcomes rather than merely collect revenue.

themes.name: Do tax incentives produce socially valuable economic behavior, or primarily create distortions, avoidance, and unintended consequences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how credits, deductions, exemptions, and rate differentials affect investment, consumption, compliance, and other taxpayer decisions.

themes.name: Should tax reform replace targeted and fragmented regimes with a more uniform tax base?
themes.definition: This question asks whether simplifying or broadening the tax base would improve coherence, fairness, revenue, and administration more than it would sacrifice legitimate policy objectives.

themes.name: Can major tax reform improve equity and efficiency while preserving continuity and administrative feasibility?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether structural reforms can correct systemic distortions without imposing unacceptable transition costs, compliance burdens, or uncertainty on taxpayers.

themes.name: How should courts, Congress, and tax administrators divide responsibility for resolving ambiguous and unsettled tax-treatment questions?
themes.definition: This question examines the institutional roles of statutory text, judicial doctrine, Treasury interpretation, enforcement, and legislative reform in determining tax outcomes.

themes.name: Should federal tax policy impose greater burdens on high-income taxpayers and large fortunes to reduce wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question examines whether progressive income, wealth-transfer, estate, or related taxes can legitimately and effectively redistribute resources from wealthy taxpayers to economically disadvantaged groups.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for savings and investment promote desirable accumulation without worsening inequality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether exclusions, deductions, and other favorable rules for retirement savings, capital income, and investment returns produce sufficient economic benefits to justify their distributional costs.

themes.name: Should the tax system distinguish less between capital income and labor income?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether differential treatment of capital gains, investment returns, and wages is economically justified or instead creates inefficient and inequitable distortions.

themes.name: Should increases in wealth be taxed when they accrue rather than when assets are realized?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether an accrual-based approach to unrealized appreciation would better measure economic income than realization-based taxation, given valuation, liquidity, administrative, and compliance constraints.

themes.name: How should tax basis and realization rules prevent taxation of capital recovery while capturing genuine economic gain?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether basis adjustments, accounting rules, and realization doctrines accurately distinguish recovery of prior investment from newly taxable income in transfers and asset transactions.

themes.name: When should noncash benefits, property exchanges, and business transactions produce taxable income?
themes.definition: This question examines how tax law should determine when in-kind receipts or economically valuable noncash transactions constitute taxable income despite difficulties in valuation and classification.

themes.name: Do tax exclusions, deductions, and credits provide justified subsidies, or should ineffective preferences be curtailed?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether particular tax expenditures achieve legitimate social or economic objectives more effectively than direct spending or other policy instruments.

themes.name: Can targeted tax benefits be designed to improve equity without creating new distortions or excessive complexity?
themes.definition: This question assesses how eligibility rules, benefit structures, and statutory limits affect the distributional, behavioral, fiscal, and administrative consequences of targeted tax subsidies.

themes.name: Should refundable tax credits function as core anti-poverty programs rather than merely as work incentives?
themes.definition: This question examines whether low-income and refundable credits should support nonworking, involuntarily unemployed, or caregiving households in addition to subsidizing employment.

themes.name: Does using the tax system to deliver social welfare produce better outcomes than direct government assistance?
themes.definition: This question compares tax-based income support with direct spending and nonstate provision in terms of effectiveness, accessibility, administrative capacity, and distributive fairness.

themes.name: Should family taxation treat married couples as a single economic unit?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the consequences of joint versus separate taxation for marital property, household resource allocation, marriage incentives, and the distribution of tax burdens between spouses.

themes.name: Does family tax policy unfairly privilege marriage, sole-earner households, or conventional family arrangements?
themes.definition: This question examines whether rules governing spousal transfers, family expenses, caregiving, and household eligibility treat nontraditional households and women’s economic agency comparably to legally married or one-earner families.

themes.name: Should federal estate and gift taxes be strengthened to limit intergenerational wealth concentration and avoidance?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether wealth-transfer rules, valuation provisions, and anti-avoidance mechanisms adequately tax accumulated wealth passed between generations.

themes.name: Do formal tax classifications produce unequal treatment of economically similar taxpayers and activities?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether distinctions based on legal form, taxpayer category, transaction structure, or property classification create unjustified departures from tax neutrality and substantive equality.

themes.name: Can anti-avoidance rules prevent abusive tax planning without denying legitimate losses, transfers, or intended tax benefits?
themes.definition: This question examines how doctrines and statutory restrictions should distinguish strategic manipulation and income shifting from lawful planning and genuine economic transactions.

themes.name: Do tax planning opportunities undermine the redistributive aims of progressive taxation?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether deferral, sheltering, income shifting, and other legally permissible strategies allow advantaged taxpayers to escape burdens intended by progressive tax rules.

themes.name: Should tax law prioritize economic substance over formal legal characterization?
themes.definition: This question examines whether courts and legislators should tax transactions according to their real economic effects rather than their contractual labels or rigid doctrinal categories.

themes.name: Can tax simplification improve fairness and compliance without sacrificing legitimate policy differentiation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether reducing specialized provisions, uncertainty, and administrative complexity would produce more equitable and effective taxation or merely eliminate useful distinctions.

themes.name: How should tax reform balance equity, efficiency, revenue, and administrative feasibility?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether proposed reforms can achieve distributive and economic objectives while remaining politically implementable, legally legitimate, fiscally sustainable, and administrable.

themes.name: Should tax rules be interpreted and reformed according to their underlying purposes rather than their formal wording?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the role of statutory purpose, tax theory, historical context, and normative commitments in resolving ambiguous provisions and correcting outcomes that conflict with policy objectives.

themes.name: Should the federal income tax be replaced or supplemented by a consumption-oriented tax base?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether shifting taxation from income toward consumption would improve efficiency, equity, revenue collection, and the treatment of saving and accumulated wealth.

themes.name: Can fundamental tax reform overcome the political and institutional forces that favor incremental legislative change?
themes.definition: This question examines why comprehensive reform proposals give way to piecemeal changes and whether durable structural reform is politically feasible.

themes.name: Should taxable income reflect taxpayers’ actual economic ability to pay rather than formal income categories?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether income taxation should measure economic resources, including implicit returns and nontraditional benefits, more directly than current legal classifications do.

themes.name: Should tax policy prioritize progressive redistribution over neutrality and equal treatment across taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question weighs progressive distributional objectives against proportional treatment, taxpayer neutrality, and other conventional principles of good taxation.

themes.name: Do deductions, exemptions, and other tax preferences achieve legitimate policy goals or mainly create inequitable implicit subsidies?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential provisions produce socially valuable behavior and assistance or instead distribute benefits inefficiently toward privileged taxpayers.

themes.name: Can refundable tax credits improve the economic security of vulnerable households without distorting work and family decisions?
themes.definition: This question examines refundable credits as welfare instruments, focusing on their effects on after-tax well-being, labor-market participation, eligibility, and distribution.

themes.name: Should the income tax treat marriage, family relationships, and caregiving responsibilities as tax-relevant economic circumstances?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether rules governing the taxable unit, children, household expenses, and caregiving fairly allocate tax burdens while supporting equal participation in work.

themes.name: Do tax-and-transfer systems reproduce gendered and racialized inequalities in income, wealth, and economic security?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether formally general tax and benefit rules distribute resources and opportunities unequally across gendered and racialized groups.

themes.name: Should tax law privilege economic substance over formal ownership, transaction, and relationship classifications?
themes.definition: This question asks whether liability and benefits should follow the real economic consequences of an arrangement when legal form produces unequal or nonneutral results.

themes.name: When should receipts, transfers, and unusual economic benefits count as taxable gross income?
themes.definition: This question addresses the boundaries of the tax base for one-time receipts, noncash transfers, personal-injury payments, and other amounts that may not represent conventional income.

themes.name: Should income taxation continue to rely on realization rather than taxing annual changes in economic wealth?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether gains should become taxable only upon realization or whether appreciation and investment returns should be recognized as they accrue.

themes.name: How should tax law treat deferred gains and noncash changes in ownership interests?
themes.definition: This question examines when property exchanges, altered ownership rights, and other noncash transactions should trigger immediate gain or loss recognition.

themes.name: Do anti-avoidance rules appropriately distinguish abusive tax manipulation from genuine losses, deductions, and transfers?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether limits on deductions, basis adjustments, and transaction planning prevent artificial tax reduction without denying legitimate economic relief.

themes.name: Should taxpayers be permitted to use sophisticated planning structures that reduce tax liability without reducing economic income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legitimacy and consequences of tax planning by affluent taxpayers and businesses when formal arrangements exploit gaps among tax regimes.

themes.name: How should tax policy balance favorable treatment of saving and retirement with the risk of subsidizing accumulated wealth?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deferral and investment-related preferences promote retirement security and productive investment or disproportionately benefit high-income and wealthy taxpayers.

themes.name: Should personal and household expenditures be deductible when they support future income or socially valuable activity?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether expenses for education, caregiving, child-related needs, and other personal uses should receive tax-favored treatment rather than being classified as ordinary consumption.

themes.name: Can tax rules reconcile economic incentives with distributive justice?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether tax design can encourage work, investment, saving, and development while reducing inequality and protecting economically vulnerable groups.

themes.name: How much should administrative feasibility and compliance cost influence substantive tax policy?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether administrability, enforcement capacity, valuation difficulty, and implementation costs justify departures from theoretically preferable tax rules.

themes.name: How should courts and tax administrators resolve conflicts between statutory text, legal precedent, historical purpose, and economic substance?
themes.definition: This question examines the institutional interpretation of ambiguous or novel tax provisions and the extent to which judicial and administrative practice should shape tax outcomes.

themes.name: Do constitutional and institutional constraints protect legitimate limits on taxing power or obstruct necessary tax reform?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether legal constraints on taxing receipts, transfers, and consumption should be retained, narrowed, or revised in response to contemporary distributive and fiscal goals.

themes.name: Should federal transfer taxes be retained and redesigned to limit the intergenerational concentration of wealth and political power?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether estate and gift taxes should be reformed rather than abolished, and whether they effectively promote egalitarianism without creating excessive avoidance or administrative costs.

themes.name: Should accrued capital gains be taxed before realization, including when property is transferred at death?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether realization-based taxation understates economic income and whether gains on appreciated assets should instead be taxed periodically or upon death.

themes.name: How should tax law measure and collect tax on appreciation in illiquid or privately held assets?
themes.definition: This question examines valuation, liquidity, payment timing, and related-liability problems that arise when taxpayers hold wealth that has increased in value but has not produced cash.

themes.name: Do tax deductions, exclusions, credits, and other preferences distribute public benefits toward affluent taxpayers rather than those with greater need?
themes.definition: This question assesses the incidence, fairness, and policy effectiveness of tax expenditures compared with direct or refundable forms of government assistance.

themes.name: Should tax preferences for saving, investment, and homeownership be limited when they increase wealth inequality?
themes.definition: This question tests whether the growth and savings incentives associated with preferential treatment justify its unequal benefits across income and wealth groups.

themes.name: Are refundable and targeted tax credits more equitable and effective than deductions or exclusions for delivering assistance to low-income households?
themes.definition: This question compares alternative tax-based benefit mechanisms according to distributional impact, work incentives, administrative feasibility, and access by households with little tax liability.

themes.name: Should the federal income tax redistribute more income toward households with limited resources while preserving work and investment incentives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the appropriate scale and design of income-tax redistribution in light of poverty reduction, economic growth, labor supply, and taxpayer autonomy.

themes.name: Does the income tax fairly account for family size, dependents, marriage, and different patterns of paid and unpaid work?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether ability-to-pay rules and family tax relief adequately reflect household circumstances, gendered work roles, and the costs of supporting dependents.

themes.name: Should receipts and benefits arising from family or personal circumstances be treated as taxable income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether transfers, compensation, and noncash benefits should be taxed according to their economic value, legal form, or underlying personal and familial purpose.

themes.name: Do formal tax classifications produce unjustified differences between economically similar payments, recipients, or transactions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether labels such as compensation, gifts, benefits, liabilities, or ownership interests obscure substantively equivalent economic positions.

themes.name: Should tax liability follow economic substance rather than the formal legal structure of a transaction?
themes.definition: This question addresses conflicts between legal form and economic reality in determining taxable income, deductions, ownership, and access to preferential treatment.

themes.name: How should tax law distinguish legitimate planning from sophisticated transactions that exploit structural loopholes or monetize tax benefits?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the proper scope of anti-abuse rules and their tradeoff between preventing opportunistic tax avoidance and preserving efficient transactions.

themes.name: Do anti-avoidance rules governing family wealth transfers prevent abuse without imposing unjust or overbroad burdens on legitimate family arrangements?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether rules addressing intra-family transfers and trust-based preferences appropriately balance enforcement, family autonomy, and equitable taxation.

themes.name: Do tax-timing, realization, and loss-recognition rules create economically significant distortions in saving, investment, and other decisions?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the timing of inclusion, deduction, or recognition causes taxpayers to alter otherwise productive behavior or produces inequitable outcomes.

themes.name: Is taxable income an adequate measure of economic welfare and ability to pay?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether income-based liability captures noncash benefits, appreciation, household circumstances, and other dimensions of economic capacity.

themes.name: Should the United States prefer an income tax or a consumption tax for taxing savings, capital returns, and accumulated wealth?
themes.definition: This question compares the distributional, efficiency, complexity, and revenue consequences of income-based and consumption-based tax systems.

themes.name: Can tax reform reduce inequality and promote economic growth without sacrificing administrative simplicity and neutrality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the central tradeoff among redistribution, incentives, economic efficiency, accurate income measurement, and manageable compliance obligations.

themes.name: Does the IRS have sufficient institutional capacity to administer tax-based benefits and enforce income- and wealth-tax rules fairly?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether administrative resources, compliance mechanisms, valuation practices, and enforcement authority determine the practical success and distributional effects of tax policy.

themes.name: Should Congress modernize specialized tax rules to address changing economic arrangements, financial products, and family structures?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether existing statutory categories remain coherent and adequate as transactions, employment, marriage, benefits, and investment products evolve.

themes.name: Can politically feasible tax reforms produce durable reductions in concentrated private economic power?
themes.definition: This question examines how political institutions, organized interests, prevailing tax ideologies, and administrative constraints shape the adoption and long-term survival of redistributive reforms.

themes.name: Should federal income taxation become more progressive to better reflect taxpayers’ ability to pay?
themes.definition: This question examines whether greater rate progressivity improves distributive fairness without creating unacceptable revenue, efficiency, or administrative costs.

themes.name: Should wealth and unrealized appreciation be taxed in addition to ordinary income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether an income-tax-centered system inadequately captures economic resources because it defers or excludes taxation of accumulated wealth and unrealized gains.

themes.name: Is the preferential tax treatment of capital income over labor income normatively and economically justified?
themes.definition: This question compares the fairness, investment, behavioral, and revenue consequences of taxing returns to capital differently from wages and business income.

themes.name: Do deductions, credits, exclusions, and exemptions distribute tax benefits inequitably among similarly situated taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether the design of tax preferences creates unequal effective tax burdens or arbitrary advantages across taxpayers with comparable economic circumstances.

themes.name: Should socially motivated subsidies be delivered through the tax code rather than through direct government spending?
themes.definition: This question compares tax-based assistance with direct benefits in terms of targeting, political legitimacy, welfare effects, transparency, and administrative cost.

themes.name: Do tax incentives actually produce their intended social or economic benefits?
themes.definition: This question tests whether targeted deductions, credits, and exemptions change behavior or improve beneficiaries’ welfare sufficiently to justify their fiscal and distributional costs.

themes.name: Do tax preferences create economically inefficient distortions in investment, work, saving, or consumption?
themes.definition: This question examines whether preferential tax treatment reallocates resources toward tax-favored activities without generating offsetting public benefits.

themes.name: How should tax timing, deferral, and phase-in or withdrawal rules be designed to balance fairness and behavioral neutrality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the timing and gradual adjustment of tax liabilities or benefits produce unjustified disparities, planning opportunities, or economic distortions.

themes.name: Can anti-income-shifting and anti-avoidance rules prevent taxpayers from exploiting formal distinctions without imposing excessive compliance costs?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether legal responses to shelters, strategic transactions, and income shifting can preserve the intended tax base while remaining enforceable and administrable.

themes.name: Should tax liability follow formal legal classifications or the underlying economic substance of receipts and transactions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how tax law should classify noncash transfers, recoveries, compensation, gifts, and other disputed items when legal form and economic benefit diverge.

themes.name: Should taxpayers be taxed on economic gains or obligations that they did not directly receive, realize, or control?
themes.definition: This question examines the normative and practical limits of imposing tax consequences on attributed income, transferred wealth, or unrealized economic benefits.

themes.name: Does the choice of taxable unit—individual, couple, household, or family—produce equitable treatment of different family forms?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether joint or separate taxation of spouses and dependents fairly reflects shared resources, marriage decisions, and diverse household arrangements.

themes.name: Do marriage-related tax rules reinforce unequal outcomes across gender, race, and family structure?
themes.definition: This question examines whether formally neutral rules governing marriage, work, caregiving, and household income produce disparate distributional or behavioral consequences.

themes.name: Are tax provisions for medical, insurance, dependent-care, and other household expenses an equitable way to address unequal economic burdens?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether these deductions and credits effectively target genuine needs or instead provide disproportionate benefits to taxpayers with greater taxable income and planning capacity.

themes.name: Can gift and wealth-transfer taxes effectively prevent tax-motivated transfers and reduce intergenerational inequality?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether estate, gift, and related transfer-tax rules capture accumulated wealth and limit avoidance without generating excessive valuation and compliance problems.

themes.name: Should tax and transfer programs be evaluated as one integrated system of redistribution?
themes.definition: This question asks whether the fairness and progressivity of fiscal policy can be assessed adequately by examining taxes and government benefits together rather than separately.

themes.name: Do complex income-tax rules impose unequal administrative and compliance burdens on vulnerable taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether statutory complexity, eligibility conditions, and enforcement practices disproportionately disadvantage low-income individuals, small businesses, or taxpayers with limited expertise.

themes.name: Should tax reform prioritize administrability and practical effectiveness over theoretically optimal equity or efficiency?
themes.definition: This question examines how much distributive or economic precision should be sacrificed when a theoretically superior tax rule is difficult to administer, enforce, or understand.

themes.name: Do constitutional equality principles constrain differential tax treatment of economically similar taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates when tax classifications based on income, wealth, family status, work, or other categories become constitutionally or normatively impermissible.

themes.name: How do political institutions, expertise, ideology, and public perceptions shape the legitimacy and design of tax reform?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether tax rules are driven primarily by principled policy analysis or by institutional incentives, organized interests, political rhetoric, and resistance to redistribution.

themes.name: Do tax-based social-policy benefits achieve their intended goals as effectively and equitably as direct government programs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax expenditures and tax subsidies are suitable instruments for promoting social welfare, economic self-sufficiency, or other non-revenue objectives.

themes.name: Do family-based tax and transfer rules unfairly disadvantage nontraditional households and women with different work and caregiving roles?
themes.definition: This question examines whether household eligibility rules, marital assumptions, and family-related benefits distribute burdens and benefits unequally across family structures and gendered economic roles.

themes.name: Should married couples be taxed as a single economic unit or according to each partner's individual economic circumstances?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether joint taxation and marital attribution accurately and fairly allocate tax liability between spouses.

themes.name: Should tax law rely on formal taxpayer categories or account for individualized economic circumstances?
themes.definition: This question tests whether categorical classifications produce unjustified differences when taxpayers who are formally different have economically similar circumstances.

themes.name: Does preferential taxation of capital and investment income worsen inequality and wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the distributional and behavioral consequences of lower rates, exclusions, deductions, or other preferences for capital income and investment returns.

themes.name: Should labor income be taxed differently from capital income, inheritance, and other unearned income?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether distinctions among labor and unearned income are justified by fairness, efficiency, or wealth-distribution concerns.

themes.name: Does the realization requirement unjustifiably defer taxation of accrued investment gains and accumulated wealth?
themes.definition: This question examines whether taxation should occur when gains accrue or only when property is sold, exchanged, or otherwise realized.

themes.name: How should federal tax law treat economically valuable noncash receipts, deferred payments, and unconventional gains?
themes.definition: This question concerns when and how the income tax should recognize, value, and include economic benefits that do not take the form of immediate cash wages.

themes.name: Does the exclusion for personal-injury recoveries appropriately distinguish compensation for physical injury from punitive damages and lost income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the scope of section 104(a)(2) and related rules governing the tax treatment of different components of personal-injury awards.

themes.name: Does progressive taxation fairly redistribute public burdens and reduce economically significant inequality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates progressive rates and related redistribution according to competing claims about economic justice, opportunity, and taxpayer responsibility.

themes.name: Should tax systems use a broad income base with progressive rates rather than category-specific deductions, exclusions, and credits?
themes.definition: This question compares comprehensive taxation with preferential treatment for selected forms of income, activities, or taxpayers.

themes.name: Do tax incentives create economically harmful distortions in saving, investment, risk-taking, or the timing of transactions?
themes.definition: This question examines whether differences in tax treatment alter behavior and resource allocation in ways that reduce economic efficiency or undermine policy objectives.

themes.name: Do deductions, exemptions, and basis rules accurately match taxable income with genuine economic loss or expense?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether tax accounting rules prevent unwarranted deductions, duplicative benefits, and taxation that fails to correspond to underlying economic changes.

themes.name: Do existing tax rules create substantial opportunities for sophisticated taxpayers to avoid or minimize tax liability?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether formal rules, trusts, timing strategies, or nonstandard arrangements permit unintended tax advantages and how those opportunities should be limited.

themes.name: Do anti-abuse rules appropriately distinguish illegitimate tax avoidance from legitimate tax planning and investment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether anti-avoidance doctrines and statutory restrictions are sufficiently targeted without improperly invalidating lawful economic arrangements.

themes.name: Should courts, tax administrators, or Congress be primarily responsible for correcting problematic tax rules?
themes.definition: This question examines the institutional allocation of authority for resolving statutory gaps, inequities, unintended consequences, and conflicts between tax doctrine and policy.

themes.name: Should tax-law interpretation prioritize economic substance and policy consequences over formal legal status and literal statutory categories?
themes.definition: This question evaluates functional interpretation against bright-line or formalist approaches when legal classifications do not reflect the substantive character of a transaction.

themes.name: When should administrability justify tax rules that depart from theoretically accurate measurement of income and ability to pay?
themes.definition: This question considers whether simplicity, enforceability, privacy, and compliance costs warrant sacrificing precision in tax liability calculations.

themes.name: Does the complexity of using the Internal Revenue Code for social and fiscal policy undermine effective and legitimate tax administration?
themes.definition: This question examines whether fragmented provisions, uncertainty, and overlapping objectives generate excessive compliance burdens and weaken public acceptance of the tax system.

themes.name: Do estate, gift, and wealth-transfer taxes effectively prevent untaxed intergenerational accumulation without imposing unjustified burdens?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether transfer-tax structures adequately address inherited wealth and unrealized appreciation while remaining fair, coherent, and administrable.

themes.name: How should tax expenditures for saving, retirement, housing, and investment be distributed across income groups?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether targeted subsidies deliver their intended benefits or disproportionately reward high-income taxpayers and reinforce existing wealth disparities.

themes.name: Should the federal income tax retain its traditional income base, or shift toward a broad-based consumption or flat tax?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether replacing or substantially restructuring the income-tax base would improve revenue, efficiency, simplicity, and distributional fairness.

themes.name: Should economically valuable but unrealized or noncash gains be taxed before realization?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the realization principle and related exclusions appropriately defer or exclude receipts, appreciation, recoveries, and other noncash economic benefits from taxation.

themes.name: Do tax deductions, exclusions, credits, and subsidies achieve their stated policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether preferential tax provisions change behavior or deliver intended social benefits rather than subsidizing activities that would occur without them.

themes.name: Should tax preferences be treated as subsidies subject to the same scrutiny as direct government spending?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether special exclusions, deductions, credits, and other tax expenditures should be justified, measured, and limited as expenditure-like interventions.

themes.name: Do tax preferences distribute benefits inequitably because higher-income taxpayers are better able to use them?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether differences in wealth, resources, and legal access make tax-favored provisions disproportionately valuable to affluent taxpayers.

themes.name: How progressive should taxation be if redistribution may conflict with liberty, efficiency, or economic growth?
themes.definition: This question addresses the appropriate degree and structure of graduated taxation and whether progressive rates can reduce inequality without imposing unacceptable economic or political costs.

themes.name: Should tax policy be evaluated by effective system-wide burdens rather than statutory rates or individual provisions?
themes.definition: This question examines whether distributive fairness is better measured through the combined incidence of taxes, credits, transfers, and household circumstances than through isolated formal rules.

themes.name: Do tax rules create economically inefficient incentives that outweigh their equity or social-policy benefits?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how tax-induced changes in saving, investment, work, consumption, and resource allocation affect the justification for particular tax policies.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow substantive economic benefit rather than formal legal ownership, rights, or classifications?
themes.definition: This question examines whether legal categories accurately identify who receives income or bears a tax burden when formal arrangements diverge from economic reality.

themes.name: Do rigid categorical tax classifications produce irrational or inequitable results in economically diverse transactions?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether broad, formal categories should be replaced by more integrated or context-sensitive rules for property, corporate, acquisition, and related transactions.

themes.name: When should legal tax avoidance and strategic transaction structuring be respected, and when should it be curtailed?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the normative and legal status of tax planning, estate structures, and other arrangements designed to obtain favorable treatment without overtly violating statutory rules.

themes.name: Can anti-avoidance and enforcement rules prevent abuse without imposing unjustified costs on compliant taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question examines the tradeoff between protecting the public fisc and preserving certainty, administrability, and fair treatment for taxpayers who follow the law.

themes.name: Should marriage, family form, and dependent-support responsibilities determine eligibility for tax benefits?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether family-based tax rules fairly account for household structure, caregiving, dependents, and legally recognized or nonmarital partnerships.

themes.name: Should inherited wealth be taxed differently from earned wealth?
themes.definition: This question examines the normative and distributional justification for distinguishing transfers at death or within families from income generated through labor or individual enterprise.

themes.name: Are wealth-transfer taxes adequately designed to tax substantial transfers without undermining family businesses and legitimate succession planning?
themes.definition: This question addresses the treatment of closely held businesses, estate-planning structures, marital transfers, and other large transfers under gift and estate taxes.

themes.name: Do tax accounting and timing rules accurately reflect economic income across tax years?
themes.definition: This question evaluates recognition timing, deductions, recoveries, accounting periods, and cross-period transactions that may defer, accelerate, or distort taxable income.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for saving and retirement produce equitable and sustainable outcomes?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether retirement and savings incentives improve long-term financial security and social welfare or primarily benefit taxpayers who already have substantial resources.

themes.name: Can the tax-and-transfer system reduce poverty and inequality more effectively than taxation alone?
themes.definition: This question investigates how tax credits, government benefits, and complementary non-tax programs should be combined to allocate resources to economically vulnerable individuals and households.

themes.name: How should tax administration balance enforcement, taxpayer assistance, simplicity, and accurate substantive treatment?
themes.definition: This question examines the design of reporting duties, penalties, record keeping, IRS assistance, and simplified rules when administrative feasibility conflicts with fairness or abuse prevention.

themes.name: Do political, institutional, and interest-group pressures cause tax legislation to diverge from its stated purposes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how concentrated wealth, expert communities, public rhetoric, congressional choices, and administrative responses shape the design and legitimacy of federal tax policy.

themes.name: Should tax law follow the economic substance of a transaction rather than its formal legal structure?
themes.definition: This question examines whether legal characterization, ownership form, or transaction labels should yield when they produce tax outcomes inconsistent with the transaction's underlying economic substance.

themes.name: Is realization-based income taxation inadequate for taxing appreciation in financial and investment assets?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax recognition should occur before sale or another realization event when asset values have increased but the taxpayer has not received cash.

themes.name: Should the federal income-tax base be broadened to reduce deferral, avoidance, and untaxed appreciation?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether structural changes to the income-tax base should limit exclusions, timing strategies, and other mechanisms that allow income or gains to escape taxation.

themes.name: Should estate and gift taxation be strengthened to limit dynastic wealth accumulation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether transfer taxes should impose greater burdens on inherited wealth, broaden their base, or modify exemptions and deductions to reduce wealth concentration.

themes.name: How should the income tax and transfer taxes coordinate when inherited property contains unrealized gains?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether wealth transferred at death or by gift should receive carryover basis, stepped-up basis, income-tax recognition, or another coordinated treatment.

themes.name: Should federal income taxation become more progressive to reduce wealth and income inequality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether higher-income taxpayers should bear a larger share of federal tax burdens as a means of redistributing resources and reducing economic inequality.

themes.name: Can tax policy redistribute wealth without producing unacceptable effects on saving, investment, work, or consumption?
themes.definition: This question examines the tradeoff between equality-oriented taxation and the incentive or efficiency consequences of progressive rates and wealth-related tax reforms.

themes.name: Do deductions, exemptions, and credits distribute tax benefits according to ability to pay?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether the structure of tax preferences produces equitable outcomes across taxpayers with different incomes and economic capacities.

themes.name: Do tax expenditures achieve their intended behavioral and distributive objectives better than direct government spending?
themes.definition: This question compares tax-based subsidies and preferences with direct public programs in terms of effectiveness, targeting, administrative cost, and distributional consequences.

themes.name: Should tax preferences be limited when their benefits primarily accrue to affluent taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether unequal access to deductions, exclusions, and other tax advantages justifies statutory limits or restructuring of those preferences.

themes.name: Can targeted tax credits and transfers protect economically insecure households without creating inequitable household distinctions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the design of cash assistance, refundable credits, and related benefits for low-income, disabled, or otherwise economically vulnerable populations.

themes.name: Should tax policy account for earning potential and human capital rather than only realized market income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether ability-to-pay analysis should consider education, training, earning capacity, or other forms of human capital in addition to current income.

themes.name: Does married-couple income-tax filing unfairly burden second earners and shape family decisions?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether joint filing, marital deductions, and related rate structures create gendered or otherwise inequitable incentives affecting marriage and labor-market participation.

themes.name: Should similarly situated taxpayers receive comparable tax treatment despite differences in family status, location, or property-law classification?
themes.definition: This question concerns horizontal equity and whether formal household, jurisdictional, or ownership categories produce unjustified differences among taxpayers with similar economic resources.

themes.name: How should tax law balance administrability and enforcement costs against substantive equity and neutrality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether simplifying rules, limiting classifications, or accepting rough proxies is justified when more precise taxation would impose substantial administrative and compliance burdens.

themes.name: Does tax-system complexity impose disproportionate compliance burdens on less-affluent taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question examines whether technical rules, specialized benefits, and difficult filing requirements systematically disadvantage taxpayers with fewer resources for tax planning and professional advice.

themes.name: Should taxpayer planning and structured transactions be restricted when they exploit gaps between formal rules and policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the appropriate scope of anti-avoidance doctrines, statutory barriers, and IRS enforcement against legal arrangements designed to reduce or defer tax.

themes.name: Do political institutions and special-interest pressures produce tax provisions that are inefficient or inconsistent with stated policy goals?
themes.definition: This question investigates how legislative bargaining, private lobbying, and political feasibility explain the persistence or expansion of fragmented tax preferences.

themes.name: Does perceived unfairness or opacity undermine public trust and voluntary compliance with the tax system?
themes.definition: This question examines how public attitudes, transparency, and perceptions of unequal treatment affect the legitimacy of taxation and taxpayer behavior.

themes.name: Should federal tax authority be used to pursue social-policy objectives beyond revenue collection?
themes.definition: This question assesses the legitimacy and limits of using the Internal Revenue Code to influence education, philanthropy, family support, economic behavior, or other social outcomes.

themes.name: Should the federal income-tax base include economically valuable receipts that are excluded or deferred under specialized statutory provisions?
themes.definition: This question examines whether exclusions, deferrals, and favorable treatment for particular forms of compensation, investment returns, or financial receipts accurately reflect taxpayers’ economic income.

themes.name: Should wages contributed to savings or retirement accounts be taxed when earned rather than when withdrawn?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the timing and distributional consequences of taxing employment income placed in retirement or savings vehicles.

themes.name: Does the income tax measure economic income more fairly than a personal-consumption tax?
themes.definition: This question compares income- and consumption-based tax bases as alternative ways to measure taxpayers’ resources, saving, and ability to pay.

themes.name: Should returns to human capital receive different tax treatment from returns to financial capital?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether wages, compensation, investment income, and other returns should be distinguished when defining and taxing income.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for wealth and capital disproportionately benefit high-income taxpayers and increase inequality?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether preferential treatment of capital gains, wealth accumulation, deductions, or other capital-related items produces regressive distributional effects.

themes.name: Should wealth taxation be expanded to reduce intergenerational wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether taxes on accumulated wealth, transfers, or affluent taxpayers are justified as instruments of distributive equality.

themes.name: Do estate and gift-tax rules adequately prevent wealthy taxpayers from shifting wealth across generations without effective taxation?
themes.definition: This question examines whether transfer-tax bases, valuation rules, and planning strategies preserve the effectiveness of taxation at lifetime transfers and death.

themes.name: Should tax basis and recognition rules account for pre-transfer appreciation and accumulated investment when property or income rights change hands?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether tax liability should follow the underlying economic gain rather than the formal timing, form, or legal characterization of a transfer.

themes.name: Do tax rules governing business acquisitions and affiliated-corporation transactions create unjustified economic distortions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether related-party transactions, acquisitions, and dispositions receive tax benefits despite producing little or no corresponding change in economic value.

themes.name: Can tax incentives effectively promote socially desirable behavior without creating regressive or counterproductive effects?
themes.definition: This question tests whether deductions, credits, exclusions, and other preferences achieve their intended behavioral objectives while avoiding abuse and unequal benefits.

themes.name: Should tax policy be used to pursue social-policy goals that could instead be addressed through direct spending or regulation?
themes.definition: This question compares tax expenditures with direct government interventions, focusing on effectiveness, transparency, distribution, and administrative feasibility.

themes.name: Do tax benefits and eligibility rules impose disproportionate burdens on economically vulnerable households?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax-and-transfer programs unintentionally deepen poverty, stigmatize need, or fail to provide socially adequate support.

themes.name: Does the tax treatment of marriage and family structure produce equitable outcomes for households with different arrangements?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether joint filing, spousal treatment, household-based benefits, and family-related provisions fairly reflect economic relationships and gendered consequences.

themes.name: Should tax rules recognize substantive economic relationships when formal legal status does not reflect the parties’ actual financial arrangements?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether legal tax categories should yield to underlying property, family, compensation, or economic relationships.

themes.name: Do formally neutral tax rules create unequal burdens for disadvantaged or differently situated taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether facially uniform rules produce disparate distributional effects because taxpayers differ in income, household structure, gender, race, or economic vulnerability.

themes.name: Can tax reform reconcile progressive distribution with economic efficiency and administrative simplicity?
themes.definition: This question evaluates competing tax designs according to their effects on equity, incentives, neutrality, compliance costs, and administrability.

themes.name: Do specialized tax rules create excessive complexity and opportunities for avoidance compared with simpler alternatives?
themes.definition: This question examines whether detailed exceptions, flexible standards, and targeted provisions undermine coherent administration and permit taxpayers to reduce liability through structured transactions.

themes.name: Should tax law rely on fixed rules or flexible standards when formal categories produce economically distorted outcomes?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether context-sensitive interpretation better protects tax equity and economic substance than rigid statutory classifications.

themes.name: Do existing tax doctrines and administrative interpretations implement legislative objectives consistently and predictably?
themes.definition: This question examines whether statutory ambiguity, judicial interpretation, enforcement practices, and administrative design create uncertainty or undermine the intended operation of tax programs.

themes.name: Is politically durable tax reform possible when entrenched deductions and competing institutional interests resist broader redistribution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the public justification, political feasibility, and institutional constraints surrounding major reforms to progressive taxation and longstanding tax preferences.

themes.name: Should the income-tax base include unrealized appreciation rather than relying primarily on realization events?
themes.definition: This question examines whether realization-based taxation of capital gains, basis, and recognition rules creates inequities, deferral opportunities, or economically inaccurate measures of income.

themes.name: Do preferential tax rules for capital income unfairly benefit affluent taxpayers and intensify wealth inequality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the distributional effects of preferential rates, exclusions, and other special treatment for capital gains, investment income, and accumulated wealth.

themes.name: Do deductions, exclusions, and other tax preferences erode the tax base more than they advance their stated policy goals?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether targeted tax benefits produce sufficient social or economic benefits to justify lost revenue, unequal treatment, and opportunities for tax planning.
