themes.name: Does realization-based taxation of capital gains and property transfers create sufficiently serious inequities and distortions to warrant reform?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether taxing capital and property only upon realization improperly defers taxation, encourages inefficient timing, and fails to capture economic gains.

themes.name: Should savings and investment returns be taxed under an income-tax model or a consumption-tax model?
themes.definition: This question compares the equity, efficiency, and administrative consequences of taxing returns on saving as income versus exempting or otherwise deferring them under consumption-based approaches.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation effectively reduce the concentration of income and wealth without unacceptable economic or political costs?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether higher tax burdens on affluent and super-rich taxpayers achieve meaningful redistribution while preserving incentives, legitimacy, and feasible administration.

themes.name: Should tax burdens reflect taxpayers' differing needs and economic circumstances beyond their measured income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether ability-to-pay principles justify adjustments for family responsibilities, health costs, unequal resources, or other forms of heterogeneous taxpayer circumstance.

themes.name: Are deductions, exclusions, and credits equitable instruments for delivering tax relief and pursuing public policy?
themes.definition: This question compares the distributional and behavioral effects of major forms of tax relief, including whether credits are preferable to deductions for achieving stated objectives.

themes.name: Should tax law recognize family relationships according to actual economic interdependence rather than formal or traditional legal categories?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether rules concerning children, spouses, divorce, and household expenditures produce justified outcomes when family arrangements do not fit conventional classifications.

themes.name: Does the federal estate and wealth-transfer tax system effectively limit intergenerational concentration of wealth?
themes.definition: This question assesses the design, valuation rules, avoidance opportunities, and political constraints affecting taxation of property transfers and accumulated wealth.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for wealthy taxpayers undermine distributive fairness and the goals of progressive taxation?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether preferential treatment of capital, savings, transfers, or other investments disproportionately benefits high-income and high-wealth taxpayers.

themes.name: Should tax preferences be used to pursue social-policy goals such as philanthropy, nonprofit activity, or private welfare provision?
themes.definition: This question examines whether subsidizing socially valued private conduct through the tax code is more justified or effective than relying on direct government programs.

themes.name: Do tax-based benefits for low-income households adequately advance social-welfare objectives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether credits, exclusions, and related tax programs protect vulnerable beneficiaries and distribute support effectively across income groups.

themes.name: Do tax rules governing healthcare expenditures improve affordability without creating unjustified inequalities or behavioral distortions?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether tax treatment of health-related spending and insurance advances access to care while remaining administrable and distributionally defensible.

themes.name: Does the tax system appropriately classify compensation and income earned by nontraditional workers?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax rules for independent contractors, contingent workers, and restructured compensation accurately reflect their economic position and allocate burdens fairly.

themes.name: Should substantive economic substance prevail over formal labels when determining the tax treatment of transactions and payments?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether courts and tax authorities should recharacterize formally distinct transactions when their economic effects are equivalent or designed to shift income.

themes.name: Do tax-planning and income-shifting opportunities undermine the objectives of progressive taxation?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether taxpayers can exploit related-party arrangements, compensation structures, legal classifications, or timing rules to reduce liabilities in ways that defeat policy goals.

themes.name: Do the complexity and nonuniformity of federal tax rules undermine compliance, administration, and substantive fairness?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether intricate deductions, special regimes, valuation rules, and inconsistent applications impose costs that outweigh their regulatory or distributive benefits.

themes.name: Should economically similar financial arrangements receive harmonized tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question asks whether divergent treatment of comparable investments, obligations, or transaction stages creates unjustified distortions and unequal burdens.

themes.name: How should statutory interpretation and administrative practice resolve disputed inclusions and exclusions from taxable income?
themes.definition: This question examines the respective roles of statutory text, formal definitions, IRS rulings, judicial decisions, and broader tax-policy principles in determining the practical meaning of income-tax provisions.

themes.name: Are constitutional and historical limits on federal taxation consistent with contemporary redistribution and wealth-tax objectives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legal legitimacy and boundaries of federal authority to tax income, transfers, and private property for purposes extending beyond revenue collection.

themes.name: Can politically feasible tax reforms correct entrenched inequities without reproducing the path dependencies of existing tax institutions?
themes.definition: This question investigates how concentrated interests, institutional rules, historical development, and legitimacy concerns shape the adoption and durability of tax reform.

themes.name: Should structural complexity in the federal income-tax code be reduced through simplification or fundamental redesign?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the complexity, specialized assistance, litigation, and administrative burdens created by existing income-tax rules justify simplification or replacement with an alternative structure.

themes.name: Should tax burdens be allocated according to taxpayers’ ability to pay rather than formal legal categories?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether purchasing power, welfare, economic resources, and ability to pay provide a more equitable basis for taxation than formal classifications of taxpayers or transactions.

themes.name: Does progressive taxation of high-income and wealthy taxpayers appropriately reduce inequality without imposing excessive efficiency costs?
themes.definition: This question assesses the distributive justification for progressive rates and wealth-related taxation against possible effects on incentives, resource allocation, and economic performance.

themes.name: Should capital appreciation and investment returns be taxed more consistently with economic income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether preferential treatment, realization requirements, deferral, and capital-income exclusions allow returns to private wealth to escape taxation that would apply under a comprehensive income concept.

themes.name: Does the step-up-in-basis rule at death enable wealthy taxpayers to avoid capital-gains taxation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether eliminating or modifying the basis adjustment for inherited appreciated assets is necessary to prevent the permanent exclusion of unrealized gains from the tax base.

themes.name: How should the timing of income and expense recognition reflect economic income from multi-period investments?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether realization, deferral, and other timing rules accurately measure income over time while accounting for investment duration and the time value of money.

themes.name: Do gift- and estate-tax rules effectively prevent wealth-transfer tax avoidance and wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether exemptions, valuation strategies, property transfers, and interactions between the gift and estate taxes preserve the transfer-tax base and reduce concentrated inherited wealth.

themes.name: Should the tax treatment of married couples rely on marriage and state property-law classifications?
themes.definition: This question examines whether joint treatment, marital deductions, assignment of property, and differences between common-law and community-property regimes produce justified or inequitable outcomes.

themes.name: Does the income-tax definition of the individual tax base distinguish coherently between taxable receipts, savings, capital recovery, and personal expenditures?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether conventional income concepts adequately identify which economic receipts should be included and which amounts represent non-taxable savings, investment, or return of capital.

themes.name: How should federal income-tax law treat personal-injury damages and other litigation-related recoveries?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the tax treatment of damages, attorney fees, and contingent-fee arrangements properly characterizes recoveries and allows injured taxpayers to be made whole.

themes.name: Do formal tax classifications accurately reflect the economic substance of complex transactions and service arrangements?
themes.definition: This question examines whether legal characterization, contractual form, and statutory categories produce tax outcomes consistent with the real economic relationships and burdens involved.

themes.name: Do tax preferences and exclusions achieve their stated social or economic objectives without unjustified erosion of the tax base?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether deductions, exclusions, credits, deferrals, and other tax expenditures produce intended benefits rather than costly, regressive, or ineffective subsidies.

themes.name: Should tax preferences be limited when they disproportionately benefit high-income taxpayers or particular forms of saving and investment?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether formally available preferences should be constrained or made more neutral to prevent unequal advantages based on income, compensation, asset type, or investment form.

themes.name: Can tax subsidies for families, essential goods, or social welfare deliver benefits to the people who most need them?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether targeted tax relief and subsidy programs reach resource-constrained households while balancing equity, revenue, administrative feasibility, and broader policy goals.

themes.name: Do tax rules and public benefit programs create harmful work disincentives or improve labor-market participation?
themes.definition: This question examines how taxes, credits, compensation rules, and interacting benefit programs affect employment decisions, labor supply, and economic performance.

themes.name: Can the earned income tax credit expand legitimate access while limiting improper claims and administrative error?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how EITC eligibility and enforcement should balance support for low-income workers against fraud prevention, compliance costs, and the protection of vulnerable taxpayers.

themes.name: Should income taxation or consumption taxation govern the treatment of saving and investment?
themes.definition: This question compares comprehensive income, consumption-oriented, and hybrid tax designs in terms of neutrality, distribution, capital accumulation, and the treatment of saving.

themes.name: Do anti-avoidance and income-timing doctrines prevent abusive tax planning without creating excessive distortion and uncertainty?
themes.definition: This question examines whether taxpayers can exploit gaps, mismatches, transaction structures, or timing rules and whether corrective doctrines impose greater costs than the abuses they address.

themes.name: How should tax administration balance consistent enforcement with equitable treatment of vulnerable taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether enforcement regimes, administrative guidance, and judicial doctrines protect revenue and uniformity without imposing disproportionate burdens or legally problematic disparities.

themes.name: Are federal tax policies constitutionally and democratically legitimate when they redistribute wealth or pursue non-revenue social objectives?
themes.definition: This question examines the constitutional limits, public legitimacy, political acceptance, and normative justification of using federal taxation to allocate social burdens, benefits, and economic power.

themes.name: Should progressive tax rates replace flat-rate taxation to reduce inequality without unacceptable efficiency or compliance costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the distributive, behavioral, administrative, and political consequences of progressive versus flat-rate tax structures.

themes.name: Should the federal tax system deliver social-welfare benefits, or should those benefits be provided through separate spending programs?
themes.definition: This question compares tax-based benefits for low-income households and families with direct cash or in-kind welfare programs.

themes.name: Do tax preferences and exclusions effectively achieve their intended social-policy goals?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether targeted tax subsidies produce measurable benefits for their intended beneficiaries rather than merely reducing revenue or reallocating existing activity.

themes.name: Can tax reform simplify compliance and administration without sacrificing accurate treatment of taxpayers’ economic circumstances?
themes.definition: This question concerns the tradeoff between precise, individualized tax rules and standardized rules that taxpayers and the IRS can realistically administer.

themes.name: Should the United States replace or supplement its income tax with consumption- or wealth-based taxation?
themes.definition: This question compares alternative tax bases in terms of equity, efficiency, revenue, savings, and the treatment of capital income.

themes.name: Should unrealized appreciation and other difficult-to-value gains be taxed before realization?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether mark-to-market or current-assessment systems should replace or supplement realization-based income taxation.

themes.name: Should estate and inheritance taxation be strengthened to limit the intergenerational concentration of wealth and political power?
themes.definition: This question examines the historical, distributive, administrative, and behavioral case for taxing transfers of wealth at death.

themes.name: Does taxation of marriage and family units unfairly favor some household structures over others?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether joint filing, marriage recognition, and family-based tax rules distribute burdens and benefits equitably among married, unmarried, and single-parent households.

themes.name: Should tax liability depend on the economic substance of a transaction rather than its formal legal characterization?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether economically equivalent transactions, property interests, and contractual arrangements should receive comparable tax treatment despite different legal forms.

themes.name: How should tax rules account for illiquid privately held businesses and other noncash assets?
themes.definition: This question examines valuation, liquidity, timing, and payment problems that arise when taxpayers hold wealth that cannot readily be converted into cash.

themes.name: Do preferential tax rules for saving and investment promote productive accumulation more than they create inefficient or regressive subsidies?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the distributional and behavioral effects of tax-favored savings vehicles, investments, and wealth transfers.

themes.name: How should taxation of employment-related compensation account for timing, contingencies, and changes in the form of compensation?
themes.definition: This question concerns when and how wages, deferred compensation, equity compensation, and other employment-related benefits should be included in taxable income.

themes.name: Should state-law classifications of property and family relationships control federal tax consequences?
themes.definition: This question examines the conflict between uniform federal tax rules and legally diverse state definitions of ownership, marital status, and property rights.

themes.name: How should courts, Congress, and the IRS divide responsibility for resolving ambiguous or novel tax questions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates institutional authority, judicial interpretation, administrative enforcement, and uncertainty in the development of federal tax law.

themes.name: Do formally neutral tax rules produce unequal burdens for taxpayers who are economically or legally dissimilar?
themes.definition: This question tests whether equal-treatment categories and facially neutral rules adequately capture differences in economic circumstances, vulnerability, and social status.

themes.name: Should ability to pay justify greater tax burdens on wealthy taxpayers even when those burdens affect incentives and economic liberty?
themes.definition: This question addresses the moral, constitutional, political, and economic justification for redistributive taxation of high-income and high-wealth individuals.

themes.name: Do structural features of the tax code enable tax avoidance by exploiting gaps between legally distinct forms or moments of taxation?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether taxpayers can reduce liabilities through mismatches involving entity form, realization, basis, timing, transfer rules, or different tax regimes.

themes.name: Do tax incentives change private economic behavior in ways that undermine their revenue, efficiency, or distributional objectives?
themes.definition: This question examines strategic taxpayer responses and unintended effects of incentives on saving, labor, investment, compensation, and transaction structure.

themes.name: Should taxes and transfers be evaluated as one integrated system for reducing inequality and improving economic security?
themes.definition: This question assesses the combined incidence and incentive effects of taxes, refundable credits, cash benefits, and in-kind support rather than analyzing them separately.

themes.name: Does the existing income-tax framework require structural redesign rather than incremental amendments?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether fragmented provisions, loopholes, inconsistent classifications, and recurring policy failures can be corrected through targeted fixes or require comprehensive reform.

themes.name: Should unrealized appreciation be taxed as it accrues rather than only when an asset is sold?
themes.definition: This question examines whether realization-based income taxation fairly measures gains in wealth or instead creates unjustified deferral and inequity.

themes.name: Do conventional income-tax concepts adequately distinguish labor income, capital returns, and conversions of existing wealth?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the income tax correctly characterizes economic gains arising from work, investment, property dispositions, and accumulated capital.

themes.name: Should wealth transfers be taxed more heavily to limit intergenerational concentration of wealth?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether estate, gift, and inheritance taxes can fairly address inherited economic advantage without imposing excessive administrative or economic costs.

themes.name: Are estate- and gift-tax rules effective against trusts and other arrangements that shift wealth across generations?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether family wealth-holding structures and planning techniques undermine the intended reach of transfer taxes.

themes.name: Should tax law treat spouses and other intimate relationships as unified economic units?
themes.definition: This question examines whether income allocation, filing rules, and transfers within families should reflect relationship-based economic sharing or preserve individual autonomy.

themes.name: Are tax rules governing divorce and transfers between family members substantively fair?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the tax treatment of property settlements, support, and family-provided benefits reflects the parties’ actual economic circumstances.

themes.name: Do tax-based benefits effectively improve economic security for low-income households?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether credits, deductions, and related fiscal programs reduce poverty and support work without excluding or burdening vulnerable taxpayers.

themes.name: Do tax subsidies for personal needs distribute benefits equitably across income groups?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deductions and credits for housing, caregiving, health, education, or similar needs provide comparable assistance to differently situated taxpayers.

themes.name: Does progressive taxation reduce wealth inequality without producing unacceptable economic distortions?
themes.definition: This question tests the distributive and behavioral consequences of progressive rates, exemptions, and other mechanisms intended to redistribute income and wealth.

themes.name: Should the tax system explicitly limit the concentration and transmission of large fortunes?
themes.definition: This question considers whether taxation should pursue equality of opportunity and restrain socioeconomic immobility in addition to raising revenue.

themes.name: Would a consumption-based tax be fairer or more efficient than the current income-tax model?
themes.definition: This question compares income, consumption, and sales-tax bases with respect to saving, investment, distribution, administration, and economic behavior.

themes.name: Can a federal wealth tax supplement or replace income taxation without violating property and administrability principles?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the normative, constitutional, valuation, and practical feasibility of taxing accumulated holdings directly.

themes.name: Are targeted tax preferences effective tools for achieving social-policy goals?
themes.definition: This question examines whether exclusions, deductions, credits, and preferential rates accomplish their stated objectives better than direct spending or general tax rules.

themes.name: Do tax preferences create avoidance opportunities and unequal treatment among economically similar taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether statutory exceptions and selective benefits undermine neutrality, fairness, or the integrity of the tax base.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow economic substance rather than formal legal characterization?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether mixed transactions, noncash consideration, and legally equivalent payments should receive the same tax treatment despite differing labels.

themes.name: Do anti-avoidance rules prevent abusive planning without creating new distortions or arbitrary burdens?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether anti-circumvention doctrines and mandatory substitute rules strike an appropriate balance between enforcement and economic neutrality.

themes.name: Can tax rules measure and value complex economic benefits accurately enough to support fair taxation?
themes.definition: This question examines valuation, fair-market-value, timing, and accounting problems involving noncash benefits, personal-injury recoveries, and unusual wealth transfers.

themes.name: Can tax-system simplification improve compliance and legitimacy without sacrificing fairness or creating new complexity?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tradeoffs among administrability, transparency, taxpayer understanding, precise targeting, and substantive equity.

themes.name: Do retirement-tax incentives produce equitable and meaningful benefits for differently situated taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether retirement deductions, exclusions, and savings vehicles effectively encourage retirement saving or disproportionately reward higher-income households.

themes.name: Should constitutional limits constrain tax classifications and reforms aimed at reducing economic inequality?
themes.definition: This question examines congressional taxing authority, equal-protection principles, and other constitutional doctrines governing differentiated or redistributive tax burdens.

themes.name: Should the income-tax base include wealth increases and other economic benefits that are not conventionally realized as income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether taxable income should extend beyond current receipts to include unrealized appreciation, imputed benefits, and other wealth-like gains.

themes.name: Does the realization requirement cause the income tax to understate or inequitably defer taxation of capital gains?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether taxing gains only upon sale or another realization event fairly captures returns from capital and business assets.

themes.name: Should inherited wealth and lifetime gifts receive comparable tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question considers whether differences between transfers made during life and transfers at death create unjustified opportunities for wealth-transfer tax avoidance.

themes.name: Does preferential taxation of capital and investment income undermine equitable treatment of labor and business income?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether lower rates, exclusions, or deferral for capital income produce defensible economic and distributional outcomes.

themes.name: Is an income tax preferable to consumption-, wealth-, or wealth-transfer taxation for achieving both revenue and distributional objectives?
themes.definition: This question compares alternative tax bases according to their effects on equity, efficiency, administration, saving, and wealth concentration.

themes.name: Do tax credits, deductions, and exclusions effectively promote the social behaviors or policy goals for which they were enacted?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax expenditures are superior to direct regulation or spending programs in achieving specified social and economic objectives.

themes.name: Do targeted tax benefits reach their intended beneficiaries, or do they disproportionately reward taxpayers with greater resources?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether the actual incidence of tax subsidies differs from their stated distributional or social-policy purpose.

themes.name: Can tax-based safety-net programs support low-income households without creating excessive labor-supply disincentives?
themes.definition: This question examines the tradeoff between income support, work incentives, phaseouts, and the effectiveness of tax-based anti-poverty programs.

themes.name: Do family, marriage, and divorce rules distribute tax burdens fairly among household members and household types?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether tax classifications of spouses, dependents, support payments, and family resources reflect actual economic relationships rather than traditional family assumptions.

themes.name: Should the tax system provide distinct treatment for disability-related costs and substantial caregiving needs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether ordinary tax rules adequately account for the unequal financial burdens faced by people with disabilities and their caregivers.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation be maintained when taxpayers can shift, defer, exclude, or strategically characterize income?
themes.definition: This question studies whether avoidance opportunities and anti-circumvention rules erode progressivity or create new economic distortions.

themes.name: Should tax administration favor clear and stable rules over theoretically precise standards that impose substantial valuation and compliance costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tradeoff between doctrinal precision, taxpayer fairness, administrative feasibility, and uncertainty in applying tax law.

themes.name: Do depreciation, interest, deduction-timing, and matching rules accurately measure business income without distorting investment decisions?
themes.definition: This question examines whether rules governing business assets, financing costs, and the timing of deductions produce economically coherent tax results.

themes.name: Do tax rules change private economic behavior in ways that reduce rather than enhance efficiency or social welfare?
themes.definition: This question investigates behavioral responses such as altered saving, investment, transaction structure, compensation, and the choice of tax-favored products.

themes.name: Do formally neutral tax rules produce substantively unequal burdens across economic classes and similarly situated taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question compares legal classifications and nominal tax rates with the actual incidence of taxes, deductions, benefits, and compliance burdens.

themes.name: How should tax policy balance distributive justice against efficiency, liberty, neutrality, and administrative cost?
themes.definition: This question tests competing normative frameworks for deciding when unequal taxation or behavioral intervention is justified.

themes.name: Should courts resolve inequities in tax statutes through purposive interpretation, or should correction remain primarily with Congress?
themes.definition: This question examines the institutional boundary between judicial interpretation, statutory text, congressional purpose, and legislative tax reform.

themes.name: Do constitutional concepts of income and direct taxation constrain modern efforts to tax wealth, capital gains, or unconventional receipts?
themes.definition: This question analyzes how constitutional doctrines shape the permissible tax base and the classification of federal exactions.

themes.name: Can entrenched federal tax systems be reformed incrementally without sacrificing their core principles or distributive objectives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the political, fiscal, administrative, and institutional feasibility of structural reform compared with targeted amendments or replacement.

themes.name: Does globalization require domestic tax law to change its treatment of multinational activity and cross-border income?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether international economic activity undermines existing domestic tax rules, revenue collection, or equitable allocation of taxing authority.

themes.name: Should the federal income tax remain progressive in order to reduce inequality, even at the risk of weakening economic efficiency?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether graduated income taxation can achieve meaningful redistribution and fiscal equity without producing unacceptable effects on work, investment, or economic growth.

themes.name: Would replacing or supplementing the income tax with a consumption-based tax produce a fairer and more administrable tax system?
themes.definition: This question compares income- and consumption-tax bases with respect to progressivity, economic incentives, revenue, simplicity, and administrative feasibility.

themes.name: Should taxable income be measured by broader economic accretion rather than by currently realized or formally received income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether unrealized gains, noncash benefits, and other economically valuable increases in wealth should be included in the tax base.

themes.name: Do timing rules and deductions for costs of producing future income create unjustified differences in effective tax burdens?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether the timing of income recognition and recovery of income-producing expenses accurately measures economic income and treats similarly situated taxpayers equally.

themes.name: Are deductions, exclusions, and preferential rates for savings and investment justified by their effects on equity, efficiency, and revenue?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax preferences for capital income and investment generate sufficient economic benefits to justify their distributional and fiscal costs.

themes.name: Should gift and estate taxation be strengthened to limit the inequality-producing effects of inherited wealth?
themes.definition: This question examines whether wealth-transfer taxes are an appropriate and effective instrument for addressing concentrated family wealth, ability to pay, and intergenerational inequality.

themes.name: Do refundable tax credits, especially the Earned Income Tax Credit, reduce poverty without creating undesirable work or compliance incentives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the distributional effects, labor-supply consequences, and administrative performance of refundable credits for low-income workers and households.

themes.name: Should income-support programs delivered through the tax system replace or be coordinated more closely with traditional welfare benefits?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether tax-based transfers can provide economic security more effectively and equitably than fragmented welfare programs.

themes.name: Does joint taxation of married couples fairly reflect shared household resources and differing spousal contributions?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether marital filing rules and marital-property arrangements allocate tax burdens appropriately between spouses and across household types.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for traditional family structures reproduce gendered or heteronormative economic inequality?
themes.definition: This question examines whether family-based tax rules distribute benefits according to outdated assumptions about marriage, caregiving, dependency, and household organization.

themes.name: Should personal-injury damages and other bodily-injury compensation be excluded from income uniformly or differentiated by the type of loss compensated?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the scope and justification of exclusions for personal-injury recoveries, including distinctions among physical injury, emotional harm, punitive damages, and replacement of lost income.

themes.name: Should noncash consideration and disputed financial interests be taxed according to fair market value or according to formal receipt and legal ownership?
themes.definition: This question examines when tax liability should follow the economic value of property or an interest rather than the transaction’s formal legal characterization.

themes.name: Can anti-abuse rules prevent tax-motivated restructuring without denying legitimate deductions or commercial transactions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether substance-over-form doctrines, categorical tests, and anti-manipulation provisions correctly distinguish abusive arrangements from genuine business activity.

themes.name: Do formal tax classifications produce inequitable results when they diverge from the economic substance of a transaction?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether distinctions based on legal form, source, organizational type, or category of payment create arbitrary differences in tax liability.

themes.name: Do targeted tax incentives actually achieve their stated behavioral, family, social, or economic objectives?
themes.definition: This question tests whether tax subsidies and preferences change conduct or improve social outcomes sufficiently to justify their complexity, revenue loss, and distributional effects.

themes.name: Can tax-based benefit rules be simplified without sacrificing fairness, targeting, and the policy objectives they are intended to serve?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether fragmented and overlapping credits, deductions, exclusions, and eligibility rules should be replaced by a more uniform structure.

themes.name: Should tax liability be based more directly on actual economic capacity rather than observable proxies such as income, expenditures, or wealth?
themes.definition: This question examines whether current measures of ability to pay adequately capture household needs, costs, resources, and non-income forms of economic welfare.

themes.name: Do tax incentives and retirement-benefit rules allocate economic security fairly across workers, retirees, and highly compensated participants?
themes.definition: This question assesses the distributional and behavioral consequences of tax preferences and structural reforms affecting contributory retirement programs.

themes.name: How much discretion should tax administrators and courts have to adapt statutory rules to changing transactions and underlying policy purposes?
themes.definition: This question addresses the balance between formal statutory interpretation, legislative history, administrative guidance, enforcement, and flexible anti-avoidance doctrines.

themes.name: Is politically feasible incremental tax reform preferable to comprehensive reform when existing rules are inefficient, inequitable, or institutionally entrenched?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how political resistance, administrative capacity, fiscal pressures, and transitional concerns should shape the design and implementation of federal tax reform.

themes.name: Do progressive income-tax rates and distributional rules reduce inequality without imposing unacceptable efficiency costs?
themes.definition: This question examines how rate structures, deductions, exclusions, and other federal income-tax rules distribute burdens across income groups and balance redistribution against incentives and economic costs.

themes.name: Does the Earned Income Tax Credit effectively support low-income working families and reach the households most in need?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the EITC and related tax-based benefits in terms of coverage, work incentives, poverty reduction, and access for disadvantaged populations.

themes.name: Should the federal tax system target concentrated wealth through stronger wealth-transfer or wealth-based taxation?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether estate, gift, wealth, and progressive income-tax reforms should reduce entrenched wealth concentration and advance distributive justice.

themes.name: Should gift and estate taxes be unified, and do current wealth-transfer rules achieve their intended redistributive purposes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the structure, fairness, and policy coherence of inter vivos and death-time transfer taxes, including unintended consequences and opportunities for avoidance.

themes.name: Should savings and capital income receive preferential tax treatment relative to labor income?
themes.definition: This question compares income-tax and consumption-tax treatment of saving, investment returns, and capital-derived income in terms of capital formation, equity, and disparities between asset owners and workers.

themes.name: Are tax preferences for saving, investment, and other favored assets actually captured by intended beneficiaries or capitalized into asset prices?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether deductions, exclusions, credits, and favorable rates change economic behavior and returns as intended or instead accrue to asset sellers and existing owners.

themes.name: Should comprehensive economic income, rather than realization, govern the federal income-tax base?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the Haig-Simons concept of income should replace or limit realization-based taxation of unrealized appreciation, noncash benefits, and deferred gains.

themes.name: How should federal tax law classify payments and recoveries whose economic substance differs from their formal legal labels?
themes.definition: This question addresses the treatment of personal-injury damages, employment-related recoveries, litigation costs, property transfers, and other difficult-to-classify receipts or benefits.

themes.name: Do timing, basis, assignment, and allocation rules accurately match tax liability to the underlying economic event?
themes.definition: This question evaluates rules governing deferred gains, reversed compensation, recovered deductions, assignment of income, and allocation across taxable years or taxpayers.

themes.name: Are deductions and exclusions for business, investment, and personal expenses justified and equitably designed?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether expense deductions and exclusions properly measure taxable income or instead create fragmented, preferential, or distributionally inequitable outcomes.

themes.name: Do tax-favored benefits and deductions for employment and household arrangements distribute resources fairly across different types of families?
themes.definition: This question examines the distributional effects of employer-provided benefits, household benefits, and other employment-related tax provisions across taxpayers with different incomes and circumstances.

themes.name: Do marriage-based tax rules create unjustified penalties or gendered inequalities?
themes.definition: This question evaluates marriage penalties, marital dissolution rules, recognition of relationships, and tax incentives affecting gender roles and women’s economic autonomy.

themes.name: Can tax incentives and transfers effectively pursue social-policy goals beyond revenue raising?
themes.definition: This question asks whether credits, exemptions, subsidies, and tax-exempt status can achieve goals such as poverty reduction, mandated saving, benefit coverage, or organizational regulation more effectively and fairly than alternative policies.

themes.name: Do tax preferences represent defensible public policy or concealed subsidies that undermine a broad tax base?
themes.definition: This question uses tax-expenditure analysis and normative baselines to distinguish justified incentives from politically durable preferences that erode revenue, neutrality, or equity.

themes.name: Do tax rules create avoidance opportunities and distortions in otherwise comparable economic decisions?
themes.definition: This question investigates strategic tax planning, taxpayer manipulation, transactional characterization, and incentives that cause taxpayers to alter non-tax decisions or exploit gaps between specialized provisions.

themes.name: Can the income-tax system be made simpler and more administrable without sacrificing substantive fairness?
themes.definition: This question examines whether structural reform, fewer exceptions, and clearer rules can reduce compliance and enforcement costs while preserving distributional and policy objectives.

themes.name: How should uncertainty and taxpayer perceptions of tax obligations affect the design and administration of tax rules?
themes.definition: This question studies how legal ambiguity, complexity, information, psychology, and public understanding influence compliance, transaction decisions, and the legitimacy of tax-financed programs.

themes.name: Should courts and tax administrators interpret ambiguous provisions according to statutory text, formal categories, or underlying policy purposes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates historical, purposive, economic-substance, and doctrinal approaches to resolving conflicts between statutory formulations and broader tax-policy goals.

themes.name: Are federal tax rules constitutionally constrained when they impose unequal burdens or regulate state and private economic arrangements?
themes.definition: This question examines constitutional limits on federal taxing power, state-level fiscal reform, differential treatment, and fairness-based challenges to tax legislation.

themes.name: Should tax policy prioritize broad public revenue and neutral administration over politically durable concessions and targeted economic incentives?
themes.definition: This question analyzes the political and institutional tradeoffs among revenue adequacy, social-policy objectives, efficiency, distributive justice, and the durability of tax provisions.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow the economic substance of a transaction rather than its formal legal classification?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax law should characterize payments, arrangements, and transactions according to their underlying economic benefits and burdens instead of their labels or technical forms.

themes.name: Should the income-tax base include unrealized, noncash, or otherwise nontraditional increases in wealth?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether taxable income should be measured by genuine accretions to wealth, including unrealized gains and noncash benefits, rather than only by formal receipts.

themes.name: Is an income tax preferable to a consumption-based tax for promoting fairness, efficiency, and adequate revenue?
themes.definition: This question compares income, consumption, and related tax bases in light of their effects on saving, investment, distribution, administrative feasibility, and fiscal sustainability.

themes.name: Should deductions, exemptions, and credits be replaced or redesigned to distribute personal tax benefits more equitably?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether the form and availability of personal tax preferences produce defensible behavioral and distributional outcomes across taxpayers.

themes.name: Does preferential capital-gains taxation promote productive investment or mainly subsidize wealth and capital ownership?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether lower or deferred taxation of capital gains generates socially valuable investment effects sufficient to justify its distributional and revenue costs.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation of affluent taxpayers reduce inequality without imposing unacceptable efficiency and administrative costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the redistributive justification, economic effects, political feasibility, and practical limits of progressive taxation.

themes.name: Should the estate and gift tax be strengthened to limit intergenerational concentration of wealth and political power?
themes.definition: This question examines whether transfer taxation effectively reduces wealth concentration and whether anti-avoidance reforms can preserve its revenue and egalitarian objectives.

themes.name: How should property transferred at death be taxed when basis rules, estate taxation, and asset illiquidity interact?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether inherited property should receive special basis treatment or tax relief and how the system should handle noncash or privately held assets.

themes.name: Do marriage, family, and child-related tax rules allocate benefits and burdens fairly across unequal household circumstances?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the fairness, work incentives, autonomy effects, and administrative workability of using the family or household as the tax unit.

themes.name: Should tax rules treat savings, retirement contributions, and deferred compensation differently from current labor income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax preferences for saving and retirement programs are justified by investment, social-insurance, paternalistic, or distributional goals.

themes.name: How should tax law coordinate the recognition of income, deductions, losses, and interest when transactions occur at different times?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether mismatched timing creates unjustified tax advantages and whether realization, deferral, and imputed-interest rules should be revised.

themes.name: Do tax subsidies and incentives change economic behavior enough to justify their distributional and revenue costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax-favored treatment of investment, employment, saving, or other activities produces intended behavioral effects rather than inefficient distortions or benefits for already advantaged taxpayers.

themes.name: Can tax-based assistance effectively reduce poverty and protect household economic security without excessive complexity?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether tax benefits targeted at disadvantaged taxpayers reach their intended recipients and remain administrable, predictable, and fiscally sustainable.

themes.name: Do facially neutral tax rules produce racially or otherwise socially disparate economic effects?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax classifications, deductions, exemptions, and enforcement practices reproduce structural inequalities across racial, socioeconomic, or other socially differentiated groups.

themes.name: When should tax-law complexity be accepted to achieve more equitable substantive treatment?
themes.definition: This question weighs the equity gains of individualized or differentiated tax rules against uncertainty, compliance burdens, administrative costs, and reduced predictability.

themes.name: Does tax administration and enforcement determine whether formally progressive rules actually produce progressive outcomes?
themes.definition: This question studies how IRS implementation, taxpayer compliance, enforcement choices, and administrative capacity alter the real incidence of tax provisions.

themes.name: Should courts and agencies interpret ambiguous tax provisions according to legislative purpose rather than formal text or categorical precedent?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how statutory interpretation should resolve unsettled tax treatment when technical classifications conflict with the policy objectives of the legislation.

themes.name: Do tax-planning strategies exploit formal distinctions in ways that undermine the intended tax base and distribution of burdens?
themes.definition: This question investigates how taxpayers restructure compensation, assets, entities, or transactions to avoid or defer tax and whether anti-avoidance reforms are justified.

themes.name: Do narrowly framed exemptions, exclusions, and temporary tax provisions produce unintended inequities and weaken the federal tax base?
themes.definition: This question examines whether technical or temporary relief provisions fail to address their stated policy problems while creating windfalls, arbitrary distinctions, or fiscal erosion.

themes.name: Can tax reform overcome political and institutional resistance while aligning revenue, equity, and administrative objectives?
themes.definition: This question analyzes how legislative bargaining, path dependence, government legitimacy, and institutional constraints shape the adoption and practical effects of tax reform.

themes.name: Should tax expenditures such as deductions, exemptions, and exclusions be treated as government subsidies subject to the same scrutiny as direct spending?
themes.definition: This question examines whether preferential tax provisions should be evaluated as spending programs rather than merely as technical features of the tax base.

themes.name: Should unrealized capital gains be taxed as they accrue, or only when the underlying asset is sold or otherwise realized?
themes.definition: This question addresses the conflict between comprehensive accretion-based taxation and realization-based rules for capital income.

themes.name: Should a comprehensive income-tax base replace deductions and exclusions with a broader, more uniform measure of income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether fragmented preferences and special nonrecognition rules should be replaced by a principled broad-base structure.

themes.name: Should capital and investment income be taxed at lower rates than labor income?
themes.definition: This question examines the equity, efficiency, and wealth-accumulation consequences of differential taxation of returns to capital and work.

themes.name: Do progressive tax rates and income-tested benefits improve distributive fairness enough to justify their effects on work, saving, and other behavior?
themes.definition: This question weighs the redistributive benefits of progression against possible incentive and economic-efficiency costs.

themes.name: Do deductions and exclusions fairly measure taxpayers’ economic income, or do they primarily deliver unjustified benefits to higher-income taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether personal and itemized tax preferences reflect genuine reductions in ability to pay or function as regressive subsidies.

themes.name: Can tax-favored savings and retirement arrangements provide broad, equitable coverage without disproportionately subsidizing affluent households?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax advantages for retirement and precautionary saving achieve social-security goals across income groups.

themes.name: How should the Earned Income Tax Credit be redesigned to improve support for low-income workers without creating inequities among household types?
themes.definition: This question focuses on the credit’s eligibility rules, phase-ins and phase-outs, work incentives, and distributional effects.

themes.name: Should federal tax law recognize and allocate income across family and household arrangements that do not fit standard individual or entity categories?
themes.definition: This question examines how taxation should treat shared income, domestic support, and economically interdependent but legally unconventional households.

themes.name: Should estate and gift taxes be strengthened to prevent affluent families from transferring substantial wealth tax-free across generations?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether transfer-tax rules and wealth-planning strategies adequately limit intergenerational tax avoidance and wealth concentration.

themes.name: Should different forms of inherited, gifted, and family-transferred wealth receive different tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question addresses the boundary between income, gifts, inheritances, and other transfers and the distributive consequences of distinguishing among them.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow the economic substance of a transaction rather than its formal legal characterization?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether statutory labels, holding structures, and transaction categories should control taxation when they diverge from underlying economic reality.

themes.name: How should income and tax liability be allocated when economic value is transferred among related parties or between multiple claimants?
themes.definition: This question concerns the proper taxpayer and tax category for compensation, property transfers, shared returns, and other divided economic interests.

themes.name: Should damages, insurance payments, and other compensatory recoveries replacing lost earnings be taxed as income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether taxation of recoveries accurately captures economic gain while distinguishing compensation for losses from genuine enrichment.

themes.name: Do anti-avoidance doctrines appropriately distinguish abusive tax planning from legitimate business, investment, and family arrangements?
themes.definition: This question weighs protection of the revenue base against the risk that aggressive enforcement will penalize economically substantive conduct.

themes.name: Do taxpayers’ strategic responses to tax rules undermine the behavioral and revenue assumptions used to justify those rules?
themes.definition: This question tests whether avoidance, timing, restructuring, and other taxpayer responses alter the predicted effects of tax incentives and reforms.

themes.name: Can tax-based social-policy programs improve economic security more effectively than direct government programs, employer mandates, or private arrangements?
themes.definition: This question compares tax expenditures and credits with alternative institutional mechanisms for providing benefits and managing economic risk.

themes.name: Do tax rules impose systematically unequal burdens on women, racial minorities, or other historically disadvantaged groups despite formally neutral language?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether tax classifications and household assumptions reproduce structural disparities in taxation and benefits.

themes.name: Can tax reform improve equity and efficiency without creating excessive administrative, compliance, and uncertainty costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tradeoffs between technically precise or targeted rules and simpler, more administrable alternatives.

themes.name: Is major structural replacement of the existing federal income-tax system preferable to piecemeal reform?
themes.definition: This question compares comprehensive reform with incremental changes in light of institutional path dependence, political feasibility, and unintended consequences.

themes.name: Should federal income-tax burdens be allocated according to taxpayers’ ability to pay, and how should that principle be measured?
themes.definition: This question examines whether taxable income, necessary living costs, household circumstances, and economic position provide a defensible basis for distributing income-tax burdens.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation reduce economic inequality without producing unacceptable avoidance, income shifting, or efficiency costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the distributive benefits of progressive rates against taxpayer responses, revenue effects, and distortions in economic behavior.

themes.name: Should capital income and capital gains be taxed as comprehensively as labor income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether preferential or deferred taxation of returns to capital is justified by economic theory, administrative concerns, or fairness considerations.

themes.name: Should the tax system move from an income base toward consumption taxation?
themes.definition: This question compares income and consumption tax bases with respect to equity, savings incentives, revenue, and the distributional consequences of reducing income taxation.

themes.name: Do deductions, exclusions, credits, and other tax preferences advance legitimate policy goals or improperly erode the tax base?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether particular tax expenditures are justified by their intended social or economic purposes and whether their distributional costs are acceptable.

themes.name: Do tax subsidies and investment incentives primarily benefit their intended recipients, or are their benefits captured through market-price and incidence effects?
themes.definition: This question investigates how tax-favored treatment affects prices, investment decisions, and the ultimate distribution of benefits among taxpayers and economic actors.

themes.name: Should tax rules recognize noncommercial household labor, caregiving, and family resources when measuring taxable economic capacity?
themes.definition: This question examines whether unpaid work, household production, and family-based economic support should affect the definition or allocation of tax liability.

themes.name: Does federal tax law unfairly privilege marriage and traditional family arrangements over same-sex, unmarried, or otherwise nontraditional households?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether differences in filing, benefits, transfers, and household taxation produce unequal treatment among economically comparable family arrangements.

themes.name: How should federal tax law allocate income, property, and tax burdens between spouses and across family generations?
themes.definition: This question addresses the treatment of marital property, spousal transfers, inheritance, and intergenerational family interests in determining tax liability and economic security.

themes.name: Are estate, gift, and wealth-transfer taxes effective and equitable tools for limiting inherited wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the revenue, avoidance, fairness, and inequality consequences of taxing transfers of wealth during life and at death.

themes.name: Should aggressive transfer-tax planning be curtailed when formal gifts, trusts, or assignments preserve the transferor’s underlying economic control?
themes.definition: This question examines whether wealth-transfer tax law should follow formal legal arrangements or disregard them when they function as strategies for avoiding transfer tax.

themes.name: When should income, gain, deductions, and recoveries be recognized for tax purposes rather than deferred until a later event?
themes.definition: This question evaluates competing timing rules for transactions whose economic benefits or losses accrue over multiple tax years.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow legal form or the underlying economic substance of a transaction?
themes.definition: This question examines whether formal classifications, trusts, ownership structures, and transaction labels produce results that diverge improperly from economic reality.

themes.name: Do tax classifications adequately capture unusual, noncash, or nontraditional forms of income and property?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether existing income-tax concepts properly identify novel economic benefits, services, property interests, and third-party payments as taxable items.

themes.name: Can tax incentives change private behavior in ways that justify their revenue costs and unequal treatment?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether incentives for saving, investment, compensation, employment benefits, or other conduct achieve their policy objectives without excessive distortion.

themes.name: Do tax-based social benefits effectively improve the economic security of their intended beneficiaries?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the targeting, after-tax effects, distributional outcomes, and policy effectiveness of credits, subsidies, and refundable benefits.

themes.name: Does administering social policy through the tax code create unacceptable complexity, compliance costs, or limits on administrative authority?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax-based benefits remain workable when eligibility, payment, recoupment, and enforcement require substantial administrative infrastructure.

themes.name: Should simpler and more uniform tax rules replace differentiated rules that better reflect economic circumstances?
themes.definition: This question weighs administrative simplicity, compliance, and legal coherence against the fairness and accuracy gained from individualized classifications and tax treatment.

themes.name: Do overlapping federal tax regimes produce coherent and equitable effective tax burdens?
themes.definition: This question investigates how income, payroll, transfer, benefit, and related financial rules interact rather than evaluating each provision in isolation.

themes.name: Should structural reform replace piecemeal amendments to the federal income-tax system?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether persistent defects in the tax base, incentives, administration, and distribution require a redesigned framework rather than narrow statutory corrections.

themes.name: Should the federal tax base be defined by comprehensive income, consumption, or changes in wealth?
themes.definition: This question compares competing tax-base models and asks which better captures economic capacity while remaining normatively legitimate and administrable.

themes.name: Should unrealized appreciation and other accruals be taxed before realization?
themes.definition: This question examines whether changes in asset value or wealth should generate tax liability even when taxpayers have not sold or otherwise disposed of the asset.

themes.name: Do existing rules understate or mismeasure noncash and nontraditional economic income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether benefits, property, services, and other noncash gains are adequately valued and included in gross income.

themes.name: Should labor income and capital income receive more equal tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether preferential treatment of investment returns over wages is justified or instead creates inequitable burdens and distorted economic choices.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation reduce inequality without imposing excessive burdens on ordinary taxpayers or discouraging productive activity?
themes.definition: This question assesses how rates, exemptions, and income thresholds should balance redistribution, economic incentives, and political feasibility.

themes.name: Do tax rules impose disproportionately harmful burdens on low-income and economically vulnerable households?
themes.definition: This question studies whether revenue-raising provisions and tax structures deepen poverty or otherwise burden disadvantaged taxpayers more heavily than their nominal liability suggests.

themes.name: Are tax deductions, exclusions, and credits effective and equitable tools for achieving social-policy goals?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax expenditures deliver their intended benefits or instead provide poorly targeted subsidies and unequal treatment across income groups.

themes.name: Does the Earned Income Tax Credit effectively reduce poverty without creating unacceptable administrative and compliance problems?
themes.definition: This question examines the EITC as a tax-administered anti-poverty benefit, including its distributional effects, work incentives, complexity, and error risks.

themes.name: Do tax and welfare programs unfairly privilege a married-couple or traditional-family model?
themes.definition: This question asks whether family-based tax and benefit rules disadvantage single parents, unmarried partners, women, or households with nontraditional caregiving arrangements.

themes.name: How should tax law account for spouses’ and family members’ separate economic interests?
themes.definition: This question compares joint and individual approaches to family taxation and evaluates whether treating the family as a single economic unit produces equitable liability.

themes.name: Should the federal wealth-transfer tax system be expanded or redesigned to address concentrated wealth and intergenerational inequality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legal and normative design of estate, gift, and related transfer taxes, including their treatment of intimate-partner transfers and wealth-planning strategies.

themes.name: Can taxpayers use legal planning, timing, or wealth reallocation to defeat the intended progressivity of the tax system?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether avoidance opportunities allow affluent taxpayers to escape burdens that less powerful taxpayers cannot avoid.

themes.name: Do substance-over-form and anti-avoidance rules prevent tax-base erosion without creating new distortions?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether rules targeting transactions that disguise their economic substance are effective, predictable, and consistent with administrable legal principles.

themes.name: How should payments, litigation recoveries, and unusual receipts be classified for tax purposes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether formal legal categories accurately determine the tax treatment of settlements, judgments, distributions, and other ambiguous receipts.

themes.name: Does corporate tax design allocate capital efficiently without creating offsetting equity and revenue problems?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how corporate taxes affect investment, ownership, capital allocation, and the distribution of tax burdens among firms, workers, and investors.

themes.name: Do tax incentives actually produce the socially desirable behavior they are intended to encourage?
themes.definition: This question tests whether credits, deductions, exemptions, and preferential regimes change household or market behavior in ways that advance their stated policy objectives.

themes.name: Does differential tax treatment distort economic decisions and resource allocation?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether tax preferences and unequal treatment of economically similar activities alter investment, saving, employment, consumption, or other market choices.

themes.name: Does tax-law complexity undermine compliance, administration, and equitable treatment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether overlapping provisions, difficult credit rules, and uncertain obligations increase errors, avoidance, enforcement costs, and disparities between taxpayers.

themes.name: Should tax interpretation prioritize statutory text and administrable rules or congressional purpose and substantive fairness?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tension between formal legal classifications, purposive interpretation, judicial discretion, and policy-oriented enforcement.

themes.name: Can federal tax reform reconcile equity, efficiency, revenue, administrability, and political durability?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether proposed structural reforms can improve distributive fairness and policy coherence without producing unacceptable economic, administrative, institutional, or political costs.

themes.name: Does preferential taxation of capital and investment income unjustifiably increase inequality?
themes.definition: This question examines whether reduced or deferred taxation of capital gains, investment returns, and savings primarily benefits wealthy taxpayers and undermines equitable burden sharing.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation redistribute resources without imposing unacceptable efficiency costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how graduated rates and ability-to-pay principles should be balanced against investment, labor-supply, neutrality, and other behavioral effects.

themes.name: Should the federal income-tax base include unrealized, noncash, or otherwise indirectly realized increases in wealth?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether economic gains that have not been conventionally realized should nevertheless be treated as taxable income.

themes.name: Should tax law prioritize economic substance over formal legal classification?
themes.definition: This question asks whether transactions, payments, property interests, and benefits should receive tax treatment based on their economic effects rather than their statutory or private-law labels.

themes.name: Do tax preferences effectively promote socially beneficial behavior, or do they mainly create inefficient subsidies?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether targeted exclusions, deductions, credits, and deferrals change private conduct in ways that justify departing from a neutral tax system.

themes.name: How should tax law define the family and taxable household unit?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax rules should treat marriage, same-sex relationships, caregiving arrangements, and nontraditional households differently when allocating tax burdens and benefits.

themes.name: Should inter vivos gifts and transfers at death receive different tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the policy and distributional justification for distinguishing lifetime transfers from inheritances and other death-time wealth transfers.

themes.name: Do estate- and gift-tax preferences create unjustified loopholes in the taxation of accumulated wealth?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether exemptions, valuation rules, and other favorable wealth-transfer provisions undermine revenue, progressivity, or intergenerational fairness.

themes.name: Are refundable tax credits an effective and equitable substitute for direct income support?
themes.definition: This question evaluates programs such as the earned income tax credit and related refundable benefits in terms of poverty reduction, work incentives, accessibility, and administrative burden.

themes.name: Do tax-based education subsidies make higher education and human-capital investment more affordable?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax incentives and government-sponsored education programs effectively expand access without disproportionately benefiting higher-income households.

themes.name: Is publicly provided social insurance preferable to privately managed savings for addressing economic insecurity?
themes.definition: This question compares public insurance and private savings as mechanisms for distributing protection against income loss, caregiving needs, and other social risks.

themes.name: Should personal-injury recoveries, insurance payments, and litigation-related awards be excluded from taxable income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether payments connected to personal harm, medical needs, insurance, or legal claims represent taxable economic gain and how related legal fees should be treated.

themes.name: Does the complexity of specialized tax rules undermine their policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question asks whether detailed exceptions, relief mechanisms, accounting provisions, and tax-based benefits are too difficult or unpredictable for taxpayers and administrators to apply consistently.

themes.name: Should courts and tax agencies interpret ambiguous provisions by reference to statutory purpose rather than isolated text?
themes.definition: This question evaluates purposive and systemic interpretation when interconnected tax provisions, fragmented definitions, or incomplete legislative designs produce uncertainty.

themes.name: How should tax enforcement balance compliance and anti-avoidance goals against taxpayer autonomy and legal rights?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether enforcement mechanisms, reporting requirements, and administrative procedures prevent evasion without imposing disproportionate burdens or violating individual protections.

themes.name: How do political pressure and concentrated economic interests shape tax legislation?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax rules reflect public-interest policy or instead arise from partisan coalitions, organized interests, public perceptions, and the political visibility of tax benefits.

themes.name: Are facially neutral tax classifications producing unjustified burdens for particular demographic or household groups?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether formally uniform rules generate discriminatory or unequal outcomes across income groups, family types, marital statuses, or similarly situated taxpayers.

themes.name: What constitutional limits constrain the government's authority to tax private property and economic activity?
themes.definition: This question examines how constitutional principles, property rights, nondiscrimination requirements, and judicial doctrine delimit federal taxing and enforcement power.

themes.name: Should the United States replace or supplement the income tax with a consumption-based tax?
themes.definition: This question compares income and consumption tax bases in terms of equity, capital taxation, administrative simplicity, revenue, economic incentives, and distributional consequences.

themes.name: How should tax reform be evaluated when revenue, distributional, behavioral, and administrative effects conflict?
themes.definition: This question asks whether reform proposals should be judged by their net effects on government revenue, taxpayer behavior, disadvantaged groups, neutrality, and implementation feasibility rather than by a single criterion.

themes.name: Should the federal tax base be defined by comprehensive income, consumption, or a hybrid approach?
themes.definition: This question examines whether taxable income, consumption, or a combined measure best captures economic capacity while balancing equity, efficiency, and administrative feasibility.

themes.name: Should the realization principle continue to defer taxation of unrealized increases in wealth?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether income should be taxed when it accrues economically or only when it is realized through a sale, transfer, or other transaction.

themes.name: Should tax liability follow economic substance rather than formal transaction structure?
themes.definition: This question asks whether legally distinct arrangements with equivalent economic effects should receive equivalent tax treatment despite differences in form, characterization, or legal status.

themes.name: Do formal income-tax classifications produce unjustified differences among economically similar taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether categories such as income, capital, labor, gifts, deductions, and exclusions create coherent and normatively defensible distinctions.

themes.name: Should tax liability reflect ability to pay rather than observed taxable income alone?
themes.definition: This question considers whether purchasing power, accumulated wealth, economic resources, or other measures of capacity should supplement or replace conventional taxable-income measures.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation achieve distributive fairness without unacceptable administrative, economic, or political costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the equity benefits of progressive rates against effects on compliance, labor and investment incentives, complexity, revenue, and political legitimacy.

themes.name: Should tax reform broaden the tax base instead of relying primarily on rate changes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether reducing exemptions, exclusions, deductions, and preferential treatments can produce a fairer and more administrable tax system than altering rates alone.

themes.name: Do targeted tax deductions, exclusions, and credits achieve their stated social-policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether individualized tax benefits effectively advance goals such as household support, education, investment, or human development relative to their fiscal and distributional costs.

themes.name: Should refundable income-tax credits be used to support low-income households?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether refundable credits are an effective and equitable way to provide income support while preserving work incentives and administrative feasibility.
