themes.definition: This question examines the role of the IRS, administrative rules, compliance mechanisms, and enforcement constraints in determining the practical reach and legitimacy of tax law.

themes.name: Should the exclusion for personal-injury damages under IRC § 104(a)(2) be narrowed or interpreted according to the exclusion’s underlying purpose?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the scope of the personal-injury exclusion should depend on economic substance and statutory purpose rather than formal categories of damages.

themes.name: Do political institutions and concentrated interests prevent tax reforms from achieving their intended redistributive goals?
themes.definition: This question investigates how legislative bargaining, wealthy or organized interests, public acceptance, and administrative feasibility shape the design and durability of progressive tax reform.

themes.name: Should taxable income follow taxpayers’ actual net economic gains rather than the formal timing or characterization of receipts?
themes.definition: This question examines whether income-tax rules should measure substantive economic increases in wealth instead of relying on legal labels, receipt timing, or nominal amounts.

themes.name: Is the realization principle a defensible basis for taxing capital income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether capital gains should generally be taxed only upon realization or whether accrual-based approaches better reflect economic income.

themes.name: How should the tax system address the distortion created by taxing nominal rather than inflation-adjusted capital gains?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether taxation of gains that merely reflect inflation mismeasures investment income and produces economically inefficient outcomes.

themes.name: Should capital income and investment returns receive preferential treatment under the federal income tax?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legal and distributional justifications for different tax treatment of capital income, saving, and investment relative to labor income.

themes.name: Should accumulated wealth be taxed directly as a supplement to, or replacement for, income taxation?
themes.definition: This question compares wealth taxes with income-based taxation as tools for raising revenue, reducing inequality, and taxing concentrated economic power.

themes.name: Should the federal tax system be replaced or supplemented by a consumption- or expenditure-based tax?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether consumption taxation would improve neutrality, administrability, revenue collection, or distributional fairness compared with an income tax.

themes.name: How should tax rates and tax bases allocate burdens across income and wealth groups?
themes.definition: This question examines whether alternative rate structures, exemptions, and definitions of the tax base distribute tax liabilities fairly across economic classes.

themes.name: Should tax fairness depend on taxpayers’ ability to pay and economic circumstances beyond taxable income?
themes.definition: This question considers whether fair taxation must account for differences such as household obligations, financial constraints, or other substantive economic conditions.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation reduce inequality without producing unacceptable efficiency losses or behavioral distortions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tradeoff between redistributive tax burdens and effects on work, saving, investment, avoidance, and resource allocation.

themes.name: Should tax expenditures be replaced by broader, more neutral tax rules?
themes.definition: This question asks whether deductions, exclusions, exemptions, and credits that pursue social objectives create enough distortion, complexity, or unequal access to warrant structural replacement.

themes.name: Are targeted and conditional tax benefits more effective and fair than universal social benefits?
themes.definition: This question compares need-based or behavior-dependent tax subsidies with broader policies in terms of access, distribution, incentives, and administrative cost.

themes.name: Should tax deductions for socially valuable expenditures be limited when they also subsidize private consumption?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deductions for care, health, education, or similar expenses should depend on the extent to which they produce public benefits rather than personal advantages.

themes.name: Do tax incentives successfully change private behavior enough to justify their distributive and administrative costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether subsidies for saving, investment, employment, caregiving, or other conduct achieve their intended behavioral goals without excessive distortion.

themes.name: How should tax law prevent taxpayers from exploiting legal gaps or mismatches to avoid or recharacterize income?
themes.definition: This question concerns the effectiveness and legitimacy of anti-avoidance rules addressing strategic ownership, transaction structuring, timing, and favorable legal classifications.

themes.name: Can anti-avoidance rules target abusive tax planning without burdening legitimate economic transactions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how tax enforcement should distinguish opportunistic exploitation of the tax code from ordinary commercial planning and economically productive activity.

themes.name: Should tax liability follow the party receiving the real economic benefit rather than formal ownership or receipt?
themes.definition: This question addresses allocation disputes in which legal title, contractual form, or payment receipt differs from the person who economically benefits from a transaction.

themes.name: Do formal tax classifications adequately capture the economic substance and distributive consequences of transactions?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether categories such as gifts, compensation, transfers for consideration, ownership, and business or personal expenses accurately reflect underlying economic reality.

themes.name: How should federal tax rules accommodate legally diverse marriages, families, and household economic arrangements?
themes.definition: This question examines whether joint taxation, family deductions, marital status, caregiving, and parental obligations should reflect relationships beyond the traditional unified-family model.

themes.name: Does tax-law complexity undermine coherent administration, compliance, and equal treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether intricate and uncertain rules create excessive information costs, inconsistent enforcement, unequal access to benefits, or opportunities for avoidance.

themes.name: Should comprehensive tax reform be preferred to incremental amendments to an incoherent existing system?
themes.definition: This question compares broad restructuring with piecemeal reform while considering political feasibility, implementation burdens, unintended consequences, and compatibility with existing legal institutions.

themes.name: Should the federal income tax move toward a broad, relatively uniform base by eliminating exclusions, deductions, and special preferences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether categorical departures from a comprehensive income base are justified by equity, efficiency, administrative, or social-policy objectives.

themes.name: Should accrued investment gains be taxed before realization, including when property is transferred at death?
themes.definition: This question examines whether realization and deferral rules accurately measure investment income or instead permit substantial untaxed appreciation and avoidance.

themes.name: Should deductions and inclusions be matched across related transactions and tax years?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether timing rules should coordinate deductions, inclusions, changing taxpayer circumstances, and economically linked transactions to prevent arbitrary or strategic tax results.

themes.name: Should the tax treatment of employment compensation and its associated expenditures follow economic function rather than formal legal categories?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether wages, fringe benefits, and expenses connected with earning compensation should receive tax treatment based on their substantive economic character.

themes.name: Should capital gains and ordinary income continue to receive different federal tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the legal distinction between capital and ordinary income reflects meaningful economic differences or creates unjustified preferential treatment and avoidance opportunities.

themes.name: How should federal tax law classify noncash transactions, unconventional arrangements, recoveries, and personal-injury settlements?
themes.definition: This question concerns when economically consequential transfers or recoveries should be recognized as taxable income, excluded amounts, or transactions governed by special inclusion rules.

themes.name: Should federal tax treatment of marriage and family transfers be based on legal status or on the parties’ underlying economic relationships?
themes.definition: This question examines marital-property classifications, same-sex and nonmarital couples, intra-family transfers, and income allocation among related parties.

themes.name: Is the estate tax an adequate and legitimate instrument for taxing concentrated wealth and intergenerational transfers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether transfer taxation meaningfully addresses wealth concentration while fairly allocating burdens on property transferred at death.

themes.name: Should progressive taxation impose substantially higher burdens on high-income taxpayers to advance ability-to-pay and distributive justice goals?
themes.definition: This question assesses the normative, behavioral, and political case for progressive rates rather than flat or proportionate taxation.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for housing, saving, investment, and wealth preservation reduce inequality or primarily subsidize already advantaged taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question investigates the distributional effects of major tax subsidies and whether their benefits are concentrated among higher-income or wealthier households.

themes.name: Can the earned income tax credit be administered to expand access for eligible households without encouraging improper claims?
themes.definition: This question examines the tradeoff between broad participation in refundable work-based benefits and enforcement against errors, intermediaries, and illegitimate claims.

themes.name: Do technical tax-planning structures and legally permitted deferral mechanisms allow taxpayers to reduce liability without reducing underlying economic income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether structural loopholes, related-party arrangements, and sophisticated planning undermine the intended tax base and distribution of burdens.

themes.name: Can tax rules be simplified without sacrificing accurate income measurement, equitable treatment, and anti-avoidance protections?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether complexity, inconsistent classifications, and detailed limitations are necessary safeguards or sources of uncertainty and inequity.

themes.name: How should courts and the IRS resolve uncertainty when statutory tax provisions are technically incomplete, complex, or inconsistent?
themes.definition: This question concerns the respective roles of textual, contextual, purposive, judicial, and administrative interpretation in producing predictable tax outcomes.

themes.name: Should federal tax rules prioritize uniform national treatment or accommodate state-law classifications and state policy autonomy?
themes.definition: This question examines conflicts between federal tax uniformity and state control over marital status, property rights, and related legal institutions.

themes.name: Do tax incentives effectively change taxpayer behavior in ways that justify their revenue costs and distributional consequences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferences intended to promote saving, investment, housing, employment, or other conduct achieve their stated objectives rather than functioning mainly as politically attractive benefits.

themes.name: Should tax-based redistribution be delivered through the tax code or through direct government spending and social programs?
themes.definition: This question compares tax expenditures, refundable credits, transfers, and direct programs as instruments for reducing poverty and advancing social welfare.

themes.name: Can tax policy address gender-based economic disadvantage without reinforcing traditional household and caregiving roles?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether gender-neutral or targeted tax benefits and transfer rules improve women’s economic autonomy and fairly recognize unpaid contributions.

themes.name: Should longstanding federal tax doctrines be redesigned when they no longer fit contemporary economic and social arrangements?
themes.definition: This question asks whether inherited legal categories and established provisions should be fundamentally replaced rather than preserved through increasingly complex exceptions.

themes.name: What constitutional limits constrain progressive taxation and major federal tax reforms?
themes.definition: This question examines the Sixteenth Amendment, Article I direct-tax requirements, and related constitutional constraints on federal and state-level tax policy.

themes.name: Should progressive taxation be strengthened to reduce wealth and income inequality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether higher effective burdens on affluent taxpayers and redistribution through the federal tax system can reduce concentrated wealth and unequal opportunity without imposing unacceptable efficiency or administrative costs.

themes.name: Can a broad tax base combined with progressive rates and targeted credits improve both equity and administrability?
themes.definition: This question compares broad-based tax structures with narrower systems of deductions, exclusions, and preferences to determine whether they distribute burdens fairly while remaining workable to administer.

themes.name: Should the federal tax system be based on consumption rather than income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether consumption taxation would provide a more coherent or efficient tax base than income taxation and how the choice would affect progressivity, savings, and redistribution.

themes.name: How should wealth and capital appreciation be incorporated into an income-tax system?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether and how unrealized appreciation, accumulated wealth, or other capital interests can be included in income taxation without relying on a separate wealth tax.

themes.name: Should inherited wealth be taxed more heavily through gift and estate taxation?
themes.definition: This question assesses the fairness, legitimacy, behavioral effects, and revenue consequences of taxing intergenerational transfers as a means of limiting wealth concentration.

themes.name: How should income taxation interact with estate taxation when appreciated property is transferred at death?
themes.definition: This question examines whether basis, realization, and estate-tax rules produce gaps or double taxation when appreciated assets pass to heirs.

themes.name: Do anti-avoidance rules effectively prevent families from shifting wealth through trusts and other transfer-planning vehicles?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether specialized family wealth arrangements and formal transfer rules allow taxpayers to obtain unintended tax benefits despite gift- and estate-tax safeguards.

themes.name: Should tax law preserve preferential treatment for marriage and family relationships?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether joint filing, spousal treatment, family credits, and related rules fairly recognize household obligations or instead create unjustified advantages and penalties.

themes.name: How should the tax system treat economic support and contributions within families?
themes.definition: This question asks whether transfers, unpaid labor, and financial contributions among family members should be recognized as income, deductible expenses, or protected benefits for tax purposes.

themes.name: Do targeted tax credits and preferences achieve their stated social-policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question tests whether tax subsidies change behavior or deliver intended benefits, rather than merely rewarding taxpayers who would have acted similarly without the subsidy.

themes.name: Should tax preferences be replaced by direct spending or subsidies?
themes.definition: This question compares tax-based assistance with direct government programs in terms of distribution, transparency, administrative cost, eligibility, and effectiveness.

themes.name: Do income-based phase-outs and eligibility rules distribute tax benefits inequitably?
themes.definition: This question examines whether thresholds and phase-outs exclude vulnerable households, create high effective marginal rates, or produce arbitrary differences among economically similar taxpayers.

themes.name: Should labor income and capital income bear comparable tax burdens?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the distributive and efficiency consequences of taxing wages differently from investment returns, business income, and wealth-derived gains.

themes.name: How should deductions, exclusions, and loss-offset rules define taxable income?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether these provisions accurately measure economic income or instead create inequitable burdens, artificial incentives, and opportunities for tax reduction.

themes.name: Should realization and nonrecognition rules apply to economically transformed investment products and property transfers?
themes.definition: This question asks whether tax law should defer or avoid recognizing gains and losses when formal transactions differ from their underlying economic effects.

themes.name: Should tax classification follow economic substance rather than formal legal labels?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether economically equivalent payments, rights, transactions, and expenditures should receive equivalent tax treatment despite differences in contractual or legal form.

themes.name: How should deferred-payment transactions account for unstated or imputed interest?
themes.definition: This question examines whether and how tax law should separate principal from implicit interest so that timing and characterization rules accurately reflect the economics of deferred payments.

themes.name: Should damages and legal recoveries be taxed according to the underlying injury or claim?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether payments for lost wages, lost earning capacity, emotional distress, physical injury, or other legal claims should be included in or excluded from taxable income.

themes.name: Can simpler and more administrable tax rules reduce complexity without increasing avoidance?
themes.definition: This question weighs precise but complex eligibility and computation rules against simpler standards that may improve administration while creating new opportunities for strategic behavior.

themes.name: How do taxpayers and institutions strategically adapt to tax rules and enforcement?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether planning, restructuring, noncompliance, or institutional responses undermine the intended behavioral, distributional, or revenue effects of tax legislation.

themes.name: Should unrealized appreciation and noncash receipts be included in the income-tax base?
themes.definition: This question examines whether accession to wealth, economic capacity, or dominion and control should trigger taxation when income has not been converted into cash or formally realized.

themes.name: Should the tax treatment of personal-injury damages depend on whether an award replaces wages, medical costs, or other losses?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether different components of personal-injury recoveries should be taxed consistently with the ordinary income or expenses they replace.

themes.name: Does joint or separate taxation of married and unmarried households allocate income-tax burdens fairly?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether federal tax rules treat legally recognized relationships and household-level economic choices equitably across married, unmarried, and otherwise comparable taxpayers.

themes.name: How should income-tax rules treat family support and divorce-related transfers?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether deductions, inclusions, and other tax consequences for alimony, child support, and related transfers reflect their economic substance and distribute burdens fairly.

themes.name: Do tax and social-insurance systems fairly account for unpaid caregiving and gendered divisions of work?
themes.definition: This question examines whether fiscal and welfare policies reinforce or mitigate disparities in women’s labor-force participation, caregiving responsibilities, and access to benefits.

themes.name: Are tax credits more equitable and effective than deductions for subsidizing health, education, and other essential expenditures?
themes.definition: This question compares credits, deductions, exclusions, and direct benefits as mechanisms for assisting households with medical, educational, caregiving, or similar costs.

themes.name: Should inherited property receive a basis adjustment at death, or should appreciation be taxed to preserve the income-tax base?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the historical and policy justification for stepped-up basis and alternative treatments of appreciated assets transferred at death.

themes.name: Can wealth-transfer taxes limit dynastic wealth without imposing disproportionate burdens on ordinary households?
themes.definition: This question concerns the design of gift and estate taxes, including exemptions, rates, and valuation rules, to reduce concentrated inherited wealth while remaining administrable and politically legitimate.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for saving and investment produce sufficient economic benefits to justify their distributional costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential treatment of retirement accounts, capital gains, reinvestment, or particular investments improves saving and growth enough to offset inequity and revenue loss.

themes.name: Do tax expenditures effectively achieve their stated social-policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question tests whether exclusions, deductions, credits, and other tax subsidies actually improve access to targeted goods or services rather than primarily benefiting higher-income taxpayers.

themes.name: Should tax liability follow the economic substance of a transaction rather than its formal legal classification?
themes.definition: This question examines whether formally distinct but economically equivalent payments, property interests, or transactions should receive different tax treatment.

themes.name: How should anti-avoidance rules regulate legally structured transfers and economically similar transactions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether taxpayers can exploit trusts, property transfers, compensation arrangements, or technical distinctions to defer or eliminate tax contrary to legislative purpose.

themes.name: Are complex eligibility boundaries and tax-favored arrangements enforceable without imposing unequal administrative burdens?
themes.definition: This question examines IRS enforcement, noncompliance, error, and fraud risks in specialized tax programs and the effects of enforcement costs on vulnerable taxpayers.

themes.name: How should the timing of deductions, losses, and liabilities reflect economic consequences that arise over multiple periods?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether realization and accounting-timing rules accurately allocate deductions and losses while accounting for tax deferral and the time value of money.

themes.name: Can tax reform improve fairness without making the tax system too complex or costly to administer?
themes.definition: This question concerns the tradeoff between precise, flexible treatment of taxpayers and the simplicity, compliance, and administrative costs of detailed rules.

themes.name: Should progressive tax burdens be increased for wealthy taxpayers even when doing so may reduce efficiency or alter economic behavior?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how income, wealth, and transfer taxes should balance redistribution and ability-to-pay principles against work, saving, investment, and compliance incentives.

themes.name: Do tax-based benefits adequately support low-income households without weakening work incentives?
themes.definition: This question examines whether credits and other benefits provide effective income protection while avoiding phase-out structures and incentives that discourage employment or increase effective marginal tax rates.

themes.name: Should the tax code use differentiated treatment to accommodate taxpayers with different household, economic, or personal circumstances?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether uniform tax rules are fairer than targeted distinctions among taxpayers with unequal resources, family structures, or needs.

themes.name: Should constitutional meaning, legislative history, or statutory purpose control the interpretation of unsettled federal tax rules?
themes.definition: This question examines how courts and agencies should resolve ambiguity when textual classifications, original meaning, later statutory changes, and congressional objectives point in different directions.

themes.name: How should taxing authority and revenue responsibilities be divided between the federal government and the states?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legal legitimacy, fiscal consequences, and distributional effects of allocating taxation of income, property, and other bases across federal and state governments.

themes.name: Should the federal income tax be replaced or substantially supplemented by a consumption-based tax?
themes.definition: This question compares comprehensive income taxation with consumption-based alternatives and evaluates their effects on revenue, efficiency, progressivity, and distributive justice.

themes.name: Is progressive income taxation justified as a means of advancing ability-to-pay and distributive justice?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether unequal or progressive tax rates are normatively legitimate and how they affect fairness, redistribution, and public legitimacy.

themes.name: Should taxation of wealthy individuals and concentrated investment income be strengthened to reduce inequality?
themes.definition: This question examines whether higher taxation of wealthy taxpayers, capital income, or accumulated resources can reduce wealth concentration without unacceptable efficiency or avoidance costs.

themes.name: Would a federal wealth tax be constitutional under the Direct Tax, Apportionment, and Sixteenth Amendment frameworks?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether federal taxation of wealth or unrealized holdings falls within constitutional limits on federal taxing power.

themes.name: Should capital gains receive preferential tax treatment over labor income?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether lower rates, realization rules, or other preferences for capital gains are justified by efficiency, investment, administrative, or equity considerations.

themes.name: Do tax deductions and credits deliver public benefits more effectively and equitably than direct government spending?
themes.definition: This question compares tax-based subsidies with direct spending as instruments for achieving social, economic, educational, retirement, or welfare objectives.

themes.name: Should tax expenditures be redesigned to preserve legitimate support while limiting unintended benefits for affluent taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question examines whether exclusions, deductions, credits, and other preferences should be narrowed, converted, or restructured to better target their intended beneficiaries.

themes.name: Are refundable tax credits, particularly the Earned Income Tax Credit, effective and equitable tools for supporting low-income workers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the distributional, behavioral, administrative, and political performance of refundable credits tied to work and household income.

themes.name: Should family care and household support be subsidized through tax rules rather than treated as private family responsibilities?
themes.definition: This question considers whether childcare, dependency, family transfers, and related care obligations warrant broader public support through the tax system.

themes.name: Do ostensibly neutral tax and benefit rules reproduce gendered or racialized inequalities?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether formally uniform rules embed unequal effects through family roles, labor-market conditions, wealth differences, or other structural disadvantages.

themes.name: Should economically similar receipts and transfers receive the same tax treatment regardless of their formal legal classification?
themes.definition: This question tests whether tax consequences should follow economic substance rather than labels such as gift, compensation, capital, income, ownership, or transfer.

themes.name: How should the income tax treat noncash benefits, unrealized appreciation, and other difficult-to-value economic gains?
themes.definition: This question addresses the proper tax base, valuation methods, and timing rules for wealth increases or benefits that are not received as ordinary cash.

themes.name: Do realization and deferral rules create unjustified tax arbitrage and distort economic decisions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether differences in the timing of taxation across assets, transactions, or income forms enable avoidance or inefficient restructuring.

themes.name: Should inherited wealth and inter vivos transfers receive different tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether gifts made during life and transfers at death should be taxed differently in light of administrability, family autonomy, avoidance, and redistribution.

themes.name: Does the transfer-tax system adequately limit dynastic wealth accumulation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether estate and gift taxes achieve their redistributive purposes or require stronger rules, broader bases, or revised doctrines.

themes.name: Do complex categorical tax rules and statutory gaps systematically enable sophisticated taxpayers to obtain unintended advantages?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether complexity, fragmented provisions, and formal distinctions produce unequal access to tax planning and undermine compliance.

themes.name: Should tax law prioritize substantive policy purposes over rigid inherited doctrines and formal interpretations?
themes.definition: This question asks whether courts, agencies, and lawmakers should revise entrenched doctrines when their formal application conflicts with legislative purpose or contemporary policy goals.

themes.name: Are current statutory, judicial, and administrative interpretation practices adequate for resolving ambiguous tax classifications?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how effectively legal institutions develop coherent rules from statutes, regulations, precedent, legislative history, and administrative practice.

themes.name: Do tax incentives change real economic behavior enough to justify their revenue and distributional costs?
themes.definition: This question tests whether preferences intended to influence saving, investment, work, retirement, property, or other choices produce meaningful effects rather than primarily subsidizing activity that would occur anyway.

themes.name: Can tax reform improve fairness and revenue without imposing excessive efficiency, compliance, or administrative costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how policymakers should balance distributive objectives, behavioral distortions, revenue needs, enforceability, political feasibility, and public acceptance when redesigning tax institutions.

themes.name: Should the federal income-tax base follow economic accretion rather than formal labels or realization events?
themes.definition: This question examines whether income-tax law should tax underlying economic gains, including noncash, contingent, or unrealized gains, instead of relying primarily on legal characterization and completed transactions.

themes.name: Do realization and timing rules accurately measure when taxpayers have obtained taxable economic gains?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether rules governing deferral, future amounts, litigation recoveries, uncertain liabilities, and transaction completion produce economically accurate and administrable tax timing.

themes.name: Should tax treatment of capital income be shifted toward wealth or consumption taxation?
themes.definition: This question compares income, wealth, and postpaid-consumption approaches to taxing returns from saving, investment, accumulated assets, and capital transfers.

themes.name: Does the estate and gift tax system fairly tax lifetime gifts and transfers at death?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether gift-tax, estate-tax, valuation, and transfer-timing rules treat inter vivos and testamentary wealth transfers consistently while limiting planning opportunities.

themes.name: Does federal tax policy reduce concentrated wealth, or does it reinforce wealth inequality?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether income-tax preferences, capital-income rules, inheritance provisions, and wealth-transfer taxes distribute resources broadly or entrench economic hierarchy.

themes.name: Should progressive taxation take priority over neutrality and economic incentives?
themes.definition: This question examines whether graduated rates and redistributive burdens are justified despite possible effects on work, saving, investment, income shifting, and other economic behavior.

themes.name: Do deductions, exclusions, and exemptions distribute tax benefits fairly across income groups?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether deductions and exclusions are equitable or regressive compared with refundable or nonrefundable credits and whether they create unequal treatment of similarly situated taxpayers.

themes.name: Are tax-favored savings, education, retirement, and employee-benefit arrangements targeted to those who need them?
themes.definition: This question asks whether preferential treatment of savings and employment-related benefits advances its stated social objectives or primarily benefits higher-income and already advantaged households.

themes.name: Should tax subsidies be delivered through credits rather than deductions or exclusions?
themes.definition: This question compares the distributional, behavioral, and administrative consequences of using credits instead of deductions or exclusions to support personal, family, educational, or employment-related objectives.

themes.name: Do household and family tax classifications fairly account for gender, caregiving, and unequal economic power?
themes.definition: This question examines whether joint filing, household-based benefits, family transfers, and work-related rules produce equitable outcomes for people with different labor-force participation and caregiving roles.

themes.name: Do tax-and-benefit rules unintentionally undermine support for vulnerable households?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether eligibility conditions, phaseouts, tax interactions, and implementation details reduce or redirect benefits intended for low-income or otherwise vulnerable recipients.

themes.name: Do tax incentives change behavior enough to justify their revenue and distributional costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax-induced changes in work, saving, investment, transactions, or civic participation produce socially valuable effects or instead create deadweight loss and inefficient choices.

themes.name: Do progressive marginal rates induce economically harmful income shifting?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether rate differentials and classification rules cause taxpayers to recharacterize, defer, allocate, or transfer income in ways that erode revenue and distort economic decisions.

themes.name: Do anti-avoidance and loss-limitation rules prevent manipulation without denying relief for genuine economic losses?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether rules addressing fragmented interests, intra-family transfers, timing strategies, attribution, and losses appropriately distinguish abusive tax planning from legitimate transactions.

themes.name: Should substance-sensitive interpretation replace rigid formal categories in resolving tax disputes?
themes.definition: This question asks whether courts and administrators should prioritize economic substance and contextual purpose over categorical legal classifications of ownership, compensation, receipts, and transactions.

themes.name: Are statutory, judicial, and administrative tax doctrines coherent when applied to novel transactions?
themes.definition: This question examines whether interconnected provisions and judge-made doctrines produce predictable and consistent outcomes when existing rules encounter new forms of wealth, financing, or compensation.

themes.name: Has the complexity of the Internal Revenue Code made tax obligations insufficiently predictable and legitimate?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether fragmented rules, uncertain definitions, compliance burdens, and limited transparency undermine taxpayer understanding, voluntary compliance, equal treatment, and confidence in the tax system.

themes.name: Can tax reform broaden the tax base while preserving administrability and political feasibility?
themes.definition: This question considers whether eliminating exclusions, closing structural gaps, and simplifying rules can raise revenue without imposing unmanageable compliance costs or provoking politically infeasible changes.

themes.name: Should tax provisions pursue social-policy goals, or should those goals be pursued through direct spending?
themes.definition: This question compares tax expenditures with direct public programs as instruments for redistribution, work support, education, retirement security, and other social objectives.

themes.name: Do tax reforms actually deliver the fairness and distributional outcomes used to justify them?
themes.definition: This question tests whether stated egalitarian, efficiency, revenue, or social-policy rationales correspond to the actual burdens, benefits, behavioral responses, and ultimate incidence produced by reform.

themes.name: Should tax provisions pursue redistribution, regulation, or social welfare in addition to raising revenue?
themes.definition: This question examines whether using the tax system for extra-fiscal objectives is legitimate and effective compared with relying on direct regulation or spending.

themes.name: Does the federal income tax distribute burdens according to taxpayers’ actual ability to pay?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether nominal liabilities, effective tax burdens, and tax preferences accurately reflect taxpayers’ underlying economic capacity and relative well-being.

themes.name: What economic benefits should count as income under the federal income tax?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether noncash benefits, personal recoveries, service labor, and other nonstandard gains should be included in the income-tax base.

themes.name: Should capital gains receive preferential treatment compared with labor and ordinary income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the fairness, efficiency, and distributional consequences of lower rates, exclusions, or other favorable treatment for returns to capital.

themes.name: Do realization, deferral, and basis rules allow investment appreciation to escape or be undertaxed?
themes.definition: This question examines whether timing rules and inherited or transferred basis prevent the tax system from accurately taxing accumulated gains.

themes.name: Should taxpayers deduct expenses and interest incurred to produce income when calculating the tax base?
themes.definition: This question assesses how tax law should distinguish deductible business or investment costs from nondeductible personal consumption and debt.

themes.name: Do deductions, exclusions, and other tax preferences undermine a broad and equitable income-tax base?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential provisions create unjustified disparities, reduce progressivity, or distort the allocation of tax burdens.

themes.name: Are tax expenditures preferable to direct government assistance for achieving social-policy goals?
themes.definition: This question compares credits, deductions, exclusions, and subsidies delivered through the tax code with direct spending or regulatory alternatives.

themes.name: Should spouses and family members be taxed as a single economic unit or as separate individuals?
themes.definition: This question examines how filing rules, marriage, parental investment, household roles, and family support should affect income-tax liability.

themes.name: How should the tax system treat transfers made through gifts, estates, trusts, divorce, and family support?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether transferors and recipients should bear tax liability and how gift, estate, and income taxes should interact.

themes.name: Can wealth and transfer taxes reduce intergenerational inequality without imposing unacceptable economic or administrative costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the distributive, revenue, and behavioral case for supplementing income taxation with taxes on wealth, bequests, or large transfers.

themes.name: Is a federal wealth tax constitutionally permissible under the Direct Tax and Apportionment Clauses?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether taxing net wealth would constitute an unapportioned direct tax and on the judiciary’s constitutional authority to define the tax base.

themes.name: Should the United States tax consumption rather than, or in addition to, income?
themes.definition: This question compares income and consumption as tax bases in terms of fairness, saving incentives, revenue, administration, and distributional effects.

themes.name: Do tax rules for saving and investment encourage productive accumulation or distort capital allocation?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deferral, preferential rates, deductions, and other investment provisions improve economic efficiency or favor particular assets and transactions.

themes.name: Can progressive tax rates and refundable credits reduce inequality without excessively weakening work and investment incentives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tradeoff between redistribution, economic security, and behavioral responses among lower-resource and higher-income households.

themes.name: Do tax rules create unequal burdens for economically comparable taxpayers or socially differentiated groups?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether formally neutral provisions distribute benefits and liabilities unevenly across income groups, racial groups, households, or other taxpayer categories.

themes.name: When should courts disregard formal tax classifications in favor of the economic substance and policy purpose of a transaction?
themes.definition: This question examines the boundary between legitimate tax minimization and impermissible avoidance, especially when legally distinct arrangements have similar economic effects.

themes.name: Does the complexity of the Internal Revenue Code generate inequity, avoidance opportunities, and unpredictable administration?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether fragmented definitions, exceptions, specialized regimes, and formal rules produce unintended outcomes and whether simplification would improve fairness.

themes.name: Can federal tax programs be implemented and enforced consistently enough to achieve their intended policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question concerns administrative capacity, compliance mechanisms, intermediary behavior, state implementation, and the gap between statutory design and practical operation.

themes.name: How do partisan politics, lobbying, legislative compromise, and judicial interpretation shape tax reform?
themes.definition: This question examines why contested or inefficient tax provisions persist and how political and institutional processes affect the legitimacy, coherence, and evolution of tax policy.

themes.name: Should tax deductions, exemptions, and credits that disproportionately benefit high-income taxpayers be curtailed?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential departures from the income-tax base distribute benefits inequitably and should be redesigned to provide comparable gains to lower- and middle-income households.

themes.name: Should capital income be taxed more heavily than labor income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether preferential treatment of capital gains, investment returns, and business income is justified or instead shifts tax burdens toward workers.

themes.name: Should taxpayers owe tax on increases in wealth before they realize cash through a sale?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether realization and deferral rules fairly measure economic income when assets appreciate without conventional disposition or receipt.

themes.name: Should wealth transfers be taxed consistently during life and at death?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether differences between gift, estate, and inheritance taxation create avoidable planning opportunities or inequitable treatment of similarly situated transfers.

themes.name: Do estate-planning vehicles allow wealthy taxpayers to circumvent the purposes of transfer taxes?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether specialized trusts, valuation techniques, and other planning mechanisms undermine the intended taxation of large transfers and require legislative or administrative responses.

themes.name: Should family obligations and household structure affect tax liability under an ability-to-pay standard?
themes.definition: This question considers whether the tax system adequately accounts for dependents, caregiving, marriage, and other family-related reductions in available income.

themes.name: Do relationship-based tax benefits unjustifiably favor legally recognized couples or traditional households?
themes.definition: This question examines whether eligibility rules tied to marriage, family status, or formal legal relationships produce defensible or discriminatory differences in federal tax treatment.

themes.name: Can targeted tax incentives change socially desirable behavior without creating larger economic distortions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether credits, exclusions, and other incentives achieve intended behavioral or social-policy goals while avoiding restructuring, inefficiency, and unintended distributional effects.

themes.name: Should tax preferences be judged by whether they achieve their stated social-policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question asks whether subsidies embedded in the tax code remain justified when their actual beneficiaries, effectiveness, or social consequences diverge from their original purposes.

themes.name: Do deductions and exclusions provide a coherent measure of taxable income?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether particular inclusions, exclusions, and deductions have principled justifications or instead distort the tax base and distribute benefits arbitrarily.

themes.name: Do facially neutral tax rules reproduce unequal burdens for disadvantaged groups?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether formally uniform rules generate disparate effects across low-income households, workers, caregivers, or socially marginalized populations.

themes.name: Does the federal income tax meaningfully reduce inequality through progressive redistribution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the actual distributional effects of rates, bases, preferences, and enforcement rather than relying on the nominal progressivity of the tax system.

themes.name: Can tax reform promote economic growth while also reducing inequality?
themes.definition: This question examines whether changes to rates, bases, and preferences can improve investment and resource allocation without worsening unequal wealth and opportunity.

themes.name: Do tax rules encourage taxpayers to restructure transactions primarily to avoid tax?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether formal distinctions, timing rules, and entity structures create incentives for economically motivated taxpayers to alter transactions for tax rather than productive reasons.

themes.name: Should economic substance prevail over formal transaction labels in determining tax consequences?
themes.definition: This question asks whether courts and administrators should disregard legal form when it fails to reflect the economic reality or policy purpose of a transaction.

themes.name: Does tax-system complexity undermine equitable and enforceable taxation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether technical rules, valuation uncertainty, and administrative burdens produce unequal compliance costs, opportunities for avoidance, or loss of legitimacy.

themes.name: Should tax administration prioritize accurate tax collection over taxpayer privacy and other legal values?
themes.definition: This question examines the institutional tradeoffs among transparency, enforcement, procedural fairness, privacy, and protection of public revenue.

themes.name: Should tax rules be interpreted according to underlying policy purposes when statutory language is incomplete or outdated?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the respective roles of statutory text, judicial doctrine, administrative practice, and foundational tax principles in resolving unsettled or technologically changing situations.

themes.name: Are retirement-benefit tax rules adequate to protect the long-term financial security of workers and caregivers?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether the design and distribution of retirement-related tax benefits fairly address differences in earnings, saving capacity, caregiving, and future economic security.

themes.name: Should tax-exempt and nonprofit organizations receive preferential treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether exemptions and deductions for nonprofit activity produce sufficient public benefits to justify their revenue costs and unequal treatment of taxable entities.

themes.name: Should tax-favored transfers and estate-planning strategies be restricted to prevent the concentration of inherited wealth?
themes.definition: This question examines whether wealth-transfer taxes and anti-avoidance rules effectively limit intergenerational inequality without imposing excessive burdens on closely held businesses and other substantial property.

themes.name: Does the federal estate tax effectively achieve its objectives of raising revenue and limiting inherited wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the historical justification, current design, and distributional performance of taxing gratuitous transfers at death.

themes.name: Should the income tax shift more heavily from labor income toward capital income, accumulated wealth, and wealth appreciation?
themes.definition: This question compares the equity, efficiency, and revenue consequences of reducing preferential treatment for investment returns while taxing wealth and capital income more heavily.

themes.name: Is comprehensive income taxation preferable to consumption-oriented taxation?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether taxing returns to saving and investment is more consistent with fairness and revenue goals than relying primarily on consumption taxes or exempting saving returns.

themes.name: Do tax deductions, credits, exemptions, and rate structures distribute benefits according to taxpayers’ ability to pay?
themes.definition: This question evaluates which tax instruments best implement progressive taxation and whether their distributional effects undermine substantive tax equity.

themes.name: Does broadening the tax base produce fairer and more effective reform than changing statutory tax rates alone?
themes.definition: This question examines whether eliminating exclusions, preferences, and other deviations from a comprehensive base improves revenue, progressivity, and neutrality.

themes.name: Do tax preferences achieve their intended social-policy goals without creating regressive benefits and harmful externalities?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether deductions, exclusions, and credits used to promote saving, investment, family security, or other goals work better than direct spending or neutral taxation.

themes.name: Do tax-favored saving and compensation arrangements meaningfully improve long-term household financial security?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether preferential retirement, benefit, and savings mechanisms change financial planning and investment behavior enough to justify their fiscal cost and unequal access.

themes.name: How should joint income taxation treat marriage, divorce, and intra-family income allocation?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax rules governing spouses, divorce settlements, and family transfers fairly allocate income and prevent strategic manipulation while remaining administrable.

themes.name: Do joint filing and marriage penalties unfairly reduce married women’s paid-employment incentives and disadvantage unpaid caregivers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the gendered effects of family-based tax units and considers whether alternative designs can balance equal treatment, work incentives, and support for caregiving.

themes.name: Should tax law treat nontraditional households and family relationships comparably to legally married or single-earner families?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether formal marital and entity classifications accurately reflect economic dependency, family obligations, and the distributive purposes of tax benefits.

themes.name: Does the choice of tax unit or entity create avoidable differences in liability and opportunities for tax planning?
themes.definition: This question studies how individual, household, partnership, corporate, and other classifications affect the allocation of income, ownership, and tax burdens.

themes.name: Do formal legal classifications accurately reflect the economic substance of transactions and relationships for tax purposes?
themes.definition: This question examines when courts and legislatures should disregard statutory or contractual form to tax noncash benefits, structured transactions, compensation, and wealth transfers according to their economic consequences.

themes.name: Can purposive interpretation and anti-avoidance doctrines prevent tax-motivated restructuring without producing overbroad or unpredictable results?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tension between enforcing legislative purpose and preserving legal certainty when taxpayers exploit gaps between formal compliance and economic substance.

themes.name: Do complex tax rules and professional planning give resourceful or wealthy taxpayers advantages unavailable to others?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether complexity, specialized advice, and statutory exceptions weaken uniformity, progressivity, and equal access to tax benefits.

themes.name: Should administrative feasibility and information-reporting capacity limit redistributive tax reform?
themes.definition: This question weighs accurate and equitable taxation against enforcement costs, compliance burdens, institutional capacity, and the practical difficulty of measuring after-tax outcomes.

themes.name: Do tax incentives for saving, investment, and compensation produce economically significant behavior or merely reward decisions taxpayers would have made anyway?
themes.definition: This question tests whether observed household and market responses justify preferential treatment or reveal limits in conventional models of tax-induced behavior.

themes.name: Should personal, investment, and insurance-related losses receive symmetric tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether restrictions or preferences for recognizing different kinds of losses fairly measure economic capacity and avoid opportunities for selective loss shifting.

themes.name: Can income taxation effectively reduce inequality, or should redistribution rely more heavily on direct transfers and welfare programs?
themes.definition: This question compares the distributive, behavioral, and administrative effects of using the tax system versus separate social-welfare mechanisms to support disadvantaged households.

themes.name: Can tax reform simultaneously promote economic growth and reduce inequality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether changes in rates, bases, capital taxation, and targeted benefits can reconcile investment and labor-market incentives with progressive distributional outcomes.

themes.name: How do political institutions, interest groups, public attitudes, and historical path dependence shape the adoption of tax reforms?
themes.definition: This question investigates why politically feasible tax rules may diverge from expert recommendations concerning revenue, progressivity, efficiency, and social welfare.

themes.name: Should the income tax recognize increases in wealth as they accrue, or only when gains are realized?
themes.definition: This question examines whether periodic taxation of economic accretions is preferable to realization-based taxation of sales, exchanges, and other triggering events.

themes.name: Do formal tax classifications produce outcomes that diverge unjustifiably from the economic substance of transactions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax liability should follow the underlying economic benefit, ownership, or burden rather than labels such as gift, exchange, compensation, or expense.

themes.name: Are capital-gains preferences justified by their effects on saving, investment, efficiency, and distributional equity?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether preferential treatment of capital income produces sufficient economic benefits to justify unequal treatment of labor and other income.

themes.name: Do trusts, gifts, bequests, and related transfer-tax rules permit substantial wealth transfers without appropriate taxation?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether specialized transfer-tax provisions and valuation or exclusion rules create loopholes that facilitate intergenerational wealth transmission.

themes.name: Should the federal tax treatment of marriage and family arrangements be redesigned to avoid penalizing or subsidizing particular household forms?
themes.definition: This question compares joint filing, the marital deduction, family-related benefits, and treatment of nontraditional households in light of marriage-related behavior and distributive fairness.

themes.name: How should tax law treat legal recoveries and contingent attorney's fees when a payment contains both compensation and deductible legal costs?
themes.definition: This question concerns the classification, timing, and allocation of taxable income and deductions arising from litigation recoveries and attorney compensation.

themes.name: Should transfers of business interests or property between related parties trigger immediate income recognition?
themes.definition: This question examines recognition, allocation, and timing rules for contributions, exchanges, and other transfers involving family members, controlled entities, or affiliated parties.

themes.name: Is annual taxable income an adequate measure of a taxpayer's economic well-being and ability to pay?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether annual income properly captures wealth, consumption capacity, income volatility, timing, and economically beneficial but excluded receipts.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation reduce inequality without imposing unacceptable efficiency and compliance costs?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tradeoff among progressivity, revenue, labor and investment incentives, administrative feasibility, and distributive justice.

themes.name: Do formally broad tax obligations impose unequal practical burdens on low-income, vulnerable, or otherwise disadvantaged taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether exemptions, caps, enforcement practices, and administrative procedures produce disparate distributional effects despite facially uniform rules.

themes.name: Should wealth taxation rely on broader bases and fewer exemptions despite the administrative and valuation difficulties involved?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether taxing accumulated wealth more comprehensively can improve revenue and equity without creating excessive implementation problems or economic distortions.

themes.name: Do tax deductions, credits, exclusions, and deferrals effectively subsidize socially desirable behavior?
themes.definition: This question asks whether targeted tax preferences achieve their intended behavioral or social-policy objectives more effectively than direct spending or neutral taxation.

themes.name: Do tax incentives and disincentives produce behavioral responses that undermine their revenue or policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question examines taxpayer changes in labor supply, saving, investment, transactions, and avoidance in response to changing tax rates and preferences.

themes.name: Can anti-avoidance rules prevent strategic exploitation without suppressing legitimate transactions or imposing excessive uncertainty?
themes.definition: This question assesses the effectiveness and collateral costs of doctrines and statutory mechanisms aimed at distinguishing avoidance from evasion and protecting the tax base.

themes.name: Should tax administration favor bright-line simplicity or economically precise rules for difficult classification and timing problems?
themes.definition: This question compares administrability, predictability, and enforcement against the risk that categorical rules generate inequitable or economically irrational outcomes.

themes.name: Do tax accounting rules properly match income with economically corresponding costs across time and related taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question concerns duplication, mismatches, deferral, and allocation problems that arise when income and expenses occur in different periods, entities, or stages of a transaction.

themes.name: How should conflicts between specialized tax provisions and general statutory principles be resolved?
themes.definition: This question examines whether courts and administrators should apply specific exceptions rigidly or interpret them in light of the purposes and coherence of the overall tax system.

themes.name: Are federal tax institutions and judicial interpretations adequately authorized to determine the tax treatment of new forms of income and wealth?
themes.definition: This question addresses the allocation of tax authority among Congress, agencies, and courts, including constitutional and statutory limits on federal administration.

themes.name: Does political influence by concentrated wealth undermine the democratic legitimacy and distributive fairness of tax policy?
themes.definition: This question investigates how ideology, organized interests, political narratives, and fiscal politics shape tax legislation and the durability of progressive or redistributive regimes.

themes.name: Do major tax reforms achieve their advertised revenue and distributional goals once taxpayer behavior and indirect effects are considered?
themes.definition: This question evaluates tax reforms by their actual effects on fiscal capacity, inequality, economic behavior, administrative burdens, and unintended consequences rather than by statutory design alone.

themes.name: Should the federal income-tax base include economically valuable receipts and transfers that do not fit conventional income categories?
themes.definition: This question examines whether accessions, nontraditional transfers, recoveries, and other economically valuable receipts should be taxable despite formal classification difficulties.

themes.name: Should labor income and capital income receive different federal tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether differential taxation of wages, human capital, investment returns, and inherited wealth is economically efficient and normatively justified.

themes.name: Should accumulated wealth and unrealized appreciation be taxed before an asset is sold?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether tax liability may appropriately be based on unrealized economic capacity rather than realization through an actual sale or receipt.

themes.name: Should estate and gift taxation be strengthened to reduce wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether federal taxation of large fortunes and inter vivos or testamentary transfers should impose greater burdens to advance redistribution and democratic equality.

themes.name: Does tax progressivity need to be measured by overall effective fiscal burdens rather than statutory income-tax rates?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deductions, credits, transfers, and other tax-benefit interactions substantially alter the progressivity suggested by formal rate schedules.

themes.name: When should distributional equity justify tax rules that reduce economic efficiency?
themes.definition: This question investigates how policymakers should resolve conflicts between redistribution, behavioral incentives, revenue, and productive economic activity.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for savings and investment produce benefits that justify their distributional and revenue costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential treatment for capital preservation, retirement saving, and investment achieves its stated economic objectives without disproportionately benefiting affluent taxpayers.

themes.name: Are tax incentives more effective for pursuing social objectives than direct government subsidies?
themes.definition: This question compares tax-based interventions with direct spending or regulatory alternatives in terms of targeting, behavioral effects, administrative cost, and welfare outcomes.

themes.name: Should deductions and exclusions for personal expenses be replaced with more targeted support for basic needs and work-related costs?
themes.definition: This question examines whether existing treatment of personal expenditures, living costs, and employment-related expenses fairly distinguishes consumption from costs associated with earning income.

themes.name: Does the tax treatment of marriage and family status allocate burdens fairly between spouses and households?
themes.definition: This question evaluates joint taxation, spousal economic interdependence, family benefits, and the gendered distribution of tax burdens within households.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow economic substance rather than formal legal classifications?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether labels, statutory categories, and transaction form produce unjustified differences when economically comparable arrangements have the same substantive function.

themes.name: Do related-party transactions allow affiliated taxpayers to manufacture tax benefits without corresponding economic transfers?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether attribution, characterization, and substance-over-form rules adequately police intra-group transactions designed to shift deductions, income, or other tax advantages.

themes.name: Do realization and timing rules enable taxpayers to defer or avoid progressive taxation?
themes.definition: This question examines how taxpayers exploit the timing of receipts, sales, deductions, and reversals to reduce present tax liability or alter the effective burden.

themes.name: Does tax planning undermine the intended operation of progressive tax rules?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether affluent taxpayers can use legal structures, shelters, and planning strategies to neutralize statutory rates and redistribute tax benefits toward themselves.

themes.name: Should tax benefits be conditioned on compliance with the substantive policy objectives they are intended to promote?
themes.definition: This question asks whether eligibility for exemptions, deductions, or subsidies should depend on actual fulfillment of specified social or economic goals rather than formal qualification alone.

themes.name: Do interactions and complexity within the Internal Revenue Code generate inequitable outcomes that require structural reform?
themes.definition: This question examines whether overlapping provisions, unclear classifications, and implementation burdens produce unintended consequences that piecemeal corrections cannot resolve.

themes.name: Should broad structural tax reform replace narrow, historically inherited preferences and categorical rules?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether a simpler and more uniform tax structure would better align tax consequences with economic substance, revenue needs, and current policy goals.

themes.name: Can a flat-rate or single-rate income tax improve neutrality and simplicity without worsening distributional inequality?
themes.definition: This question compares flat-rate designs with progressive systems on neutrality, compliance, administrative feasibility, revenue, and effects across income groups.

themes.name: How should administrative and legal institutions resolve ambiguous tax rules while preserving fairness and democratic accountability?
themes.definition: This question investigates the respective roles of Congress, the IRS, courts, and legal doctrine in clarifying and enforcing complex or under-specified tax provisions.

themes.name: Do political framing and public perceptions of tax benefits determine the legitimacy of redistributive taxation?
themes.definition: This question examines how narratives about subsidies, loopholes, fairness, punishment, and government intervention shape support for or opposition to tax reforms.

themes.name: Do tax expenditures and targeted tax incentives achieve their intended behavioral and social-policy objectives at an acceptable fiscal cost?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether credits, deductions, exclusions, and other tax subsidies actually change socially valued behavior and whether their benefits justify their revenue and distributional costs.

themes.name: Should the federal tax code replace piecemeal complexity with a simpler and more coherent structure?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether fragmented statutes, reactive legislation, and overlapping rules create administrative burdens and uncertainty that outweigh the benefits of detailed tax treatment.

themes.name: Should tax reform pursue fundamental structural change rather than incremental correction of existing provisions?
themes.definition: This question compares wholesale redesign of the federal tax system with targeted amendments intended to remedy particular defects without disrupting the existing framework.

themes.name: Should tax liability depend on economic substance rather than formal legal classifications?
themes.definition: This question examines whether courts and administrators should determine tax consequences from the underlying economic reality of transactions, ownership, injuries, or payments rather than their legal labels.

themes.name: Do federal tax timing rules accurately measure taxpayers’ economic income and ability to pay?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether realization, deferral, accrual, and deduction-timing rules produce fair tax burdens when economic benefits arise before or after cash is received.

themes.name: How should tax law coordinate deductions, losses, and later income or economic benefits across tax years and taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question examines whether mismatches between deductions and corresponding income or benefits create unwarranted tax advantages or inequitable burdens.

themes.name: Should specialized tax planning and entity structures be limited when they exploit formal rules to avoid tax or obtain unintended benefits?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legitimacy of tax engineering, taxpayer choice, and anti-abuse doctrines when planning strategies erode the tax base or undermine statutory purposes.

themes.name: How should courts, the IRS, and lawmakers resolve ambiguity when statutory tax classifications conflict with broader policy purposes?
themes.definition: This question concerns the appropriate division between statutory interpretation, administrative practice, and legislative reform in determining eligibility for tax relief.

themes.name: Are deductions and exclusions more equitable and effective than refundable credits or direct public assistance?
themes.definition: This question compares tax-based subsidies with credits, cash transfers, and other forms of government support in terms of distribution, incentives, dignity, and administrative implementation.

themes.name: Do deductions and exclusions distribute tax benefits fairly across taxpayers with different incomes and economic resources?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether preferential treatment embedded in the income-tax base disproportionately benefits affluent taxpayers or produces unjustified differences in effective tax burdens.

themes.name: Should marital-status and family-based tax rules be redesigned to avoid penalizing economically vulnerable spouses, parents, or nontraditional households?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether filing-status, marriage, divorce, and intrafamily-transfer rules reflect actual household resources and distribute tax burdens fairly among family structures.

themes.name: Should federal tax policy recognize unpaid, historically devalued, or gendered forms of household labor?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax rules disadvantage nonearning spouses, caregivers, and economically vulnerable women by treating only market income and formal contributions as economically significant.

themes.name: Should the United States tax capital gains more like ordinary income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential capital-gains rates are justified by investment, realization, and efficiency concerns or instead produce inequitable advantages and undermine progressivity.

themes.name: Should appreciated property receive a basis step-up at death?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether the interaction of income taxation, estate taxation, and death-time transfers should preserve, eliminate, or modify the basis adjustment for unrealized gains.

themes.name: Can wealth-transfer taxation effectively reduce intergenerational concentration of wealth without excessive avoidance and administrative costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legitimacy, design, and practical effectiveness of estate, inheritance, and gift taxes as tools for limiting accumulated economic power.

themes.name: Should progressive taxation be expanded to reduce wealth and income inequality despite possible effects on investment and economic growth?
themes.definition: This question weighs redistribution from affluent taxpayers against efficiency, investment, political feasibility, and the risk that taxpayers will alter behavior or avoid tax.

themes.name: Is an income-tax base preferable to a consumption-tax base for achieving fairness and economic efficiency?
themes.definition: This question compares income and consumption taxation with respect to saving, investment, distribution, administrative feasibility, and the taxation of accumulated wealth.

themes.name: Should tax policy influence private behavior, such as homeownership, investment, employment, or retirement saving, rather than primarily raise revenue?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legitimacy and effectiveness of using tax provisions to direct resource allocation and encourage behaviors favored by public policy.

themes.name: Do tax rules governing personal-injury recoveries correctly distinguish taxable economic gain from restoration of a pre-injury position?
themes.definition: This question examines the scope of the section 104(a)(2) exclusion and related rules for determining whether nonphysical injury recoveries constitute income.

themes.name: Should tax rules governing attorney compensation and assigned income follow the person who earned the underlying economic benefit or the person who legally receives payment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates assignment-of-income principles and fee arrangements where formal payment structures diverge from the taxpayer’s substantive contribution or entitlement.

themes.name: How much should administrative feasibility constrain the design of a normatively fair tax system?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether complexity, enforcement capacity, compliance costs, and institutional convenience justify retaining tax rules that are economically or distributionally imperfect.

themes.name: Does progressive income taxation reduce inequality without imposing unjustified economic costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the normative justification and distributive effects of progressive rates and tax burdens relative to their effects on efficiency, labor, saving, and investment.

themes.name: Should tax burdens be based on ability to pay rather than realized income alone?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the tax base should account for economically relevant resources such as wealth, imputed income, or unrealized appreciation instead of relying primarily on realization.

themes.name: Do tax preferences disproportionately benefit wealthy taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether exclusions, deductions, credits, exemptions, and preferential rates distribute public benefits upward and thereby undermine horizontal or vertical equity.
