themes.definition: This question asks whether timing rules should adjust for deferral, discounting, and interest so that economically equivalent transactions receive comparable tax treatment.

themes.name: Do tax deferral and nonrecognition rules efficiently encourage saving and investment, or do they mainly create planning opportunities?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether postponing tax on investment transactions or savings produces productive economic benefits sufficient to justify its revenue cost and unequal access.

themes.name: Who should be taxed when compensation or service income is routed through a separate entity?
themes.definition: This question examines whether income should be attributed to the service provider, the entity, or another recipient when entity structures separate legal ownership from the performance generating the income.

themes.name: Do progressive tax rates achieve redistribution without creating economically harmful distortions in work, saving, and investment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tradeoff between progressive burden-sharing and behavioral responses that may reduce efficiency or alter resource allocation.

themes.name: Does formally neutral tax policy impose disproportionate burdens on racial, demographic, or otherwise disadvantaged groups?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether facially uniform rules reproduce structural inequality through differences in income, wealth, household structure, or access to tax benefits.

themes.name: Should tax policy pursue social and behavioral objectives beyond revenue collection and efficiency?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legitimacy and effectiveness of using tax provisions to promote work, investment, family support, private transfers, or other social goals.

themes.name: Can tax rules be made sufficiently precise to reflect economic differences without becoming too complex to administer and comply with?
themes.definition: This question addresses the central tradeoff between accurate, equitable liability calculations and simplicity, transparency, enforcement capacity, and compliance costs.

themes.name: Should ambiguous tax statutes be interpreted according to statutory purpose and the coherence of the tax system rather than rigid textual or formal rules?
themes.definition: This question examines how courts and administrators should resolve uncertainty when literal interpretation conflicts with legislative purpose, economic substance, or broader tax principles.

themes.name: Should the federal income-tax base be broadened by reducing categorical exclusions and special preferences?
themes.definition: This question examines whether a broader, more uniform definition of income would improve neutrality, fairness, revenue, and coherence compared with the existing system of exclusions and preferences.

themes.name: Is realization-based taxation adequate for taxing unrealized appreciation and accumulated wealth?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether income tax should continue to defer taxation of gains until realization or instead tax unrealized appreciation and other forms of accumulated wealth.

themes.name: How should gifts, inheritances, and other intergenerational wealth transfers be taxed to limit wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question considers whether transfer-tax rules and exemptions reduce or reinforce concentrated wealth and how they should be redesigned.

themes.name: Are preferential tax rates and exclusions for capital income justified by efficiency or fairness?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether favorable treatment of investment, property-derived, and other capital returns is defensible despite its effects on the tax base and distribution of wealth.

themes.name: Do retirement-savings tax preferences increase socially valuable saving or primarily subsidize affluent taxpayers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the behavioral, distributional, and revenue effects of deductions, exclusions, and other preferences for retirement and investment saving.

themes.name: Does progressive income taxation fairly allocate burdens according to taxpayers’ ability to pay?
themes.definition: This question examines whether progressive rates promote distributive justice or instead create horizontal inequities and unequal treatment among taxpayers with comparable resources.

themes.name: Do tax preferences and deductions produce justified incentives or unjustified distributional distortions?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether targeted benefits achieve legitimate policy objectives or mainly generate inequitable subsidies, inefficient behavior, and erosion of the tax base.

themes.name: Should tax benefits be broadly available or targeted more narrowly to households most in need?
themes.definition: This question compares universal or widely available deductions and credits with targeted benefits intended to provide progressive relief and reduce poverty.

themes.name: Does the joint income-tax return treat married and unmarried taxpayers fairly?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether joint filing creates marriage bonuses or penalties and whether family-based tax units produce equitable treatment of similarly situated households.

themes.name: How should family circumstances, caregiving, and household labor affect individual tax liability?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax rules adequately account for dependents, unpaid care, gendered household labor, and legally recognized family relationships.

themes.name: Can tax policy reduce economic inequality and poverty without undermining autonomy and work incentives?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tradeoff between redistributive taxation or transfers and the incentives, independence, and behavioral responses of taxpayers.

themes.name: Do tax and transfer programs effectively reach their intended beneficiaries and improve economic security?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether fiscal benefits, welfare-linked tax provisions, and safety-net programs deliver meaningful support to low-income households, children, and other vulnerable groups.

themes.name: How should tax rules balance revenue collection with the affordability of healthcare, disability support, and care?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax treatment of healthcare expenditures, disability, and caregiving adequately supports basic needs without creating incoherent or regressive incentives.

themes.name: Should taxation pursue social and behavioral goals beyond raising revenue?
themes.definition: This question examines the legitimacy and effectiveness of using tax instruments to promote preferred conduct, redistribute resources, or remedy discrimination rather than simply finance government.

themes.name: Do tax incentives change saving, investment, and other economic behavior enough to justify their complexity and distributional costs?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether taxpayer responses to rates, deductions, and preferences materially advance policy goals or instead create inefficient distortions.

themes.name: Can anti-avoidance rules prevent abusive tax planning without penalizing legitimate economic arrangements?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the boundary between lawful planning and avoidance or evasion, including whether substance-over-form doctrines and anti-abuse mechanisms impose fair liabilities.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow economic substance rather than formal legal ownership, labels, or accounting categories?
themes.definition: This question examines how classification rules should treat economically related transactions, obligations, property interests, and atypical arrangements when formal categories produce inaccurate results.

themes.name: How should nontraditional receipts, recoveries, and personal-injury awards be classified as taxable income?
themes.definition: This question addresses when compensatory payments, settlements, recoveries, and other unconventional receipts should enter the income-tax base and how they should be characterized.

themes.name: Can tax reform improve equity and accuracy without making administration and compliance unmanageable?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tradeoff between theoretically correct or substantively fair tax outcomes and rules that are simple, predictable, enforceable, and inexpensive to administer.

themes.name: Would replacing or supplementing the income tax with a consumption tax improve fairness and economic efficiency?
themes.definition: This question compares income- and consumption-tax regimes with respect to distribution, incentives, revenue, administration, and the treatment of savings and wealth.

themes.name: Should unrealized gains and other unearned increases in wealth be included in the federal income-tax base?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the realization rule, valuation difficulties, and liquidity concerns justify excluding appreciation in assets until a later taxable event.

themes.name: Should economically equivalent transactions receive the same tax treatment despite differences in their formal legal classification?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax law should privilege economic substance over labels such as sale, gift, loan, compensation, or investment.

themes.name: Do tax exclusions, deductions, and other preferences provide effective public benefits or mainly create inequitable subsidies?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether tax expenditures achieve their stated economic or social objectives and whether their benefits are distributed fairly across taxpayers.

themes.name: Can politically feasible progressive taxation of high incomes, wealth, or wealth transfers be designed without triggering unacceptable avoidance or mobility responses?
themes.definition: This question connects the distributive case for greater burdens on wealthy taxpayers with political opposition, taxpayer mobility, and behavioral responses.

themes.name: Is the estate tax an effective and appropriately designed instrument for addressing inherited wealth and intergenerational inequality?
themes.definition: This question examines the estate tax’s relationship to wealth concentration, estate-planning structures, valuation, liquidity pressures, and economic growth.

themes.name: Does the federal income tax accurately measure ability to pay when taxpayers face substantial personal, family, or misfortune-related costs?
themes.definition: This question considers whether taxable income adequately reflects the practical resources available to taxpayers after necessary expenses and hardship.

themes.name: Should capital income, labor income, saving, borrowing, and debt-financed investment receive different tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether distinctions among returns to labor, capital, saving, and borrowing are justified by equity, efficiency, or behavioral considerations.

themes.name: Do marriage, family, and household-based tax rules distribute burdens and benefits fairly across different household structures?
themes.definition: This question investigates joint filing, spousal arrangements, children, nontraditional couples, and other household classifications that affect tax liability and eligibility for benefits.

themes.name: How should federal taxation interact with Social Security, Medicare, and other social-insurance programs?
themes.definition: This question examines the financing, eligibility, and distributional relationship between tax rules and government-supported social protection.

themes.name: Do tax incentives and income-support programs change work, saving, investment, or other private behavior in ways that undermine their policy goals?
themes.definition: This question tests whether behavioral responses, including reduced work or altered investment choices, change the real effectiveness and fairness of tax-based interventions.

themes.name: Are legally permitted tax avoidance strategies and structural loopholes consistent with taxpayers’ obligation to pay their fair share?
themes.definition: This question addresses the normative and practical boundary between lawful planning, aggressive avoidance, evasion, and effective anti-avoidance enforcement.

themes.name: How should tax law allocate gains, deductions, losses, and recoveries across different tax years?
themes.definition: This question evaluates timing rules when income or economic benefits arise in one period while related costs, losses, or recoveries occur in another.

themes.name: Do categorical distinctions in the tax code violate horizontal equity by treating economically similar taxpayers or receipts differently?
themes.definition: This question examines whether formal categories based on source, form, timing, or legal status produce unjustified unequal treatment among comparable economic situations.

themes.name: Can tax systems preserve substantive equity and policy effectiveness while reducing complexity and administrative costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tradeoff between sophisticated tax rules and the burdens of compliance, enforcement, interpretation, and implementation.

themes.name: Is incremental reform of the existing federal income tax preferable to replacing it with a substantially different tax system?
themes.definition: This question compares amendment, simplification, and structural redesign against alternative income-tax models while considering revenue, legitimacy, and administrability.

themes.name: How should tax reform balance distributive equity, economic efficiency, revenue protection, and administrative feasibility?
themes.definition: This question evaluates competing criteria for choosing among tax-base, rate, incentive, and enforcement reforms.

themes.name: Should tax policy be justified primarily by ability to pay, broader social welfare, or other theories of distributive justice?
themes.definition: This question compares competing normative foundations for assigning tax burdens and determining when departures from neutrality or equal treatment are legitimate.

themes.name: Does the gap between expert tax analysis and public understanding undermine tax legitimacy, compliance, and reform?
themes.definition: This question examines how public knowledge, trust, professional expertise, and perceived fairness influence taxpayer behavior and political support for tax policy.

themes.name: How do political and institutional constraints determine whether proposed tax and welfare reforms become operative?
themes.definition: This question studies the effects of legislative coalitions, entrenched provisions, administrative capacity, and public opposition on the adoption and implementation of reform.

themes.name: How should federal tax law handle conflicts between federal classifications, state-law categories, and taxpayer mobility?
themes.definition: This question examines how differing legal classifications, interstate competition, and taxpayer movement affect tax liability, property assessment, and governments’ ability to tax economic resources.

themes.name: When statutory text is incomplete or ambiguous, are judicial and administrative tax doctrines legally legitimate and sufficiently predictable?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether nonstatutory rules, judicial doctrines, and administrative practices are grounded in legislative authority and provide coherent guidance for disputed tax outcomes.

themes.name: Does realization-based income taxation unfairly defer or exclude taxation of gains and other accessions to wealth?
themes.definition: This question examines whether taxing income only upon realization, while excluding noncash benefits, unrealized appreciation, or returns of capital, creates inequities and economic distortions.

themes.name: Should capital gains receive preferential or deferred tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential rates and deferral for capital gains are justified by investment incentives, the time value of money, and economic growth despite their distributional costs.

themes.name: How should tax law distinguish taxable income from the recovery or preservation of capital?
themes.definition: This question concerns the classification of receipts, losses, and payments as income rather than nontaxable returns of capital or recoveries of previously incurred costs.

themes.name: Do tax deductions, exclusions, and credits achieve their stated social objectives without producing inequitable distributional effects?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax preferences generate intended benefits or instead disproportionately assist higher-income taxpayers and distort economic decisions.

themes.name: Should tax preferences be limited when taxpayers can avoid or offset their intended effects?
themes.definition: This question examines whether statutory caps, phaseouts, and other limits are needed to control the scope, cost, and unintended consequences of deductions, exclusions, and credits.

themes.name: Can anti-avoidance doctrines prevent abusive tax planning without denying relief for genuine economic losses or transactions?
themes.definition: This question addresses the balance between substance-over-form rules, judicial doctrines, and statutory anti-abuse provisions on one hand and legitimate tax planning on the other.

themes.name: Do gaps and asymmetries in tax rules allow wealthy taxpayers to circumvent redistributive objectives?
themes.definition: This question investigates how mismatches, loopholes, and legally engineered financial arrangements reduce intended tax burdens or preserve tax benefits.

themes.name: Should tax law classify economically similar receipts, expenditures, and transactions consistently despite different legal forms?
themes.definition: This question tests whether formal categories adequately capture substantive economic relationships or instead produce arbitrary differences in tax treatment.

themes.name: Does the federal tax system treat taxpayers with equal nominal incomes as genuinely equal for horizontal-equity purposes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether differences in family status, expenses, wealth, support obligations, or economic circumstances justify departures from equal treatment of nominally similar taxpayers.

themes.name: Should federal tax law recognize family relationships and household costs when determining tax liability?
themes.definition: This question examines how marriage, caregiving, intrafamily support, and family-related expenditures should affect income-tax burdens and household economic security.

themes.name: Do ostensibly gender-neutral tax rules reproduce gender hierarchy or disadvantage people outside traditional family and work arrangements?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether tax classifications retain coverture-era assumptions or impose unequal burdens on women, caregivers, nontraditional families, and workers outside standard employment.

themes.name: Does the earned income tax credit effectively support low-income workers without excessively privileging labor-market participation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether refundable work-based credits improve income security and employment while respecting autonomy and avoiding disadvantages for people unable to engage in market work.

themes.name: Should tax and welfare policy prioritize labor-market participation over economic security and personal autonomy?
themes.definition: This question compares work-oriented tax benefits and conditions with unconditional or broader income-support approaches for low-income households.

themes.name: Do tax-financed social-benefit programs deliver redistribution more effectively and fairly than direct government spending?
themes.definition: This question examines the administrative, distributional, and behavioral consequences of using the tax system to administer subsidies, transfers, retirement support, or other social programs.

themes.name: Should progressive taxation and wealth-transfer taxes play a larger role in reducing income and wealth inequality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether greater burdens on high-income and wealthy households are justified as a response to concentrated income, inherited wealth, and unequal economic security.

themes.name: Do estate and gift tax rules effectively prevent lifetime transfers and estate-planning strategies from eroding transfer-tax progressivity?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether intrafamily transfers, estate freezes, exemptions, and other planning techniques preserve or undermine the redistributive purposes of wealth-transfer taxation.

themes.name: Should the estate-and-gift-tax system be substantially redesigned to better reflect economic wealth transfers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether existing transfer-tax classifications, valuation rules, and administrative mechanisms adequately capture the policy consequences of transferring wealth during life or at death.

themes.name: Do tax rates and targeted incentives improve resource allocation enough to justify their behavioral distortions?
themes.definition: This question assesses how tax design affects labor supply, saving, investment, consumption, and other economic choices relative to its revenue and distributive benefits.

themes.name: Can tax reform improve fairness and economic efficiency without making avoidance or administration substantially worse?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether proposed structural reforms can reconcile distributional goals, neutral incentives, enforcement, compliance costs, and political feasibility.

themes.name: Does tax-law complexity undermine substantive fairness more than it improves precision and administrability?
themes.definition: This question examines whether detailed rules, fragmented provisions, and technical classifications produce arbitrary outcomes and conceal distributional effects despite making administration more predictable.

themes.name: Should tax rules use flexible, context-sensitive standards rather than fixed statutory classifications?
themes.definition: This question compares administrable bright-line rules with interpretive and judicial standards designed to respond to economically diverse transactions and changing institutional conditions.

themes.name: Do judicial and administrative interpretations of ambiguous tax provisions preserve statutory purposes or create inconsistent taxpayer outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates how courts, the IRS, and other legal institutions determine the reach of tax benefits and resolve conflicts between textual, formal, and functional approaches.

themes.name: Should the corporate income tax be fundamentally redesigned to align taxation with economic policy goals?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the existing corporate tax appropriately addresses revenue, investment incentives, entity-level taxation, avoidance, and the distribution of burdens between corporations and individuals.

themes.name: How should authority over tax administration and revenue collection be divided between federal and state governments?
themes.definition: This question examines whether intergovernmental allocations of taxing power and administrative responsibility promote coherent policy, accountability, and equitable fiscal governance.

themes.name: Does public trust in tax institutions affect compliance and the legitimacy of redistributive taxation?
themes.definition: This question explores whether perceptions of fairness, governmental competence, and fiscal legitimacy influence taxpayer behavior and acceptance of revenue-raising and social-benefit policies.

themes.name: Does perceived fairness of tax rules increase voluntary taxpayer compliance?
themes.definition: This question examines whether taxpayers’ judgments about fairness, legitimacy, and equal treatment affect compliance independently of the formal economic incentives created by tax law.

themes.name: Should progressive taxation be strengthened to reduce inequality and counter the limited progressivity of the federal tax system?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether higher burdens on wealthy taxpayers and stronger redistribution are justified in light of distributional effects, regressive effective rates, and political resistance.

themes.name: Should the United States replace or substantially restructure income taxation in favor of consumption or accretion-based taxation?
themes.definition: This question compares alternative tax bases by assessing their effects on equity, saving, investment, administration, revenue, and economic behavior.

themes.name: Should accumulated wealth and capital income be taxed differently from labor income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether separate or preferential treatment of wealth, investment returns, and inherited capital is defensible under contemporary economic conditions.

themes.name: How should tax deferral and strategic realization of investment gains be reformed to improve equity?
themes.definition: This question examines whether taxpayers’ ability to postpone recognition or selectively realize gains creates unjustified advantages and how timing rules should respond.

themes.name: Do estate and gift tax rules appropriately distinguish transfers made for consideration from gratuitous transfers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legal and policy justification for different treatment of gifts, inheritances, estate transfers, and property received outside ordinary earnings.

themes.name: Do estate-planning structures and basis rules permit affluent taxpayers to avoid transfer taxes beyond the policy justification for those benefits?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether planning devices, nonrecognition rules, and basis adjustments undermine the intended taxation of intergenerational wealth transfers.

themes.name: Should tax law treat nontraditional families and economically interdependent household members comparably to married or single-earner families?
themes.definition: This question examines whether household filing, transfer, deduction, and benefit rules produce unjustified disparities among families with different legal, caregiving, and work arrangements.

themes.name: Do tax-and-transfer programs distribute assistance fairly across households with different incomes, wealth, and family circumstances?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether subsidies, credits, deductions, and related public benefits reach economically vulnerable households equitably rather than disproportionately benefiting higher-income recipients.

themes.name: Are tax preferences effective and justified instruments for pursuing social and economic policy goals?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether benefits enacted for saving, investment, housing, retirement, affordability, or other non-revenue purposes achieve their stated objectives relative to direct spending or generally applicable rules.

themes.name: Do targeted tax incentives create excessive complexity, fiscal cost, and distortion compared with uniform alternatives?
themes.definition: This question examines whether specialized preferences are sufficiently effective to justify their administrative burdens, budgetary costs, planning opportunities, and unequal access.

themes.name: Where should the boundary of taxable income be drawn through exclusions, deductions, credits, and deferral?
themes.definition: This question evaluates which receipts and expenditures belong in the tax base and whether preferential treatment reflects genuine income measurement or disguised subsidy.

themes.name: Should expenses associated with producing income be deducted immediately, capitalized, or left nondeductible?
themes.definition: This question addresses how tax law should classify costs that generate benefits over time while balancing accurate income measurement, fairness, administrability, and incentives.

themes.name: Do formal tax classifications accurately capture the underlying economic relationships and events they regulate?
themes.definition: This question challenges categorical legal distinctions involving income, ownership, payments, taxpayers, and taxable events when those distinctions diverge from economic substance.

themes.name: When should economically equivalent transactions receive equivalent tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the limits of formal tax equivalence and asks whether related taxpayers, financial arrangements, or legally different transactions should be coordinated under substantive neutrality principles.

themes.name: How should tax law distinguish legitimate tax planning from abusive avoidance?
themes.definition: This question examines the appropriate legal and institutional limits on technically valid strategies, substance-disguising transactions, and anti-avoidance rules that may burden compliant taxpayers.

themes.name: Do tax rules produce inequitable outcomes for disadvantaged groups despite facial neutrality?
themes.definition: This question uses distributional, identity-based, and critical analysis to assess whether apparently neutral classifications impose structural disadvantages based on status, wealth, gender, or family role.

themes.name: Can retirement-plan tax preferences provide equitable financial security across differently situated workers and families?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether retirement exclusions, deductions, contribution limits, and safeguards distribute benefits fairly and effectively protect older or lower-income households.

themes.name: Does the complexity of tax-based benefit programs undermine their accessibility and policy effectiveness?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether eligibility conditions, overlapping provisions, compliance costs, and administrative rules prevent intended beneficiaries from receiving statutory assistance.

themes.name: Should federal tax reform replace piecemeal provisions with a more coherent and administrable system?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether structural reform or selective amendment is preferable given existing legal commitments, implementation costs, administrative capacity, political feasibility, and competing equity goals.

themes.name: Should the federal income tax move beyond realization-based taxation toward a broader measure of economic income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether increases in wealth, including noncash and unrealized gains, should be taxed as income rather than waiting for a conventional sale or receipt.

themes.name: Do current basis, capitalization, and recognition rules allow economically real gains to escape taxation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether rules governing basis adjustments, deductions, amortization, and deferred recognition produce inappropriate omissions or distortions in taxable income.

themes.name: How should capital gains and appreciated property be taxed when assets are transferred at death?
themes.definition: This question considers the interaction between income taxation, estate taxation, basis rules, and preferential treatment of appreciated property at death.

themes.name: Should wealth taxation supplement or replace portions of the federal income and transfer-tax systems?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether taxing accumulated wealth can reduce dynastic concentration and raise revenue more effectively or fairly than income taxation alone.

themes.name: Does the progressive income-tax structure distribute burdens according to ability to pay without imposing unacceptable economic costs?
themes.definition: This question assesses the equity, behavioral, administrative, and political consequences of progressive rates, thresholds, and exemptions.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for capital income and affluent taxpayers undermine the progressivity of the federal tax system?
themes.definition: This question examines whether preferential treatment of investment returns, wealth transfers, and high-income taxpayers shifts burdens toward less affluent households.

themes.name: Should deductions be replaced or supplemented by refundable credits to make tax benefits more equitable?
themes.definition: This question compares deductions, credits, and other tax-based mechanisms as instruments for delivering benefits across taxpayers with different incomes and marginal tax rates.

themes.name: Do tax expenditures function as poorly targeted substitutes for direct social assistance?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether exclusions, deductions, credits, and subsidies deliver social benefits to those most in need or disproportionately advantage resource-rich taxpayers.

themes.name: Should tax rules treat married couples and households differently when earnings and unpaid labor are unequally distributed?
themes.definition: This question analyzes marriage penalties, household taxation, unequal earnings, and family labor under competing ideals of neutrality and distributive fairness.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for traditional family structures reproduce gendered or heteronormative inequality?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether family-based tax classifications and benefits disadvantage households that do not conform to traditional marital or gender arrangements.

themes.name: Should tax policy explicitly address racial, gender, and resource-based inequality rather than rely on formally uniform income categories?
themes.definition: This question tests whether formally neutral tax rules produce unequal effects and whether targeted tax treatment is justified for structurally disadvantaged groups.

themes.name: How should payments for support, insurance, care, or substitute rights be classified for income-tax purposes?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether nontraditional receipts and third-party payments should be included in taxable income based on their economic function rather than their formal label.

themes.name: Should tax law follow economic substance rather than formal legal classifications in commercial and family transactions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether courts and administrators should look to underlying economic relationships when statutory categories do not fit new transactions or social arrangements.

themes.name: Do timing and character rules create opportunities for taxpayers to shift income, losses, or asset transfers strategically?
themes.definition: This question examines tax trading, installment and contingent payments, business sales, liquidation, and intertemporal recognition as sources of avoidance or economic distortion.

themes.name: Is the federal gift tax necessary to prevent taxpayers from avoiding estate taxation through lifetime transfers?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether gift-tax rules appropriately limit tax-motivated transfers of income-producing or wealth-bearing assets within families.

themes.name: Are tax rules sufficiently neutral across saving, borrowing, investment, consumption, and labor choices?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether differences in tax treatment create economically coherent incentives or induce inefficient shifts in work, saving, risk-taking, and investment.

themes.name: Can targeted tax incentives effectively promote education and other socially valued investments without producing inequitable subsidies?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax-favored arrangements improve access to education or socially important services and whether their benefits reach intended recipients.

themes.name: Should retirement-related tax benefits be redesigned to provide greater protection for lower-income and vulnerable workers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether existing retirement exclusions, deductions, and subsidies distribute income security fairly across workers with different resources and employment circumstances.

themes.name: How much complexity and administrative discretion is justified to prevent avoidance and preserve equitable tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question weighs administrability, predictability, anti-avoidance enforcement, categorical rules, and taxpayer usability against the benefits of more precise tax liability.

themes.name: Can courts, agencies, and legislatures reform ambiguous or outdated tax rules without exceeding legal authority or losing political legitimacy?
themes.definition: This question investigates how statutory text, judicial interpretation, administrative implementation, public perceptions, and political power shape the development and feasibility of tax reform.

themes.name: Should the income tax recognize unrealized appreciation, or should the realization principle continue to defer taxation until an asset is sold or otherwise disposed of?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether realization-based taxation accurately measures economic income or instead creates inequities, deferral opportunities, and distortions in investment behavior.

themes.name: Do existing rules adequately distinguish taxable income from returns of capital, restoration of an asset, and other economically non-income receipts?
themes.definition: This question examines whether income-tax concepts correctly identify economically meaningful gain without taxing the recovery of a taxpayer's own capital.

themes.name: Do deductions, exclusions, and preferential rates undermine the intended income-tax base more than they advance legitimate policy goals?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether departures from a comprehensive tax base create unjustified tax preferences, deferral, or opportunities for avoidance.

themes.name: Should investment and capital income continue to receive more favorable tax treatment than labor income?
themes.definition: This question weighs the efficiency, savings, and investment arguments for preferential capital taxation against concerns about equity and wealth concentration.

themes.name: Would replacing the progressive income tax with a consumption-based, flat-rate, or accretion-based system produce fairer and more efficient outcomes?
themes.definition: This question compares alternative tax bases and rate structures in terms of distribution, economic incentives, administrative feasibility, and revenue.

themes.name: Does progressive income taxation reduce inequality without imposing excessive costs on economic efficiency, autonomy, and revenue generation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the normative and behavioral tradeoffs involved in using graduated rates to redistribute income.

themes.name: Do tax-based benefits and subsidies distribute public assistance less equitably than direct spending programs?
themes.definition: This question compares tax expenditures with direct government programs, focusing on access, regressivity, administrative burden, and achievement of social objectives.

themes.name: Are targeted tax deductions and credits effective incentives for the socially preferred behavior they are intended to promote?
themes.definition: This question asks whether particular tax incentives change behavior enough to justify their fiscal cost and distributional consequences.

themes.name: Does tax-law complexity prevent incentives and subsidies from achieving their intended policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question examines whether technical eligibility rules, compliance costs, and uncertainty reduce the effectiveness of otherwise justified tax preferences.

themes.name: Should tax reform prioritize administrability and political feasibility over a theoretically comprehensive and economically ideal tax system?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the institutional tradeoff between normatively attractive tax rules and rules that taxpayers, administrators, and legislators can realistically implement.

themes.name: Would simplifying fragmented income-tax, estate-tax, or rate-structure rules improve coherence without sacrificing important distributional or behavioral goals?
themes.definition: This question tests whether structural simplification produces better policy outcomes than incremental and increasingly complex reforms.

themes.name: Do anti-avoidance rules regulate the actual source of a tax advantage, or do they impose excessive uncertainty and overbreadth on legitimate tax planning?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether specialized doctrines and statutory safeguards effectively target abusive arrangements while preserving lawful economic activity.

themes.name: Should tax law neutralize differences among economically equivalent transactions, employment payments, or financing arrangements created by formal legal structure?
themes.definition: This question examines whether legal form should determine tax consequences when arrangements have substantially identical economic effects.

themes.name: Do tax rules governing business expenses, interest deductions, and capital transactions allocate deductions consistently with the underlying economic activity?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether expense and financing rules distinguish appropriately among personal consumption, business investment, and investment returns.

themes.name: Do tax incentives for corporate investment in factories, infrastructure, and productive capital generate benefits large enough to justify their revenue and distributional costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether investment subsidies improve capital formation and economic activity or primarily reward investments that would have occurred anyway.

themes.name: Should federal tax law preserve preferential treatment for marriage and traditional family structures?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether joint filing, marital benefits, and family-based classifications reflect legitimate policy objectives or privilege particular household forms.

themes.name: Do tax and social-insurance rules equitably address gendered divisions of paid work, unpaid caregiving, and parenting?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax treatment of marriage, children, caregiving, and labor-force participation reinforces or alleviates gender and household inequalities.

themes.name: Do formally neutral tax rules reproduce racial, class-based, or other structural inequalities in the distribution of tax burdens and benefits?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax classifications and ostensibly equal rules generate systematically unequal outcomes for economically or socially differentiated groups.

themes.name: Should gift and estate taxes be redesigned to limit family wealth concentration while preserving legitimate intergenerational transfers and administrable estate planning?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the equity, complexity, valuation, and behavioral consequences of taxing gratuitous transfers and estate-freezing strategies.

themes.name: Do tax-favored retirement savings programs effectively promote retirement security, or do they disproportionately subsidize higher-income savers?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether retirement tax preferences achieve broad savings and welfare objectives despite unequal access, complex rules, and regressive benefits.

themes.name: Should federal income taxation include unrealized appreciation in property rather than defer taxation until realization?
themes.definition: This question examines whether basis and realization rules fairly measure economic gains or improperly permit appreciation to escape or defer taxation.

themes.name: Should the federal income-tax base follow a comprehensive Haig-Simons concept of income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether taxable income should include all economically meaningful increases in wealth, including noncash, contingent, substituted, or difficult-to-value receipts.

themes.name: Should the substantive economic function of a payment control its tax treatment rather than its formal legal label?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether tax law should classify receipts, expenses, recoveries, and transfers according to economic substance when formal categories produce unequal outcomes.

themes.name: Should labor income, capital income, inheritances, and other unearned receipts receive different tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the normative and efficiency justifications for distinguishing among income sources when assigning tax burdens.

themes.name: Should the federal tax system impose greater burdens on high-income and high-wealth taxpayers to reflect ability to pay?
themes.definition: This question examines whether progressive taxation and targeted burdens on affluent taxpayers are justified by unequal resources, welfare, and economic power.

themes.name: Do facially neutral tax rules and preferences reproduce socioeconomic inequality?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether formally uniform deductions, credits, exclusions, and classifications disproportionately benefit affluent or socially advantaged taxpayers.

themes.name: Should tax deductions and credits be redesigned so that their benefits do not rise with taxpayers’ marginal tax rates?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether subsidies should be refundable, capped, or otherwise structured to distribute assistance more evenly across income levels.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for saving and investment promote capital formation enough to justify their distributional costs?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether preferential treatment of savings, investment returns, and capital contributions increases national saving and productive investment or mainly subsidizes existing wealth.

themes.name: Should tax law remain neutral toward taxpayers’ economic and personal decisions, or should it deliberately encourage socially desirable behavior?
themes.definition: This question weighs behavioral incentives for housing, saving, family formation, employment, and other activities against the distortions and autonomy costs created by nonneutral taxation.

themes.name: Should married couples be taxed through joint returns or individual filing?
themes.definition: This question examines whether marital filing rules fairly account for shared resources, marriage penalties or bonuses, and differences among household arrangements.

themes.name: Should the tax code treat the family as an economic unit while accommodating diverse caregiving and dependency arrangements?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether family-based tax treatment, child benefits, and care-related provisions accurately reflect household resources without privileging conventional family forms.

themes.name: Should tax policy supplement existing welfare programs or replace them with tax-based income support?
themes.definition: This question compares tax credits and deductions with direct transfers as instruments for reducing poverty, financing social welfare, and reaching intended beneficiaries.

themes.name: Do tax rules adequately recognize disability, caregiving costs, and other forms of reduced economic capacity?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether existing exclusions, deductions, and benefits address the actual financial effects of disability and care rather than relying on incoherent categorical rules.

themes.name: Should estate and gift taxes be strengthened to limit intergenerational concentration of wealth and power?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether transfer taxation fairly captures family wealth transfers, prevents accumulated wealth from escaping taxation, and advances distributive goals.

themes.name: Do anti-avoidance rules target the actual source of abusive tax advantages without denying relief for genuine economic losses or transfers?
themes.definition: This question examines whether targeted anti-manipulation provisions appropriately balance protecting the tax base against preserving legitimate tax treatment.

themes.name: Should taxpayers be able to exploit formal accounting, timing, or classification rules to defer or avoid otherwise taxable income?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether realization, basis, payment timing, and related accounting doctrines produce unjustified deferral and strategic tax planning.

themes.name: How should courts, Congress, and tax administrators resolve tax questions when statutory language no longer fits economic reality?
themes.definition: This question examines the institutional allocation of authority for interpreting, clarifying, or reforming unsettled tax rules and limiting agency-created restrictions.

themes.name: Do conflicts among the Internal Revenue Code, other federal statutes, and separate tax regimes produce inconsistent burdens?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether interactions among legal regimes create gaps, duplicative taxation, or unintended advantages for particular taxpayers or transactions.

themes.name: Should tax law favor administrable bright-line rules over economically accurate but complex treatment?
themes.definition: This question weighs legal precision and substantive fairness against compliance costs, enforcement burdens, uncertainty, and administrative feasibility.

themes.name: Is a consumption-tax alternative preferable to the existing income-tax structure?
themes.definition: This question compares income and consumption taxation in terms of revenue, equity, saving and investment incentives, administrability, and the treatment of accumulated wealth.

themes.name: Should tax expenditures be replaced with direct spending when they subsidize socially valuable activities?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether deductions, exclusions, credits, and other tax preferences are more effective and equitable than explicit government expenditures for achieving social-policy goals.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for capital, property, and homeownership worsen wealth inequality?
themes.definition: This question examines whether preferential treatment of capital gains, property ownership, and housing disproportionately benefits wealthy or asset-rich taxpayers and reinforces unequal wealth accumulation.

themes.name: Can progressive taxation of high incomes and accumulated wealth reduce inequality without unacceptable economic and administrative costs?
themes.definition: This question weighs the distributive benefits of higher taxes on high-income and wealthy taxpayers against effects on growth, saving, avoidance, compliance, and administrative feasibility.

themes.name: Should income-tax policy prioritize ability to pay and redistribution over neutrality and economic efficiency?
themes.definition: This question examines whether unequal or progressive tax burdens are justified by distributive justice even when they alter economic incentives or resource allocation.

themes.name: Does the tax treatment of inherited wealth adequately promote equitable intergenerational distribution?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether transfer taxes, inheritance taxation, and related rules appropriately address inherited wealth, family transfers, and the concentration of resources across generations.

themes.name: Should capital gains taxation substitute for or complement wealth-transfer taxation?
themes.definition: This question compares taxing gains from capital appreciation with taxing transfers of wealth through gifts and inheritances as methods of redistribution and revenue collection.

themes.name: Do family-tax rules distribute burdens fairly across married couples, households, and dependents?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether marriage taxation, personal exemptions, credits, and tax-unit rules treat households with different family structures and incomes equitably.

themes.name: Do refundable credits and tax-based benefit programs effectively assist low-income working families?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether programs such as the earned income tax credit provide adequate support while avoiding burdens, inadequate phase-ins, stigma, or work disincentives.

themes.name: Does the tax treatment of employee benefits distribute advantages fairly among differently situated workers?
themes.definition: This question examines whether exclusions and deductions for compensation-related benefits, including healthcare benefits, disproportionately favor particular workers, employers, or income groups.

themes.name: Do tax incentives for saving and investment increase socially valuable capital formation or mainly redistribute benefits to existing asset holders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential savings accounts, investment provisions, and capital-income rules raise national saving and productive investment enough to justify their fiscal and distributional costs.

themes.name: Should the income tax recognize the time value of money and changes in economic value when taxing payments, deductions, and recoveries?
themes.definition: This question considers whether economically equivalent transactions should receive different treatment because income, losses, obligations, or deductions occur at different times or change in value.

themes.name: Should taxable income be determined by economic substance rather than formal ownership, realization, or legal classification?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax law should look through formal labels and property arrangements to tax economically equivalent income, benefits, transactions, and changes in ownership.

themes.name: When should noncash benefits, awards, recoveries, or transfers become taxable income under the realization doctrine?
themes.definition: This question addresses the boundary between untaxed economic accretions and taxable gross income when value is received without a conventional cash payment or formal realization event.

themes.name: Do deductions for personal expenditures and mixed-use costs have coherent policy justifications?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deductions should be allowed when expenses combine personal consumption with income production or socially valuable functions, and whether such deductions create inequitable distortions.

themes.name: Do complex and fragmented tax rules create avoidable opportunities for tax planning, deferral, and income escape?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether technical limitations, overlapping provisions, and specialized doctrines undermine the tax base by enabling taxpayers to exploit gaps or postpone liability.

themes.name: Should specialized tax regimes be consolidated into simpler and more coherent rules?
themes.definition: This question asks whether replacing overlapping, ad hoc, or highly technical provisions with general rules would improve administrability, compliance, fairness, and economic neutrality.

themes.name: Can tax rules pursue social objectives without producing greater behavioral distortions and administrative costs than direct policy instruments?
themes.definition: This question assesses the tradeoff between using taxation to influence behavior or deliver social policy and preserving efficient, comprehensible, and enforceable tax administration.

themes.name: Does a formally race-neutral tax code produce racially, gender-based, or otherwise socially unequal outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether tax structures and tax-favored arrangements generate disparate effects across socially defined groups despite facial neutrality.

themes.name: Should the federal income tax be replaced by a broad-based, low-rate flat tax or a consumption-oriented regime?
themes.definition: This question compares major alternative tax bases and structures with the existing income tax in terms of equity, efficiency, revenue, saving incentives, and administrative feasibility.

themes.name: What legal and constitutional limits should constrain congressional and administrative taxing power?
themes.definition: This question examines how constitutional principles, rule-of-law requirements, statutory interpretation, and legislative intent limit the government's authority to impose or reinterpret tax liabilities.

themes.name: Should the income tax be replaced or supplemented by a consumption-based tax?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether consumption taxation would improve upon income taxation in terms of equity, efficiency, savings incentives, administrability, and revenue.

themes.name: Should the income-tax base include unrealized appreciation and other accretions to wealth?
themes.definition: This question examines whether changes in wealth, accumulated savings, and investment appreciation should be taxed even when they have not been realized through a transaction.

themes.name: Should capital income and capital gains remain subject to comprehensive income taxation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the appropriate tax treatment of returns to investment, including capital income, appreciation, depreciation, and gains that may receive preferential treatment.

themes.name: Should wealth transfers receive different tax treatment from ordinary income?
themes.definition: This question addresses how gifts, inheritances, estate transfers, and intergenerational wealth should be characterized and taxed when property or economic interests change hands.

themes.name: Does the estate-and-gift-tax system adequately prevent the concentration and intergenerational transmission of wealth?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether valuation rules, exemptions, exclusions, and preferential treatment of appreciated property effectively address inequality created by wealth transfers.

themes.name: Should tax preferences be used to pursue social-policy goals rather than merely raise revenue?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether deductions, exclusions, credits, and other tax expenditures are justified as instruments for promoting socially valued behavior or welfare objectives.

themes.name: Do targeted tax benefits effectively improve the welfare and opportunities of economically disadvantaged people?
themes.definition: This question examines the distributional effectiveness of tax credits, deductions, and other benefits aimed at low-income or otherwise disadvantaged groups.

themes.name: Do tax preferences produce sufficient social benefits to justify their costs to neutrality, revenue, and fairness?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential tax treatment is normatively and empirically justified despite its potential to distort taxpayer choices and create unequal treatment.

themes.name: Should tax neutrality yield to equity or other policy objectives when taxpayers choose among legally available arrangements?
themes.definition: This question examines when departures from equal treatment across transactions or taxpayer choices are warranted by distributional, behavioral, or social-policy goals.

themes.name: Does taxation based on ability to pay produce more equitable outcomes than formally equal tax rules?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax burdens should reflect taxpayers’ actual economic circumstances, resources, and responsibilities rather than only formal income classifications.

themes.name: Do ostensibly neutral tax rules create unjustified horizontal or distributive inequities?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether taxpayers who are formally similar, or who receive formally equal benefits, experience substantively unequal burdens because of their circumstances.

themes.name: Can tax reform broaden the tax base by limiting special exclusions, deductions, and credits without worsening social inequities?
themes.definition: This question evaluates base-broadening reforms that reduce preferential provisions while considering their effects on revenue, fairness, incentives, and vulnerable taxpayers.

themes.name: Do anti-avoidance rules successfully protect the tax base without imposing excessive compliance and administrative costs?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether statutory barriers, substance-over-form doctrines, and related rules deter avoidance and evasion while remaining workable for taxpayers and administrators.

themes.name: Should tax consequences follow the economic substance of a transaction rather than its formal legal classification?
themes.definition: This question examines whether legal labels, ownership structures, payment forms, and statutory categories accurately capture the underlying economic benefits, burdens, and relationships.

themes.name: Should the timing and form of a payment determine its tax treatment when economically equivalent benefits are involved?
themes.definition: This question addresses realization, accrual, deferral, original issue discount, and related timing rules that may tax economically similar payments differently.

themes.name: Do tax rules governing marriage, household support, and divorce allocate burdens and benefits equitably?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the federal tax consequences of marital status, joint or separate filing, family support, divorce-related transfers, and intra-family benefits.

themes.name: Do tax-favored saving and retirement arrangements distribute benefits equitably across taxpayers and families?
themes.definition: This question examines whether preferences for saving, retirement wealth, and accumulated assets disproportionately benefit particular income groups or household arrangements.

themes.name: Do tax incentives effectively change taxpayer behavior without creating unacceptable distortions or compliance problems?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether credits, deductions, timing rules, and other incentives achieve intended behavioral goals while avoiding strategic responses, evasion, or inefficient choices.

themes.name: Can tax-based redistribution achieve social objectives as effectively and legitimately as direct spending or welfare programs?
themes.definition: This question compares tax expenditures and other tax-based interventions with direct government programs in terms of targeting, transparency, accountability, administrative feasibility, and distributional impact.

themes.name: Can tax rules be simplified while preserving their substantive equity and policy objectives?
themes.definition: This question examines whether complexity, uncertainty, reporting burdens, and overlapping statutory provisions can be reduced without sacrificing accurate taxation or important social goals.

themes.name: Should federal income tax measure economic income more comprehensively than current realization-based rules?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether taxable income should better reflect Haig-Simons economic income, including accrued gains, noncash benefits, and other currently excluded returns.

themes.name: Should mark-to-market or accrual taxation replace or supplement realization for investment gains and losses?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether current-assessment systems would produce fairer and more coherent taxation than waiting for a sale or other realization event.

themes.name: How should tax law determine the timing and aggregation of income, deductions, and contingent payments?
themes.definition: This question addresses when economically related receipts, losses, deductions, and future or uncertain payment rights should be recognized for tax purposes.

themes.name: Should returns to capital receive preferential or deferred tax treatment relative to labor income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether differentiated treatment of investment income, savings, and personal-service compensation is justified by equity, efficiency, or capital-formation concerns.

themes.name: Do tax preferences for saving and investment promote capital formation enough to justify their distributional costs?
themes.definition: This question tests whether exclusions, deferrals, and reduced rates on investment returns actually increase saving and investment rather than primarily benefiting affluent taxpayers.

themes.name: Should wealth and transfer taxes supplement an income tax that inadequately reaches accumulated wealth?
themes.definition: This question considers whether taxation of estates, gifts, wealth holdings, or accumulated gains is necessary to address concentration of wealth and erosion of the income-tax base.

themes.name: Should federal estate and gift taxes be retained and redesigned to limit intergenerational concentration of wealth?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the relationship between estate and gift taxation, including exclusions and deductions that may allow substantial transfers to escape tax.

themes.name: Is a federal wealth tax constitutionally permissible under the Direct Tax and Apportionment Clauses?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether a tax imposed on accumulated wealth can satisfy constitutional limits on federal direct taxation.

themes.name: Should the tax system treat marriage and marriage-equivalent relationships as household units or as separate individuals?
themes.definition: This question addresses joint filing, marriage bonuses and penalties, domestic partnerships, and the equitable allocation of tax burdens between couples and single taxpayers.

themes.name: How should federal income tax treat family support, divorce-related transfers, and other intra-family economic exchanges?
themes.definition: This question examines whether payments and benefits exchanged within families should be taxed, deducted, attributed, or ignored based on economic substance rather than formal legal characterization.

themes.name: Can progressive personal income taxation reduce inequality without imposing unacceptable efficiency or welfare costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the distributive justification for progressive rates against behavioral responses, administrative burdens, and possible economic distortions.

themes.name: Do formally neutral tax rules produce discriminatory effects for taxpayers with different economic resources or social circumstances?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether equal-looking classifications, deductions, and benefits systematically advantage affluent taxpayers or disadvantage historically devalued forms of labor.

themes.name: Should ability-to-pay analysis use taxpayers' net economic resources rather than their gross receipts?
themes.definition: This question asks whether deductions and tax burdens should account for economically necessary costs, losses, and other circumstances that reduce the practical value of income.

themes.name: Are tax expenditures effective and equitable instruments for delivering social benefits?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether deductions, exclusions, credits, and subsidies achieve their stated social-policy objectives more effectively and fairly than direct spending or regulatory programs.

themes.name: Do refundable credits such as the earned income tax credit provide effective and fair income support to working poor households?
themes.definition: This question concerns the design, eligibility rules, distributional effects, and work incentives of refundable tax transfers for low-income workers.

themes.name: Should tax preferences be evaluated individually according to their policy results rather than accepted or rejected categorically?
themes.definition: This question asks whether each targeted benefit should be assessed separately for effectiveness, incidence, revenue cost, and consistency with its stated purpose.

themes.name: Can anti-avoidance and attribution rules prevent strategic legal arrangements from eroding the tax base without sacrificing legitimate flexibility?
themes.definition: This question examines how courts and administrators should address timing, characterization, formal ownership, and related-party structures used to reduce tax liability.

themes.name: Should tax law prioritize economic substance over formal classifications when determining the treatment of transactions and benefits?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether legal labels such as debt, income, gift, loss, or compensation accurately reflect the underlying economic and distributive consequences.

themes.name: How should courts, Congress, and tax administrators divide authority when statutory tax rules are ambiguous or produce anomalous results?
themes.definition: This question addresses judicial interpretation, anti-avoidance doctrines, legislative redesign, and administrative discretion in resolving gaps or conflicts within the Internal Revenue Code.

themes.name: Can the Internal Revenue Code remain administrable and predictable while pursuing more accurate and equitable tax outcomes?
themes.definition: This question concerns the tradeoff between complexity, enforcement and informational costs, taxpayer certainty, and the normative benefits of more finely calibrated tax rules.

themes.name: Should the federal government rely primarily on an income tax, or should consumption- and wealth-based taxes supplement or replace it?
themes.definition: This question compares income, consumption, and wealth as competing tax bases in terms of equity, efficiency, revenue, and administrative feasibility.

themes.name: Should income taxation move toward accrual-based taxation rather than taxing income only when it is realized?
themes.definition: This question examines whether increases in economic value should be taxed continuously or deferred until realization through a sale, transfer, or other event.

themes.name: Should tax liability reflect taxpayers’ broader economic ability to pay rather than only their realized taxable income?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether unrealized wealth, resources, and economic capacity should influence tax burdens when reported income does not capture a taxpayer’s position.

themes.name: Are progressive marginal tax rates a justified and effective means of reducing inequality and concentrated wealth?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether graduated rates can advance redistribution without creating unacceptable efficiency, behavioral, or political costs.

themes.name: Does the nominal payer of a tax accurately identify who bears its economic burden?
themes.definition: This question investigates how tax burdens are shifted among capital owners, businesses, workers, and consumers rather than remaining with the party legally liable for payment.

themes.name: Do tax preferences distribute benefits inequitably across income groups and forms of economic activity?
themes.definition: This question examines whether exclusions, deductions, deferrals, and other preferences disproportionately benefit wealthy taxpayers or favored investments and arrangements.

themes.name: Do tax-based subsidies effectively achieve social-policy objectives, or do they create costly and inequitable alternatives to other policy instruments?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether tax expenditures and credits produce their intended welfare, investment, and social outcomes relative to their revenue and administrative costs.

themes.name: Can refundable credits such as the Earned Income Tax Credit improve the economic security and work incentives of low-income households?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether targeted credits successfully support low-income workers while encouraging employment and avoiding gaps caused by eligibility or implementation rules.

themes.name: Does the tax treatment of marriage and family relationships fairly allocate household resources and tax burdens?
themes.definition: This question evaluates joint taxation, marriage-related benefits, family expenses, parent-to-child transfers, and legally recognized family arrangements as a coherent tax system.

themes.name: Is the estate and gift tax necessary and appropriately designed to prevent avoidance through lifetime wealth transfers?
themes.definition: This question examines whether gift taxation, transfer-at-death rules, and family-transfer provisions adequately prevent taxpayers from escaping estate taxation while treating different families fairly.

themes.name: How should the tax system treat appreciated property when it is exchanged, transferred, or received outside ordinary earnings?
themes.definition: This question addresses realization, basis, exclusions, and tax liability when ownership of appreciated assets changes without a conventional cash sale.

themes.name: Do tax exclusions and preferences for employment compensation produce fair and efficient treatment of different forms of labor income?
themes.definition: This question compares the tax treatment of wages, benefits, deferred compensation, and other employment-related rewards and considers its effects on workers and employers.

themes.name: Do categorical tax rules adequately classify economically mixed, nontraditional, or difficult-to-measure benefits?
themes.definition: This question asks whether formal classifications of receipts, recoveries, compensation, and other benefits accurately reflect their economic substance or produce distortions.

themes.name: Should courts use substance- and policy-based interpretation to resolve ambiguous tax rules, or should they adhere primarily to formal statutory text?
themes.definition: This question examines how tax doctrine should balance legally grounded interpretation with fairness, statutory purpose, and the practical consequences of competing readings.

themes.name: Can tax simplification reduce compliance and administrative costs without undermining equity, neutrality, or legislative objectives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tradeoff between simpler tax rules and the exceptions, eligibility conditions, and adjustments needed to achieve substantively fair outcomes.

themes.name: Do weaknesses and fragmentation in tax rules create significant opportunities for sophisticated tax avoidance?
themes.definition: This question investigates how taxpayers and advisers exploit statutory gaps, categorical distinctions, timing rules, and tax-planning structures to reduce effective taxation.

themes.name: Should tax policy prioritize neutrality toward private decisions, or should it deliberately use incentives to influence behavior?
themes.definition: This question weighs the behavioral effects of deductions, credits, savings preferences, and investment incentives against concerns about distortion, equity, and income protection.

themes.name: Is structural tax reform preferable to piecemeal corrective legislation for producing coherent and policy-consistent tax treatment?
themes.definition: This question compares comprehensive reform with targeted statutory and doctrinal fixes in terms of unintended consequences, fairness, simplicity, and administrative effectiveness.

themes.name: Does the tax system impose unequal or discriminatory burdens on marginalized and economically vulnerable populations?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax rules, administration, compliance demands, and benefit eligibility reproduce structural inequalities affecting disadvantaged groups.

themes.name: Can political and administrative institutions make progressive tax reform both feasible and legitimate?
themes.definition: This question concerns how political opposition, institutional design, courts, agencies, and enforcement mechanisms shape the adoption and practical consequences of redistributive reform.

themes.name: Should federal income tax include atypical receipts and nontraditional forms of economic value in gross income?
themes.definition: This question examines whether existing concepts of income adequately capture unusual payments, benefits, property interests, and other economically valuable receipts.

themes.name: Should accrued investment gains be taxed before realization, including when assets are transferred at death?
themes.definition: This question evaluates realization-based taxation against accrual, mark-to-market, or deemed-realization approaches for investment gains and losses.

themes.name: How should federal tax law distinguish taxable income from returns of capital and restoration of an underlying asset?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether tax rules correctly separate genuine economic gain from the recovery of previously invested or impaired capital.

themes.name: Should deductions and exclusions be coordinated with associated receipts to measure net economic income?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether taxpayers should receive deductions or exclusions only when related receipts are included, so that taxable income reflects net rather than nominal amounts.

themes.name: Do formal legal classifications produce inappropriate tax results when economically comparable transactions or payments have different labels?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax consequences should follow legal form or economic substance when classifications determine materially different treatment.

themes.name: How should federal tax law allocate consequences among different organizational and legal forms?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether businesses, investments, and transfers conducted through different entities or legal arrangements receive neutral and coherent tax treatment.

themes.name: Should tax treatment be harmonized across economically substitutable saving, financing, and investment vehicles?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether preferences for particular savings or investment arrangements create unjustified inequities, distortions, or planning opportunities.

themes.name: Do retirement tax preferences provide broad and equitable pension coverage, or primarily subsidize affluent savers?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the distributional and behavioral effects of tax-advantaged retirement arrangements and their relationship to earned entitlements and public retirement programs.

themes.name: Should marital status and family structure determine federal income and transfer-tax liability?
themes.definition: This question examines whether tax rules appropriately account for marriage, household relationships, caregiving, and legally or economically diverse family arrangements.

themes.name: Should federal estate and gift taxes be retained or redesigned to limit intergenerational wealth concentration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the structure, scope, and effectiveness of transfer taxes in taxing estates, inheritances, and transfers of wealth while limiting avoidance.

themes.name: Would a direct wealth tax reduce wealth concentration more effectively than relying primarily on income and transfer taxation?
themes.definition: This question compares direct taxation of accumulated wealth with existing approaches and considers revenue, avoidance, liquidity, administrative, and legal constraints.

themes.name: Do capital-income preferences and tax subsidies disproportionately benefit affluent taxpayers and asset owners?
